mobile-ios.source_cluster: plaud-sdk-public iOS template app (PlaudTemplateApp, 38 Swift files) vs Android template app (parity)
repos: reference/plaud-org/plaud-sdk-public (ios/PlaudTemplateApp/**, ios/project.yml, ios/PartnerConfig.xcconfig, android/app/src/main/java/com/plaud/template/** for parity, sdk/ios/*.swiftinterface for SDK API existence, README.md)
mobile-ios.evidence_role: OFFICIAL_SOURCE (Plaud-published template app source; evidence class PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE for what the APP does; SDK-internal behaviour cited from the shipped swiftinterface is PROVEN_BINARY_INTERFACE; cloud behaviour described only in comments/README is CLOUD_OBSERVED-by-Plaud-engineer-comment, i.e. a CLAIM)
mobile-ios.why_in_corpus: The iOS template is the only Plaud-published, human-written client that shows the full product layer above the packet: launch routing, local persistence (UserDefaults + recordings.json), the sync/WiFi state machines, the cloud bind/unbind/binding + brick-recovery flow, the 3-step S3 upload + transcription poll loop, OTA sheet, and multi-device handling. Compared side-by-side with the Android template (same authors, same tickets PLA2-3xx/4xx) it separates app policy (identical constants on both platforms) from platform requirements (CoreLocation gating, NEHotspotConfiguration, SDK facade gaps on Android). Its source comments also carry a dozen cloud/firmware behaviour CLAIMS (bind_history duplication, wav rejection, opus pipeline empty results, sdk-token 404) that no other source in the corpus states.
mobile-ios.summary: The iOS template (bundle com.plaud.PlaudTemplateApp1, v1.0.57) is a UIKit app whose SceneDelegate routes to MainTabBarController (Home/Files/Settings, custom floating capsule bar) when UserDefaults holds pairedDeviceSNs or hasSkippedOnboarding plus a userId, otherwise to Welcome->Scanning->ConnectSheet->Success. All user identity is a partner-issued JWT (USER_ACCESS_TOKEN) baked in via xcconfig or pasted in Settings; userId = JWT `sub`, X-Client-Id = JWT `client_id`. Persistence is UserDefaults (pairedDeviceSNs, activeDeviceSN, pairedDeviceNames, userId, autoSyncEnabled, hasSkippedOnboarding, serverDomainOverride, userAccessTokenOverride, apiKeyOverride, fastTransfer_neverShowAgain) plus Documents/recordings.json (Codable [RecordingFile]) and MP3 audio in Documents/. Both templates DEFAULT the server domain to platform-test.plaud.ai. PlaudAPIService builds exactly seven request shapes against https://{domain}/developer/api: presigned-urls, S3 PUT, complete-upload (Bearer user token), transcriptions POST/GET (X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key, fixed params model plaud-fast-whisper, diarization off, poll 5s x240), sdk/bind|unbind and sdk/binding (Bearer) with no retries anywhere. Device lifecycle: GATT connect is not success; success = bleBind status 0, after which the app cloud-binds (403 -> alert), persists pairing, and 3s later silently fetches the file list; every downloaded file is MP3-exported then deleted from the device; auto-reconnect is a 30s timer x10; a handshake drop offers the brick-recovery flow (GET binding -> up to 5 deduped historical ids via SDK recoveryConnectBleDevice -> depair -> rescan because MAC changes -> reconnect). OTA and firmware check are delegated entirely to the iOS SDK, whereas Android reimplements the version check itself against /sdk/version/latest with X-Device-Signature because its SDK path needs a non-existent sdk-token. Parity is very high by design (comments say "mirrors iOS/Android", identical recovery timeouts 25/5/20s, identical transcription params, identical storage schema), and the differences that remain are platform requirements (CoreLocation/NEHotspot gating, 185s watchdog, AVAudioPlayer vs ExoPlayer+OpusRepair, SDK facade gaps) or iOS-only defects (auto-sync toggle never rendered and never honoured; Files-tab Fast Transfer pill unwired; local delete uses a bare filename). Summary/AI insights are not implemented on either platform (summaryText is never written), search/memory/subscription do not exist in the template, and observability is the SDK's encrypted .plaud log export with auto-upload explicitly disabled by the app.

findings.behavior: Launch routing: SceneDelegate shows MainTabBarController when (pairedDeviceSNs non-empty OR hasSkippedOnboarding) AND userId != nil, calling DeviceManager.configure(userId:) first; otherwise UINavigationController(WelcomeViewController).
findings.notes: Android mirror: WelcomeActivity.kt:30-36 (pairedDeviceSNs.isNotEmpty || hasSkippedOnboarding) and MainActivity.kt:45-49 (lastConnectedDeviceSN==null && !hasSkippedOnboarding -> Welcome). PARITY: same policy.

findings.behavior: Foreground reconnect: on sceneDidBecomeActive, if activeDeviceSN and userId exist, after 2s and only if not .connected and not isOTAInProgress, DeviceManager.startScan() (scan result auto-connects the last SN).
findings.notes: Android: PlaudTemplateApp.kt:52-66 registers an app-wide ActivityLifecycleCallbacks foreground trigger (2s) -> attemptReconnect(), plus MainActivity.kt:74-79. PARITY: same 2s constant; Android guards OTA via firmwareUpdateState phase (DeviceManager.kt:712-718).

findings.behavior: Navigation: MainTabBarController hosts three UINavigationControllers (Home, Files, Settings) with the native tab bar hidden and a 272x62 floating capsule; the capsule hides whenever a nav stack depth > 1 (Scanning / DevicePanel / FileDetail). It also subscribes to recoveryOfferPublisher (alert 'Device Locked' -> startDeviceRecovery) and cloudAlertPublisher ('Device Binding' alert).
findings.notes: Android MainActivity.kt:62-64 shows the same 'Device Binding' AlertDialog; HomeFragment.kt:199-219 shows 'Device Locked'/Recover.

findings.behavior: User identity is entirely the partner JWT: Welcome 'Get Started' parses base64url payload `sub` as userId (falls back to a random UUID if unparseable), stores it in UserDefaults, calls DeviceManager.configure(userId:), pushes Scanning. 'Connect device later' does the same but sets hasSkippedOnboarding=true and shows MainTabBarController.
findings.notes: No login screen, no OTP, no account API in the template: the backend issuing the JWT (README.md:83 'POST /open/partner/users/access-token') is the partner's, not the app's. Android WelcomeActivity.kt:64-103 identical.

findings.behavior: Token precedence (read per use): UserDefaults 'userAccessTokenOverride' > Info.plist UserAccessToken > legacy Info.plist PartnerToken. Settings 'Replace' parses the pasted JWT; same `sub` -> PlaudDeviceAgent.setUserAccessToken(newToken) applied live; different `sub` -> RecordingStore.userId = new user_id, takes effect on relaunch, with a note that the device must be unpaired on the old account first.
findings.notes: Android SettingsFragment.kt:165-196 identical semantics but calls sdk.NiceBuildSdk.setPartnerToken (facade lacks setUserAccessToken, TODO(SDK) at line 147). PARITY: policy identical, SDK entry point differs.

findings.behavior: UserDefaults keys: lastConnectedDeviceSN (legacy, migrated into pairedDeviceSNs/activeDeviceSN on first read), pairedDeviceSNs [String], activeDeviceSN, pairedDeviceNames [SN:name], userId, autoSyncEnabled, hasSkippedOnboarding, serverDomainOverride, userAccessTokenOverride, apiKeyOverride, fastTransfer_neverShowAgain.
findings.notes: Android RecordingStore.kt:12-19, 85, 94, 130, 139 uses SharedPreferences 'plaud_template_prefs' with snake_case keys (last_connected_device_sn, paired_device_sns as JSON, paired_device_names JSON, user_id, is_auto_sync_enabled, fast_transfer_never_show, user_access_token_override, api_key_override, server_domain_override, has_skipped_onboarding). PARITY: same schema, different key spelling; Android has no legacy migration.

findings.behavior: Recording metadata persists as Documents/recordings.json, a Codable [RecordingFile] {id UUID, sessionId Int, deviceSN, name, duration, createdAt, syncedAt?, localPath?, summaryText?, transcriptJSON?}; isSynced == (localPath != nil). Writes are atomic whole-file rewrites; markAsSynced stores only lastPathComponent and resolveAbsolutePath re-roots it under the current sandbox Documents dir.
findings.notes: Android RecordingStore.kt:151-266 same file name recordings.json (Gson) under filesDir, but stores ABSOLUTE localPath (markAsSynced line 216) and has updateDuration; iOS has updateSummary (never called by any UI). PARITY: schema identical (field names match SerializedName), path relativity differs (iOS relative to survive container re-path).

findings.behavior: Audio files: BLE and WiFi exports write MP3 mono into Documents/ (audioDir); share-export writes WAV into Documents/exports; helper audioFilePath(sessionId) returns '<sessionId>.ogg' but is dead code on both platforms.
findings.notes: Android SyncManager.kt:391-400, 595-611, 785-791 exports MP3 for sync AND for share (iOS share = WAV), into cacheDir/export (RecordingStore.kt:230-235) rather than an internal files dir. PARITY DIFFERENCE: share format wav(iOS) vs mp3(Android); Android keeps synced audio in cache (evictable).

findings.behavior: Server environment: three selectable domains Production platform-us.plaud.ai, Pre-release platform-us-pre.plaud.ai, Test platform-test.plaud.ai; activeServerDomain = serverDomainOverride ?? TEST (default is the TEST environment, comment 'cloud bind/unbind testing'); the same domain feeds PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK(customDomain:) and every PlaudAPIService base URL https://{domain}/developer/api; switching requires relaunch.
findings.notes: Android RecordingStore.kt:110-135 identical constants and identical TEST default. Android additionally must call NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl(host) because 'the platformHost passed to initSdk is not forwarded to the Partner API (known SDK issue)... US token sent to jp returns 401 CLIENT_USER_NOT_FOUND' (DeviceManager.kt:164-173) -> corroborates frozen baseline default host platform-jp for the AAR. README.md:322/424 documents production domain only.

findings.behavior: PlaudAPIService.perform: single URLSession.shared dataTask, no retry, no backoff, success = 2xx and JSONDecoder decode (EmptyResponse tolerated); logs go to AppLog (SDK log file) only in DEBUG; S3 URLs are recognised by 'amazonaws.com' substring to suppress logging.
findings.notes: Android TranscriptionManager.kt:62-66, 257-266: OkHttp connect 30s / read+write 120s, throws on non-2xx, no retry either. PARITY: no client-side retry policy on either platform.

findings.behavior: Transcription flow (TranscriptionManager): file must exist -> generate-presigned-urls(filesize, filetype from extension) -> sequential PUT of chunks (chunk = response ChunkSize ?? 5MiB) collecting ETags -> complete-upload(part_list, file_md5) -> DownloadUrl -> POST transcriptions with fixed params -> poll GET every 5s up to 240 (20 min); statuses PENDING/RECEIVED/STARTED/PROGRESS keep polling, SUCCESS -> data.results [TranscriptionResult{speaker_id,start,end,text,language}], FAILURE/REVOKED -> failed, unknown -> keep polling. A generation counter drops stale tasks' emits.
findings.notes: Android TranscriptionManager.kt:47-50, 89-120, 125-181, 185-238 is a line-for-line mirror (same 5s/240, same params). Android adds a pre-check refusing .wav ('upload API rejects wav (FILE_TYPE_INVALID)', lines 100-107) and a missing-credentials check up front; iOS checks credentials only at submit time (resolveTranscriptionAuth, lines 193-200). Diarization is requested OFF, so speaker_id rendering ('Speaker N') is cosmetic unless the backend returns it anyway.

findings.behavior: Summary is NOT implemented: FileDetail hides the Summary tab ('Summary not yet integrated'), defaults to Transcript, and RecordingStore.updateSummary has no caller; summaryText is only ever populated by MockSyncManager. The empty-state copy 'Transcript and summary will be generated' is aspirational.
findings.notes: Android FileDetailActivity.kt:114-118 shows a summary block only if summaryText non-null; nothing writes it. No search, RAG, memory, or subscription/entitlement code exists in either template (grep negative).

findings.behavior: Transcript persistence and display: completed results are JSON-encoded into RecordingFile.transcriptJSON and rendered as 'Speaker N  ·  HH:MM:SS' headers + text; Copy Transcript copies the same header format; FileDetail re-reads the store on load because SyncManager's in-memory snapshot can be stale.
findings.notes: Android FileDetailActivity.kt:66-71, 191-192, 213-243 same shape ('same shape iOS persists'). Android additionally alerts 'no speech was detected' on empty results (lines 183-188); iOS shows an empty transcript list.

findings.behavior: iOS FileDetail 'Generate' on an unsynced file offers 'Sync Now' which runs SyncManager.startSync() and, on .completed, re-reads the file and starts transcription automatically.
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android FileDetailActivity.kt:147-156 only alerts 'Local audio file not found. Sync the recording first.' (no sync-then-transcribe chaining).

findings.behavior: Scan: cachedBleDevices cleared, refuses immediately with 'Bluetooth is off...' if the SDK's bleState(powered:false) was seen, otherwise state .scanning and PlaudDeviceAgent.startScan(). bleScanResult filters SN prefix 881 (NotePro) / 882 (NotePin S) only, sanitises BLE names (control chars / U+FFFD), sorts by RSSI desc, deliberately keeps already-paired devices visible (PLA2-323), and auto-connects if lastConnectedDeviceSN matches, state is .scanning and suppressAutoReconnect is false.
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:47-49, 73-81, 215-260, 738-775 identical policy; Android adds its own 10s scan timeout job (lines 770-774) and reads BluetoothAdapter.isEnabled instead of an SDK callback. PARITY DIFFERENCE: iOS relies on the SDK's bleScanOverTime callback (line 616-623), Android on an app timer.

findings.behavior: Connect: connect(device,userId) requires a cached BleDevice, sets awaitingHandshakeSN, state .connecting, and calls PlaudDeviceAgent.connectBleDevice(bleDevice:, deviceToken: userId). GATT connect (bleConnectState 1) is NOT success; success is bleBind(status 0) which sets .connected, sends any pendingDeviceWiFiClose, cloud-binds, addPairedDevice(sn,name) (also sets activeDeviceSN), publishes PlaudDevice from recentConnectDevice, refreshDeviceInfo (getState+getStorage). blePenState then populates device info once and runs checkFirmwareUpdate; blePenState state==4099 (0x1003) or BleAgent.isRecording resyncs a recording already in progress and starts syncFile(sessionId,0,0).
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:800-849 must itself wait for NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() (10s poll) and call NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(type,sn) before connectBleDevice(bleDevice) (no deviceToken param); success also on bleBind 0 -> onDeviceConnected (lines 439-501) which additionally calls syncTime(), getConnectedDeviceVersion(), refreshRecordState() (facade blePenState lacks sessionId, line 374-378). PARITY: iOS SDK hides sn-sign/gen-key readiness; Android app must orchestrate it.

findings.behavior: Handshake rejection = brick signal: if bleConnectState reports 0 (drop) or 2/-1/-2 (fail) while awaitingHandshakeSN is set, the app stops auto-reconnect, publishes .failed('The device refused the connection — it may still be locked by another account.') and, if the attempt was an auto-reconnect, emits recoveryOfferPublisher so Home/MainTab can offer recovery.
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:263-309, 625-637 identical; its comment records the platform difference: 'iOS drops after GATT (state 1 -> 0), Android reports a connect failure (state 2, ~10s timeout)'.

findings.behavior: Brick recovery (recovery flow): GET /open/partner/sdk/binding -> fail if unreachable, fail if is_bind==true ('bound to another account'), dedupe bind_history and take first 5 -> for each historical id: PlaudDeviceAgent.recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice:, historicalUserId:) and wait up to 25s for bleBind(0)/blePenState (success) or connect state 0/2 (fail); on success depair(clear:false) waiting up to 5s for bleDepair, disconnect, sleep 1.5s, rescan up to 20s for the SN to re-advertise (MAC changes after depair), then connect() as the current user. Runs blocking on a private DispatchQueue with semaphores.
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:53-63, 1037-1195 identical constants (25000/5000/20000 ms, 5 attempts) and identical failure strings, implemented with coroutines. SDK method recoveryConnectBleDevice exists in the shipped iOS interface (sdk/ios/PlaudDeviceBasicSDK.framework/Modules/PlaudDeviceBasicSDK.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios.swiftinterface:1242). The 'historical id transformed: strip client_user_ prefix, drop hyphens' description (DeviceManager.swift:337-338) is a comment about SDK internals -> CLAIM.

findings.behavior: Cloud binding policy: POST /open/partner/sdk/bind after EVERY successful handshake (idempotent for same owner per comment); HTTP 403 -> user alert 'already bound to another account'; any other status/transport failure silently ignored. Unpair does POST /sdk/unbind first (fire-and-forget), then PlaudDeviceAgent.depair(clear:true), removePairedDevice(sn) (active falls back to first remaining), SyncManager.reset(), publishes disconnected.
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:857-890, 1199-1243 identical order and strings, but depair(false) with a 3s fallback disconnect (iOS depair(clear:true) and no wait). PARITY DIFFERENCE: depair clear flag true(iOS)/false(Android) — meaning of the flag is SDK-internal (UNKNOWN).

findings.behavior: Auto-reconnect: on an unexpected disconnect (not user, not OTA, not during WiFi transfer) startAutoReconnect(initialDelay 3s) runs a repeating 30s Timer, each tick sets .scanning and startScan(), giving up after 10 attempts; stopped on GATT connect. switchDevice(sn): user-disconnect, set activeDeviceSN=sn, .scanning, startScan after 1.5s (auto-connect picks the new SN). Add-device flow sets suppressAutoReconnect=true, disconnects, and scans after 1.2s (PLA2-331).
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:142-143, 639-676, 695-708; ScanningActivity.kt:307 DISCONNECT_SETTLE_MS=1200. Same 30s x10 and 1.5s/1.2s constants; Android initial delay 2s vs iOS 3s. PARITY: policy identical, one constant differs (2s vs 3s).

findings.behavior: Multi-device: Home device card lists other paired devices (from UserDefaults) with tap -> switchDevice(sn) and '+ Add device' -> ScanningViewController(isAddingDevice:true) which pops back to Home on success instead of showing the Success page. Unpair of one device pops to Home if others remain, else replaces root with Welcome. Sign out (Settings) refuses while recording, otherwise unpairs the CURRENT device only and ALWAYS returns to Welcome (hasSkippedOnboarding=false).
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android SettingsFragment.kt:289-303 sign-out goes to Welcome only if pairedDeviceSNs is empty, otherwise recreate() (stays signed in with the next device). Android DevicePanelActivity.kt:66-90 matches iOS unpair.

findings.behavior: BLE sync state machine: fetchFileList (silent) and startSync (banner) both call PlaudDeviceAgent.getFileList(startSessionId:0); handleFileList treats EVERY file on the device as to-download (synced files are supposed to have been deleted from the device), builds placeholder RecordingFiles (createdAt = sessionId as epoch seconds, duration from BleFile.duration()/1000), replaceAllFiles(localSynced + placeholders), then serial exportAudio(sessionId, Documents, .mp3, mono). Progress 0-99 = download (speed from SDK currentDownloadSpeedKBps), 100 = local transcode ('Converting…'). On complete: markAsSynced, PlaudDeviceAgent.deleteFile(sessionId) (device copy deleted), next file. Home triggers fetchFileList 3s after every .connected unless recording; RecordingManager triggers startSync 1s after record stop.
findings.notes: Android SyncManager.kt:101-139, 616-667, 746-817 identical except: silent fetch never auto-downloads (line 650-654) whereas iOS silent fetch DOES auto-download when new files exist (SyncManager.swift:309-324); Android computes speed itself from fileSize (lines 669-690); Android BleFile exposes no duration so duration is read from the exported file (lines 692-744) and OpusRepair patches the SDK's corrupt OpusTags (OpusRepair.kt:5-16). PARITY DIFFERENCE: iOS device-file placeholders use BleFile.duration(); Android derives it post-export.

findings.behavior: Auto-sync toggle is dead on iOS: SettingsViewController.setupSyncCard() exists but is never called and syncCard is never added to the view hierarchy; RecordingManager.handleRecordStop unconditionally calls SyncManager.startSync() after 1s; isAutoSyncEnabled (default false via UserDefaults.bool) is never read on a live path.
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android renders the toggle (SettingsFragment.kt:44-46), defaults it to true (RecordingStore.kt:143) and honours it in handleRecordStop (RecordingManager.kt:139-146: startSync if enabled else fetchFileList). This is app policy drift, not a platform requirement.

findings.behavior: WiFi fast transfer entry: Home banner 'Fast Transfer' pill -> if CoreLocation denied/restricted show 'Location Permission Needed' with Open Settings; else if UserDefaults fastTransfer_neverShowAgain start directly; else FastTransferSheet (10x copy, Never show again checkbox, Turn on). startWiFiTransfer: if location .notDetermined request WhenInUse and resume on grant; if denied fail; if a BLE export already received bleSyncFileTail defer WiFi until its transcode completes; else stopDownloadFile, state .wifiConnecting(.openingHotspot), PlaudWiFiAgent.delegate=self, PlaudDeviceAgent.setDeviceWiFi(open:true), arm 185s watchdog. bleWiFiOpen(status 0, ssid, pass) -> wait 3s ('matching production C-end waitDeviceWifiDuration=3s') -> PlaudWiFiAgent.connectWifi(ssid,pass,180). wifiHandshake(0) -> .wifiTransferring, getFileList(now,0,false). wifiFileList -> filter already-synced, addFiles placeholders, serial exportAudioViaWiFi(.mp3, mono). After queue drains: batch deleteFile(sid,1) for all synced, wait for wifiFileDelete confirmations (4s fallback), then awaitDeviceWiFiClose (publish .completed, 20s fallback forced teardown). wifiClose(1000) during connect = 'nothing to transfer' treated as completed; other close during connect = 'Could not join the device hotspot'.
findings.notes: Android SyncManager.kt:141-316, 439-561: same policy (no pre-check for unsynced files, deferred batch delete, device-led close with 20s fallback) but: no location gating (Android manifest grants ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION for BLE already), 1.5s DEVICE_IDLE_GRACE before opening the hotspot instead of a 3s post-open wait, 15s delete-confirm timeout vs 4s (PLA2-309 says the 4s window expired too early), keeps publishing WiFiTransferring at 100% until the device closes instead of Completed, and Android's WiFi session is opened with PlaudDeviceAgent.startWifiTransfer(userId, callback) + NiceBuildSdk.stopWifiTransfer. Entitlements com.apple.developer.networking.HotspotConfiguration + wifi-info and NSLocationWhenInUse/NSLocalNetwork usage strings are iOS platform requirements (ios/project.yml:33-35, 58-61).

findings.behavior: BLE drop during WiFi is swallowed (bleDroppedDuringWiFi) to avoid UI flicker; after the transfer reconnectAfterWiFiTransfer sets pendingDeviceWiFiClose = !isConnected() (so the hotspot-close command is sent on the next BLE bind), coalesces one DispatchWorkItem 1.5s later that publishes disconnected and startAutoReconnect(initialDelay:0).
findings.notes: Android DeviceManager.kt:134-140, 447-458; SyncManager.kt:537-560 same pendingDeviceWiFiClose mechanism and 1.5s settle. Comment on both: device otherwise sits in WiFi mode until its '~2 min firmware timeout' (CLAIM about firmware).

findings.behavior: iOS Files tab shows the shared sync banner with the Fast Transfer pill but never assigns syncBanner.onFastTransferTapped, so the pill is inert on Files; only Home wires it.
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android FilesFragment.kt:56-60 wires the pill (never-show-again shortcut included).

findings.behavior: Recording: RecordingManager is a pass-through to PlaudDeviceAgent start/stop/pause/resumeRecord; state comes from bleRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume callbacks (startedAt = sessionId as epoch, else startTime, else now). On bleRecordStart status 0 the iOS app calls PlaudDeviceAgent.syncFile(sessionId,start,0) which makes the SDK stream live audio; blePcmData (decoded PCM 640 B mono) feeds JXRecordVolumer.averageVolume (dB 0-90 normalised) sampled by a 100ms timer into an 80-bar waveform. RecordingViewController shows 'Starting...' with a 4s ack timeout (PLA2-317); tapping while recording stops AND dismisses; there is no pause button (paused state only resumes on tap).
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android RecordingManager.kt:72-108 passes scene=0 and needs the sessionId for pause/resume, adds a 1.5s refreshRecordState fallback, computes RMS itself (lines 166-178), BUT no Android listener method forwards PCM (grep handlePcmData callers: none) so the Android waveform is never fed by real audio; Android RecordingActivity has an explicit Pause/Resume button (lines 43, 124-137). Same 4s START_ACK_TIMEOUT.

findings.behavior: Firmware update is delegated wholly to the iOS SDK: PlaudDeviceAgent.checkFirmwareUpdate after every connect (sets latestFirmwareVersion) and startFirmwareUpdate(progress:completion:) with phases downloading/installing/restarting/complete. The app only sets isOTAInProgress (suppresses reconnect on disconnect), on failure republishes disconnected and startAutoReconnect(3s). FirmwareUpdateSheet (non-dismissable, 30-segment bar) waits after SDK completion for connected->disconnected->connected via connectionStatePublisher with a 60s timeout, then dismisses after 1.5s; Update button appears when latestFirmwareVersion != nil (Settings and DevicePanel). Firmware version displayed as versionTypeStr + major.minor.patch decoded from versionCode (code<255 shown as %04d).
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE (platform/SDK requirement, not policy): Android DeviceManager.kt:521-603 implements the version check in the APP: GET {host}/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/version/latest?type=&sn=&current_version=-1 with X-Device-Signature = PlaudDeviceAgent.getSnSignature() (re-signing via NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn if empty), parses version_code/download_url/version_type/version_number/version_description/is_force/is_strong_guidance/file_md5, then facade downloadFirmware + installFirmware with an app watchdog sized file/2KBps + 5 min (lines 956-1026). Reason stated: Android SDK checkFirmwareUpdate needs an sdkToken from /api/oauth/sdk-token which '404s on platform-us' (lines 524-529). Android version format V{code/65536}.{(code%65536)/256}.{code%256} (lines 514-519) equals iOS decoding.

findings.behavior: AppDelegate raises SDK log rotation (50 files x 50MB x 7 days) and logs a build marker 'wifi-stability-r2'; configure() re-sets 25 x 20MB, disables PlaudLogUploadManager auto-upload, and routes BleAgent mlog/wlog to NSLog so handshake stage lines land in the file. AppLog mirrors every app log line into the SDK's Documents/PlaudLogs/plaud.log via PlaudLogRedirect.addLog. Settings 'Export' calls PlaudLogEncryption.exportEncryptedLogFile() (encrypted .plaud bundle), then PlaudLogRedirect.deleteAllLogFiles(), and presents a share sheet. bleConnectStage(sn,stage,detail) is logged with stages such as preHandshake/sendRSAPublic/firstHandshake and details like sn_signature_invalid.
findings.notes: The SDK exposes uploadLogFile/uploadRecording/uploadLogsAfterRecording/setAutoUploadEnabled (swiftinterface:335-366) -> the SDK has a cloud log/recording upload channel that the template turns OFF; its endpoint is not visible from app source (UNKNOWN). Android SettingsFragment.kt:98-128 uses NiceBuildSdk.exportLog(ctx) + share + clear (same policy).

findings.behavior: Audio playback: AudioPlayerView uses AVAudioPlayer (category .playback), 5s rewind/forward, thumbless slider, CADisplayLink 5-15 fps; shown whenever the synced MP3 exists regardless of transcript. FileDetail 'More' menu: Export Audio (SDK exportAudio .wav to Documents/exports -> UIActivityViewController), Copy Summary (only if summary), Copy Transcript, Delete Recording (local only: SyncManager.deleteFile removes the file at file.localPath and the record).
findings.notes: Android FileDetailActivity.kt:276-340 uses media3 ExoPlayer because 'OEM MediaPlayerNative frequently fails on Ogg/Opus' and self-heals legacy .opus via OpusRepair; adds Rename (line 503) which iOS has only in the store/manager (renameFile has no iOS UI caller). Delete is local-only on both.

findings.behavior: Mock managers exist (MockDeviceManager/MockSyncManager/MockRecordingManager) but nothing in the iOS app instantiates them; every screen binds directly to the .shared singletons.
findings.evidence: ios/PlaudTemplateApp/Managers/Mock/*.swift; ios/PlaudTemplateApp/UI/Home/HomeViewController.swift:8-10 (grep for Mock usage outside Managers/Mock: none)
findings.notes: PARITY DIFFERENCE: Android PlaudTemplateApp.kt:23-38 has USE_MOCK=false switch wiring the mocks. Cosmetic.

findings.behavior: Firmware/device facts asserted by app comments (CLAIMS, not verified here): depair changes the device MAC; the device self-disconnects the WiFi session after 3 heartbeats and otherwise times out in ~2-2.5 min; device refuses openWiFi with status 4 while streaming and WiFi connect fails with 1003; blePenState 4099 (0x1003) = recording; BLE battery reports -1 until known (PLA2-312); firmware install validation requires versionCode matching ^[VT]\d+$.
findings.confidence: INFERRED (engineer comments; LINEAGE-quality claims about firmware)
findings.notes: Cross-check with docs/protocol-ledger.md for 0x1003 and depair semantics is out of this task's scope; listed so the ledger owner can reconcile.

findings.behavior: Cloud facts asserted only by app comments (CLAIMS): bind_history contains one entry per device.bind event with 50+ duplicates of one id 'live-verified'; a missing device on GET /sdk/binding is a bare 404 without ErrorCode body; bind_history is not client-scoped; complete-upload DownloadUrl 'valid for 24h'; upload API rejects wav (FILE_TYPE_INVALID); backend opus pipeline returns empty transcription results; /api/oauth/sdk-token does not exist on platform-us (404); a US token sent to platform-jp returns 401 CLIENT_USER_NOT_FOUND; Partner API baseUrl does not follow initSdk customDomain on Android.

endpoints.purpose: Step 1 of S3 multipart upload; body {filesize:Int, filetype:String}; response {FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize?, Parts:[{PartNumber, PresignedUrl}]}; default URLSession timeout; no retry
endpoints.relationships: TranscriptionManager.uploadFile -> uploadParts; chunk size = ChunkSize ?? 5 MiB

endpoints.purpose: Step 2: raw chunk body, timeoutInterval 120s; success 2xx; ETag header (quotes stripped) collected as {PartNumber, ETag}; sequential, first failure aborts the whole flow

Step 3: body {file_id, upload_id, part_list:[{PartNumber,ETag}], filetype, file_md5?(hex MD5 of whole file)}; timeout 120s; response {FileId?, FileType?, DownloadUrl?, FileMd5?}; empty DownloadUrl treated as failure
endpoints.relationships: DownloadUrl becomes file_url of the transcription submit

endpoints.auth: X-Client-Id: <JWT client_id claim or Info.plist PlaudClientId>; X-Client-Api-Key: <apiKeyOverride or Info.plist PlaudApiKey>; Content-Type: application/json
endpoints.purpose: Submit transcription: body {file_url, params:{transcribe:{language:'auto', model:'plaud-fast-whisper'}, vad:{decode_silence:false}, diarization:{enabled:false, return_embedding:false}}}; timeout 60s; response {status (Int|String), message?, data:{task_id?}, transcription_id?}; id = transcription_id ?? data.task_id

Poll every 5s, max 240 polls (20 min); status top-level or data.task_status in {PENDING,RECEIVED,STARTED,PROGRESS,SUCCESS,FAILURE,REVOKED}; on SUCCESS uses data.results[{speaker_id,start,end,text,language}] (data.text / data.segments also decoded as fallbacks)

Cloud device binding after every successful handshake; body {type:'notepro'|'notepins'|'notepin'|'note' from SN prefix, sn}; only the HTTP status is consumed: 403 -> user alert; nil (transport error) / others ignored; no retry
Cloud unbind before local depair on Unpair / Sign out; body {type, sn}; fire-and-forget (result ignored)
Authoritative binding state for recovery: 200 body {is_bind: true|false|null (three-state), bind_history:[String client_user_ids, newest-first per comment]}; any non-200 -> nil -> recovery fails

unexplained_behaviors: Both published templates default activeServerDomain to platform-test.plaud.ai (comment: 'cloud bind/unbind testing') even though README documents platform-us.plaud.ai as the integration domain (RecordingStore.swift:130-133; RecordingStore.kt:133-135) — why a customer-facing template ships pointed at a test environment is not explained.

iOS SyncManager.deleteFile calls FileManager.removeItem(atPath: file.localPath) but markAsSynced stores only lastPathComponent, so the removal targets a bare filename relative to the process cwd and almost certainly no-ops (try?); local audio is therefore likely orphaned on delete on iOS (SyncManager.swift:243-249; RecordingStore.swift:186-192). Android deletes by absolute path (RecordingStore.kt:174-177).

iOS auto-sync toggle card is fully built but never added to the Settings hierarchy, and record-stop always auto-syncs; Android honours the toggle. No comment explains the removal on iOS (SettingsViewController.swift:164-171, 220-267).
iOS Files tab's Fast Transfer pill has no handler (FilesViewController.swift has no onFastTransferTapped assignment) while Android's Files tab wires it.

Silent fetch semantics diverge: iOS fetchFileList auto-downloads new files (SyncManager.swift:309-324); Android fetchFileList only refreshes the list (SyncManager.kt:650-654) despite both being triggered 3s after connect.

Android listener never forwards PCM (no blePcmData override in DeviceManager.kt) so RecordingManager.handlePcmData is dead and the Android waveform shows nothing real; iOS gets PCM only because it calls PlaudDeviceAgent.syncFile(sessionId,start,0) on bleRecordStart status 0 — whether this opens a live sync stream that also counts toward the file transfer state is not explained (DeviceManager.swift:853-858).

blePenState magic 4099 (0x1003) = 'device is currently recording' and the meaning of the other blePenState fields (privacy, keyState, uDisk, findMyToken, hasSndpKey, deviceAccessToken) are unexplained by any source (DeviceManager.swift:879-895).

depair(clear:true) on normal unpair vs depair(clear:false) during recovery on iOS, and depair(false) everywhere on Android: the semantics of the clear flag are SDK-internal and unexplained (DeviceManager.swift:218, 405; DeviceManager.kt:880, 1163).

PlaudDevice.deviceType maps SN prefix 883 -> 'notepin' on iOS but Android maps 880 -> 'notepin' and 888 -> 'note'; which prefixes really exist for NotePin is unresolved (PlaudDevice.swift:38-46; DeviceManager.kt:791-797).

The 'X-Device-Signature' used by Android for /sdk/version/latest is PlaudDeviceAgent.getSnSignature() (the sn-sign result), which answers the frozen baseline's 'computation site not located' for that header on the version endpoint — but the same header for /sdk/metadata is still only asserted by a comment in PlaudAPIService.swift:9.

The SDK exposes uploadRecording(sn:sessionId:duration:) and uploadLogsAfterRecording — a cloud recording/log upload path the template never uses and whose endpoint/destination is unknown (swiftinterface:335-336, 366).

Android's checkFirmwareUpdate comment states the SDK's own path needs /api/oauth/sdk-token which '404s on platform-us' — this corroborates the frozen baseline's unresolved contradiction between the /api/... AAR surface and the /developer/api/open/partner surface, but does not resolve whether iOS's SDK checkFirmwareUpdate uses the partner surface (it must, since iOS OTA works per FirmwareUpdateSheet, but that is INFERRED).
FastTransferSheet body copy hardcodes 'Plaud NotePin hotspot' even though the template scope is NotePro/NotePin S (FastTransferSheetViewController.swift:37).
cross_source_agreements: iOS and Android templates agree on every cloud request shape: presigned-urls/complete-upload field names (FileId/UploadId/ChunkSize/Parts/PartNumber/PresignedUrl; file_id/upload_id/part_list/filetype/file_md5; DownloadUrl), transcription params (plaud-fast-whisper, language auto, vad decode_silence false, diarization disabled), poll 5s x240, bind/unbind body {type,sn}, binding response {is_bind, bind_history} (PlaudAPIService.swift vs TranscriptionManager.kt/DeviceManager.kt).
Both agree with README.md:543-550 on base URL /developer/api and the auth split (Bearer user token for files; X-Client-Id + X-Client-Api-Key for AI) and with r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md surface B.

Recovery constants (25s handshake, 5s depair, 20s rescan, 5 attempts), auto-reconnect (30s x10), foreground reconnect 2s, post-connect file list 3s, record-stop sync 1s, start-ack 4s, device-close fallback 20s, BLE-settle 1.2s/1.5s are identical on both platforms -> these are app POLICY constants, not platform requirements.

Both platforms persist the same recordings.json schema and the same UserDefaults/SharedPreferences key set (modulo naming), and both delete the device copy only after a successful download, never from the user delete action.

Both templates confirm SDK 1.0.13 recoveryConnectBleDevice and SDK 1.0.9+ semantics (empty BLE name possible, endWiFiTransfer/stopWifiTransfer also closes the device hotspot, progress 100 = local transcode).
cross_source_disagreements: Firmware check ownership: iOS delegates to SDK checkFirmwareUpdate; Android calls GET /sdk/version/latest itself with X-Device-Signature because the AAR path needs a non-existent sdk-token (DeviceManager.kt:524-529) — the frozen baseline lists version/latest under Bearer user token (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:124-126) whereas the Android template sends X-Device-Signature; the inventory's auth attribution for that endpoint should be amended.
Auto-sync: iOS always syncs after record stop and hides the toggle; Android honours a default-on toggle.
Silent fetch: iOS downloads new files; Android only lists them.
Sign out: iOS always returns to Welcome; Android stays in-app if other paired devices remain.
Share export format: iOS WAV, Android MP3; Android refuses to transcribe WAV files with an explicit message, iOS has no such guard (would let the upload API reject them per the Android comment).
Depair flag: iOS depair(clear:true) on unpair, Android depair(false) with 3s fallback.

Initial auto-reconnect delay after an unexpected drop: iOS 3s, Android 2s. WiFi delete-confirm wait: iOS 4s, Android 15s (PLA2-309). Pre-hotspot wait: iOS 3s after bleWiFiOpen, Android 1.5s before opening.
Device-type map: iOS 883->notepin; Android 880->notepin, 888->note.
Version numbers: iOS 1.0.57 (57) vs Android 1.0.56 (56); both cite the same PLA2-3xx/4xx tickets so they are the same release train.

repos: reference/third-party/python-plaud-ai (DmytroLitvinov, v0.1.1 2026-02-10) — THIRD_PARTY_CLOUD_CLIENT (developer platform, docs-mirroring; as shipped cannot authenticate, see findings)

cloud-consumer-api.evidence_role: CLOUD_OBSERVED for the consumer surface (api.plaud.ai) via three reverse-engineered clients whose fixtures encode captured response shapes; CLOUD_OBSERVED-by-documentation only for the developer platform (platform.plaud.ai) because python-plaud-ai mirrors docs.plaud.ai paths and its shipped client has an auth bug that prevents it from ever having talked to the cloud. Nothing was called.
cloud-consumer-api.why_in_corpus: These three clients are the only sources in the corpus that describe what a Plaud USER (not a partner SDK) can do against the cloud: list/upload/download recordings, trigger and poll transcription+summary, edit transcripts and speaker names, read tags, read account/membership. Their test fixtures freeze the JSON envelopes (`data_file_list`, `trans_result`, `ai_content`, `transsumm` status codes, `-302` region redirect, `/user/me` membership) that the frozen baseline (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md section C) lists only as paths. python-plaud-ai additionally establishes that the developer platform is a separate surface (OAuth client credentials, device bind/unbind, workflow submit/status/result, HMAC webhooks) with no overlap in paths or auth with the consumer API.
cloud-consumer-api.summary: The consumer cloud (api.plaud.ai, regional api-euc1/api-apse1, plus api-usw1/api.plaud.cn per baseline r7:21) exposes a File-centric model: a recording is a `file` record (`id`, `filename`, `fullname`, `filesize`, `duration` ms, `start_time`/`end_time` epoch ms, `is_trash`, `is_trans`, `is_summary`, `filetag_id_list`, `serial_number`, `scene`, `edit_time`, `edit_from`, `keywords`) whose transcript (`trans_result[]` of `{speaker, content, start_time, end_time}`) and summary (`ai_content`, a markdown string or JSON `{markdown|content.markdown|summary, header}`) are embedded in the same record when read via `POST /file/list`, or delivered as typed `content_list[]` items (`transaction`, `auto_sum_note`, `sum_multi_note`, `outline`, each with `task_status` and a presigned `data_link`, some inlined in `pre_download_content_list`) when read via `GET /file/detail/{id}`. Upload is client-driven S3 multipart (presign → PUT → merge → confirm with `scene:101`, `serial_number:uuid4`), and — the most product-revealing finding — AI processing is a three-step client-orchestrated flow: `PATCH /file/{id}` with `extra_data.tranConfig{language,type:"REASONING-NOTE",type_type:"system",diarization:1,llm:"auto"}` starts the job, `POST /ai/transsumm/{id}` is polled (status 0 "task processing" → 1 "task complete", with a live-observed `-111 "success"` variant), and the client must `PATCH` `trans_result`/`ai_content`/`outline_result`/`task_id_info` back onto the file to persist them (plaud-api README:117-128). Auth on the consumer surface is a JWT bearer: plaud-toolkit mints it with `POST /auth/access-token` (form username/password; each login mints a new `sid` session and evicts the phone app's session), decodes `iat/exp/region` claims, and observed lifetime shrank from ~300 d to ~30 d; plaud-api takes whatever bearer the user copies from DevTools, which riffado shows is usually the ~24 h workspace token (WT, claims `ut_ref/wid/wtype`) rather than the long-lived user token (UT, `localStorage.pld_tokenstr`); applaud shows the newest model is cookie-based (`pld_ut` ~1 d + `pld_urt` ~30 d, `POST /auth/refresh-user-token`) with WTs minted via `POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{wid}`. Region mismatch is signalled in-band as `{status:-302, msg:"user region mismatch", data:{domains:{api}}}`; plaud-toolkit/riffado/applaud follow it, plaud-api raises. Subscription/entitlement is visible only as `membership_type` on `GET /user/me` (fixture value "starter"); no quota, credit or plan-limit field appears in any request or response, and no client gates anything, so enforcement location is UNKNOWN. The developer platform (platform.plaud.ai/api) is a disjoint surface: `oauth/api-token` (Bearer base64(client_id:secret)), `devices` list/detail/bind/unbind (`owner_id`, `sn_type` in note|notepin|notepro, `sn`), `files/upload-s3/generate-presigned-urls`+`complete-upload`, `workflows/submit|{id}/status|{id}/result`, and HMAC-SHA256 `Plaud-Signature` webhooks whose event names and payloads appear nowhere in the corpus. Speakers are a cloud-side voiceprint list (`/speaker/list` items carry `embedding[]`) but speaker NAMES live only inside each file's `trans_result`, so renaming is a client-side rewrite and PATCH. Tags are `filetag` records with `file_count`; tag→file membership is filtered client-side over the full list.

findings.behavior: Consumer API base hosts are api.plaud.ai (default) with regional api-apse1.plaud.ai (plaud-api) and api-euc1.plaud.ai (plaud-toolkit); JWT `region` claim values observed as 'aws:eu-central-1' and 'aws:us-east-1'; applaud default region key 'aws:us-west-2'.

Region mismatch is an in-band envelope `{status:-302, msg:'user region mismatch', data:{domains:{api:'api-euc1.plaud.ai'}}}` returned with HTTP 200. plaud-toolkit switches region and retries; riffado/applaud follow it once; plaud-api raises APIError and does not follow.

Password login: `POST /auth/access-token`, form-encoded `username`+`password`, response `{status:0, access_token, token_type:'bearer'}`; failure `{status:-2, msg:'wrong account or password'}`. Google-SSO users have no password and must set one via Forgot Password.

Every password login mints a NEW server session (JWT `sid` claim) and the backend evicts older sessions for the account, logging the phone app out. Toolkit therefore reuses the cached token until 5% of lifetime / max 6 h before expiry and re-logs in only on a 401.
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED (single client; behavior is a code-comment claim backed by a regression test)
findings.notes: The `sid` claim is also read by applaud (session.ts:52-53) to mark 'our own session'.

findings.behavior: Token lifetime disagreement inside plaud-toolkit itself: README and plan doc say ~300 days with refresh at <30 days remaining; auth.ts comment says 'Plaud currently issues ~30 days, not the ~300 days this code once assumed' and all current tests use 30-day tokens. Indicates the cloud shortened UT lifetime between the plan (2026-03-11) and the code.

Two token kinds exist on the consumer surface: long-lived user token (UT; web stores it in localStorage `pld_tokenstr`; identity endpoints `/user/me`, `/team-app/workspaces/list`) and short-lived (~24 h) workspace token (WT; JWT claims `ut_ref`, `wid`, `wtype`; used by web.plaud.ai on data requests `/device/list`, `/file/simple/web`). WT minted by `POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{wid}` with Bearer UT; response carries `workspace_token, expires_in, wt_expires_at, refresh_token, refresh_expires_in, refresh_expires_at, workspace_id, member_id, role`.
findings.notes: None of the three target clients mints a WT. plaud-toolkit uses the /auth/access-token JWT directly on /file/simple/web (client.ts:59-63) and its integration test passes with it (integration.test.ts:21-31), so data endpoints accept a UT too.

findings.behavior: Newest first-party auth is cookie-based: `pld_ut` (~1 day) + `pld_urt` (~30 days); `POST /auth/refresh-user-token` with both cookies rotates them (Max-Age=0 clearers first, real value last in Set-Cookie). Plaud stopped exposing `tokenstr` for newer accounts.
findings.notes: Contradicts plaud-toolkit plan doc line 23 'no refresh endpoint, must re-auth'.

findings.behavior: plaud-api's token-acquisition instructions tell the user to copy the `Authorization` header from ANY api.plaud.ai request in DevTools (examples: simple/web, list, filetag). Per riffado those data requests carry the ~24 h WT, which explains plaud-api's troubleshooting entry 'Authentication failed (401): Token expired. Run plaud auth setup'. plaud-api has no refresh path and stores the token in .env or ~/.config/plaud/token.

Consumer API rejects the default Node fetch User-Agent ('node') with 403; clients send a desktop-Chrome/Safari UA. plaud-api additionally sends `Origin: https://web.plaud.ai`, `app-platform: web`, `edit-from: web`, `Sec-Fetch-*` and a random `r` query/body parameter on every GET/POST/PATCH, and uses lowercase `bearer` in Authorization.
findings.notes: `edit-from: web` header pairs with an `edit_from` field on the file record (riffado/src/types/plaud.ts:26): the cloud records which client last edited a file.

findings.behavior: Recording list: `GET /file/simple/web?skip&limit&is_trash=0&sort_by=start_time|edit_time&is_desc=true` → `{status, msg, data_file_total, data_file_list[]}`. Fields per item (union across clients): id, filename, fullname, filetype, filesize, file_md5, ori_ready, version, version_ms, edit_time, edit_from, is_trash, start_time(ms), end_time(ms), duration(ms), timezone, zonemins, scene, filetag_id_list[], serial_number, is_trans, is_summary, keywords[].
findings.notes: is_trans/is_summary are 0/1 ints in plaud-api fixture and booleans in toolkit/riffado types; clients coerce.

findings.behavior: Two distinct detail representations exist. (A) `POST /file/list` body=[file_id,...] → `data_file_list[]` items that embed `trans_result[]`, `ai_content`, `summary_list[]` (plaud-api). (B) `GET /file/detail/{id}` → `{status:0, data:{file_id, file_name, duration, start_time, scene, content_list[], pre_download_content_list[]}}` where content_list items are `{data_id ('source_transaction:'|'auto_sum:'|'sum_multi:' prefix), data_type ('transaction'|'auto_sum_note'|'sum_multi_note'|'outline'), data_title, data_tab_name, task_status (1=ready), data_link (presigned, gzip JSON e.g. trans_result.json.gz)}` and pre_download_content_list inlines `{data_id, data_content(JSON string)}` (plaud-toolkit, riffado).
findings.confidence: CORROBORATED (each representation by ≥2 sources; relationship between them UNKNOWN)

findings.behavior: Transcript segment shape: `{speaker: string, content: string, start_time: ms, end_time: ms}` inside `trans_result[]`. Default speaker labels are 'Speaker 1', 'Speaker 2'. The server-rendered text form seen by plaud-toolkit is markdown lines prefixed `[Speaker N]` with no timestamps.

Summary field `ai_content` is polymorphic: plain markdown, or a JSON string with `{markdown}`, `{content:{markdown}}`, legacy `{summary}`, plus optional `header` which the client re-persists as `extra_data.aiContentHeader`. Fallback source is `summary_list[0]`. riffado's detail parser additionally accepts `key_points|keyPoints|highlights` and `action_items|actionItems|todos` arrays.

Starting transcription+summary is a metadata write: `PATCH /file/{id}` body `{extra_data:{tranConfig:{language:'en', type_type:'system', type:'REASONING-NOTE', diarization:1, llm:'auto'}}}` → response `data_file`. No dedicated 'start job' endpoint.
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED (single client, corroborated by baseline path list)

findings.behavior: Job polling: `POST /ai/transsumm/{id}` body `{is_reload:0, summ_type:'REASONING-NOTE', summ_type_type:'system', info: JSON-string {language, diarization:1, llm:'auto'}, support_mul_summ:true}`. Responses observed: `{status:0, msg:'task processing'}`; `{status:1, msg:'task complete', data_result[], data_result_summ, outline_result[], task_id_info{}}`; and a live-captured `{status:-111, msg:'success', data_result[...], data_result_summ:''}` treated as complete. Client polls every 10 s up to 500-600 s; README says long recordings take up to 10 min.
findings.notes: The -111/'success' case is explicitly labelled a live observation in the test name ('test_complete_live_success_status_negative').

findings.behavior: Persisting results is the CLIENT's job: after polling, `PATCH /file/{id}` with `{trans_result, ai_content, outline_result, support_mul_summ:true, extra_data:{task_id_info, aiContentHeader}}` — README: 'required after wait() to persist the transcription and summary to the Plaud cloud'. The same PATCH with only `trans_result` is used to rename speakers (client rewrites `speaker` strings in every segment).
findings.notes: Implies the web app, not the server, commits AI output to the file record; whether the mobile app behaves the same is UNKNOWN.

findings.behavior: Speakers: `GET /speaker/list` → `data_speaker_list[{id, name, embedding:[float...]}]` (global, read-only, 'used for voice identification'); `/speaker/sync` path declared but never called. Speaker names in transcripts are not linked to these ids; per-recording speaker stats are computed client-side from `trans_result`.

Tags: `GET /filetag/` → `data_filetag_list[{id, name, file_count}]`. There is no tag-filter parameter: tag→recordings is computed client-side by fetching `/file/simple/web` with limit=99999 and filtering `filetag_id_list`.

Upload (consumer): `POST /file/get_upload_presigned_url {filesize, file_type:'MP3'|'OPUS'}` → `data{part_urls[], upload_id, object_name}`; PUT bytes to `part_urls[0]` with no Plaud auth and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, capture `ETag`; `POST /file/merge_multipart {upload_id, object_name, parts:[{Etag, PartNumber:1}]}`; `POST /file/confirm_upload {upload_id, object_name, scene:101, is_tmp:0, support_mul_summ:true, file_type, filename, start_time(ms), session_id(sec), serial_number: uuid4}` → `data` = new file record. '.asr' extension is mapped to OPUS.
findings.notes: `serial_number` on device-originated files is presumably the device SN (riffado type plaud.ts:35 lists it on every file); web uploads fake it with a UUID. `scene` is a numeric category (101 for web upload).

findings.behavior: Audio download: `GET /file/temp-url/{id}?is_opus=0|1|false` → `{status, temp_url, temp_url_opus?}` presigned S3; `GET /file/download/{id}` with Bearer streams bytes directly. plaud-toolkit sniffs the first bytes for ID3/MPEG sync because the download may be MP3 or Opus regardless of extension; riffado prefers `temp_url_opus`.

Trash: list excludes `is_trash` items; plaud-toolkit's Obsidian plugin trashes remotely via `PATCH /file/{id} {is_trash:true}` with fallback `POST /file/trash {file_ids:[id]}` — both untested guesses (no fixture).

Account: `GET /user/me` → `data_user{id, nickname, email, country}` and `data_state.membership_type` (toolkit code) — but the toolkit's own fixture puts `membership_type:'starter'` inside `data_user`, so the code path yields 'unknown' against its own fixture. No quota, credits, minutes, plan-limit or entitlement field appears in any request or response of the three clients; no client gates transcription start on plan.
findings.evidence: plaud-toolkit/packages/core/src/client.ts:84-94; plaud-toolkit/packages/core/src/types.ts:88-94; plaud-toolkit/packages/core/test/client.test.ts:75-86; plaud-api/src/plaud/models.py (no such fields); python-plaud-ai (no such fields)

findings.behavior: The web app (web.plaud.ai) is the reference client both Python/TS clients emulate: Origin/Referer headers, `app-platform: web`, `edit-from: web`, token in localStorage `pld_tokenstr` (older) or `pld_ut`/`pld_urt` cookies (newer).

plaud-toolkit Obsidian sync model: poll `/file/simple/web` every 60 min; dedup by a local `syncedIds[]` list in plugin settings and `plaud_id` frontmatter; per recording: download audio → if original is .opus, fetch MP3 via temp-url → `GET /file/detail` → use server transcript if `hasRealTranscript` (len>20 and not JSON) else run local mlx-whisper → write note. Pending markers ('Awaiting Plaud server transcription', 'No MP3 version available yet', ...) drive a retranscribe pass.

`pre_download_content_list[].data_content` can contain a 'marks' JSON payload (`mark_type`, `mark_content`, `timestamp`) before the real transcript is ready; toolkit's longest-string heuristic would otherwise pick it as the transcript.
findings.notes: Consistent with riffado's data_id-keyed model (content.ts:92-108): toolkit ignores data_id and so misreads which inline item is which.

findings.behavior: The MCP server exposes exactly five user-facing operations: plaud_list_recordings (id,title,date,duration_minutes,has_transcript), plaud_get_transcript, plaud_get_recording_detail, plaud_user_info, plaud_get_mp3_url. No search, no summary, no tags, no speakers, no upload — i.e. read-only consumption of the cloud's list/detail/temp-url.

Developer platform device operations: `POST devices` (list), `GET devices/{id}`, `POST devices/bind {owner_id, sn_type, sn}`, `POST devices/unbind {same}`; `sn_type` enum note|notepin|notepro taken from docs.plaud.ai device_operations tutorial. Consumer surface device enumeration is `GET /device/list` → `data_devices[{sn, name, model, version_number}]` (riffado).

Developer platform auth: `POST platform.plaud.ai/api/oauth/api-token` with `Authorization: Bearer base64(client_id:secret_key)` → `data['api_token']`; all other calls `Authorization: Bearer <api_token>`; app credentials issued via a Google Form survey linked from docs.plaud.ai. This mirrors the SDK-internal 3-hop chain in baseline surface A (sdk-token ← Bearer Base64(appKey:appSecret)).
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED (docs-mirroring), CORROBORATED with BYTECODE_PROVEN baseline for the Basic-under-Bearer pattern

findings.behavior: Developer platform processing is a workflow abstraction: `POST workflows/submit` (opaque data dict), `GET workflows/{id}/status`, `GET workflows/{id}/result`; upload via `POST files/upload-s3/generate-presigned-urls` and `POST files/upload-s3/complete-upload` (opaque data). No field names for any of these are in the corpus.

Developer platform webhooks: the ONLY thing documented is signature verification — HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the raw request body keyed by `webhook_secret`, compared (constant-time) to the `Plaud-Signature` header. No event names, no payload schema, no delivery/retry semantics anywhere in the corpus (grep for Plaud-Signature/webhook/event across reference/ finds only Langfuse's Stripe handler).
findings.evidence: python-plaud-ai/plaud_ai/webhook.py:7-15; python-plaud-ai/README.md:52-64; corpus grep (no other hits)

findings.behavior: python-plaud-ai as shipped cannot authenticate: `__init__` sets `self.api_token = api_token` then overwrites it with `self._get_module(OAuthTokenAPI)`, so `_get_headers` emits `Bearer <OAuthTokenAPI object repr>`; also `DeviceAPI.list(self, token)` ignores its argument. Its evidence weight is therefore 'transcribed from docs.plaud.ai', not 'observed the live cloud'.

Consumer vs developer surface are disjoint: different hosts (api.plaud.ai vs platform.plaud.ai/api), different auth (user JWT/WT vs OAuth client-credential api_token), different nouns (file/filetag/speaker/ai/transsumm/user vs devices/files/upload-s3/workflows/oauth), different job model (client-orchestrated PATCH+poll+PATCH-persist vs submit/status/result + webhook). The developer 'files/upload-s3/*' paths coincide with the SDK-internal paths (baseline A) not the consumer '/file/get_upload_presigned_url' path.

Response envelope convention on the consumer surface: HTTP 200 with `{status:int, msg:str, ...}`; `status:0` = success on auth/detail/user endpoints; `data_*` prefixed collections (`data_file_list`, `data_filetag_list`, `data_speaker_list`, `data_devices`, `data_user`, `data_state`, `data_file`, `data_file_total`); errors are negative status codes (-2 wrong password, -302 region, -111 observed on a successful transsumm). HTTP 401 is used for dead tokens, 403 for bot UA, 5xx retried.

OTP login exists as an alternative to password: `POST /auth/otp-send-code {username, user_area}` → `{token}` (may return -302), then `POST /auth/otp-login {code, token, user_area}` → `{access_token, token_type}` (returns a UT).
findings.notes: Not implemented in plaud-toolkit code; plan-only there.

findings.behavior: plaud-toolkit claims the raw `.opus` from `/file/download` is 'encrypted' and cannot be transcribed locally, and that opening the recording in the Plaud app is what makes an MP3 available. Baseline shows cloud downloads are ordinary Ogg/Opus tagged vendor 'PALUD.AI' served as .mp3; whether 'encrypted' means anything beyond 'mlx-whisper could not decode it' is unexplained.

mobile-android.why_in_corpus: This is the only Plaud-published, complete, buildable mobile client in the corpus, so it is the sole PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE for the product model above the packet: what a partner app persists locally, how it decides when to pull/delete recordings, how ownership of a device is split between firmware lock and cloud binding record, how transcription is driven (upload -> submit -> poll) and what is kept afterwards. It also fixes the division of labour between phone, SDK, device and cloud that the SDK binary alone cannot show. Its code comments additionally leak Plaud-internal facts (ticket ids PLA2-3xx/401, SDK bugs, facade gaps, backend quirks such as "opus pipeline returns empty results", "upload rejects wav", "bind_history not client-scoped") that are LINEAGE-grade claims about the live system.
mobile-android.summary: The Android template app (40 Kotlin files, 7.1k lines, com.plaud.template, versionName 1.0.56) is a thin product shell over the sdk.PlaudDeviceAgent facade. Persistence is deliberately primitive: one SharedPreferences file "plaud_template_prefs" (device pairing list, active SN, userId, auto-sync flag, token/api-key/server overrides, onboarding-skip flag) plus a single Gson-serialised filesDir/recordings.json holding RecordingFile rows (id, sessionId, deviceSN, name, duration, createdAt, syncedAt, localPath, summaryText, transcriptJSON); there is no database, no encryption at rest in the app, and audio is exported by the SDK as mono MP3 into cacheDir/export (an evictable cache directory) while the filesDir/audio/<sid>.opus helper and clearAll() are dead code. Navigation is Welcome -> Scanning(+DeviceConnectBottomSheet) -> Success -> Main(Home/Files/Settings) with Recording, DevicePanel and FileDetail activities and FastTransfer/FirmwareUpdate sheets; routing is decided from pairedDeviceSNs/hasSkippedOnboarding/userId before the first screen inflates. The recording state machine (Idle/Recording/Paused) is device-authoritative: the app only sends commands and mirrors bleRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume callbacks, with a 1.5 s refreshRecordState drift check; the advertised PCM waveform is never fed on Android because handlePcmData has no caller and the facade listener has no blePcmData. Sync is "device is the inventory": every file-list reply rebuilds recordings.json as (locally-synced rows) + (unsynced device rows named "Untitled Recording", createdAt = sessionId*1000), downloads sequentially, and always deletes each file from the device after a successful download (BLE: per file, fire-and-forget; Wi-Fi: batched deleteFiles with a 15 s confirm and 20 s device-self-close wait). Contrary to the README, connecting only triggers a silent list refresh; the auto-sync toggle only governs download after a recording stops. Device ownership is dual: the firmware lock (handshake must carry the bound client_user_id) and a cloud binding record (POST sdk/bind on every successful connect, POST sdk/unbind before local depair, GET sdk/binding for is_bind/bind_history), and the app implements a "brick recovery" that replays up to five historical ids from bind_history through recoveryConnectBleDevice, depairs, rescans (MAC changes) and reconnects; r7-s12 runtime capture confirms that entry point writes the historical id into the k3 handshake with no network call. Identity is a partner-issued userAccessToken JWT baked in via local.properties or pasted in Settings; userId is the unverified JWT sub (random UUID fallback), X-Client-Id is the JWT client_id claim, and the default server environment is platform-test.plaud.ai. Transcription is upload (3-step presigned S3 multipart, Bearer) -> POST ai/transcriptions/ (X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key, model plaud-fast-whisper, language auto, VAD on, diarization off) -> GET poll every 5 s up to 240 times; only the results array is persisted (as transcriptJSON), the transcription_id is not, and no summary is ever requested although the UI and model carry summaryText. Auto-reconnect is foreground-only (ActivityLifecycleCallbacks, 2 s delay, rescan every 30 s, max 10, 10 s scan timeout), there are no services, notifications, WorkManager or offline queues. OTA is app-side version check (GET sdk/version/latest with X-Device-Signature, current_version=-1) then facade download/install with an app watchdog of fileLen/2 KB/s + 5 min.

findings.behavior: Navigation graph: WelcomeActivity is the LAUNCHER and routes BEFORE inflating: if (pairedDeviceSNs non-empty OR hasSkippedOnboarding) AND userId != null it calls deviceManager.configure(userId) and jumps to MainActivity; 'Get Started' derives userId from the token and opens ScanningActivity; 'Connect device later' sets hasSkippedOnboarding=true and opens Main. ScanningActivity shows DeviceConnectBottomSheet on the first scan hit (re-shown only if a not-yet-dismissed SN appears), navigates to OnboardingSuccessActivity on Connected (or finish() when launched in add-device mode), and restarts the scan 2 s after any Disconnected. Success -> Main with CLEAR_TASK. MainActivity re-routes to Welcome if lastConnectedDeviceSN==null && !hasSkippedOnboarding, then hosts Home/Files/Settings fragments via hide/show. Home -> RecordingActivity, DevicePanelActivity, ScanningActivity(add-device), FileDetailActivity; Files -> FileDetailActivity. Sheets: DeviceConnectBottomSheet, FastTransferSheet (Home and Files), FirmwareUpdateSheet (Settings and DevicePanel). Dialogs: cloud binding alert, recovery offers, Bluetooth-off prompt.

findings.behavior: RecordingStore persists two things. (1) SharedPreferences file 'plaud_template_prefs' (MODE_PRIVATE) with keys: last_connected_device_sn (String, doubles as activeDeviceSN), paired_device_sns (Gson JSON array String), paired_device_names (Gson JSON map SN->name), user_id, is_auto_sync_enabled (default TRUE), fast_transfer_never_show, user_access_token_override, api_key_override, server_domain_override, has_skipped_onboarding. (2) filesDir/recordings.json: a Gson List<RecordingFile> rewritten in full on every mutation (add/delete/rename/updateDuration/updateTranscript/markAsSynced/replaceAllFiles) under a JVM lock. No SQLite/Room, no EncryptedSharedPreferences, no encryption at rest in the app.
findings.notes: The token override is stored in plain SharedPreferences (RecordingStore.kt:84-86). allFiles is sorted createdAt-desc on every read (153-156).

findings.behavior: RecordingFile schema (Gson @SerializedName): id (UUID string, app-generated), sessionId (Long, device session id = epoch seconds), deviceSN, name (default 'Untitled Recording'), duration (seconds), createdAt (ms = sessionId*1000), syncedAt (ms or null), localPath (absolute path or null), summaryText (never written by any code path), transcriptJSON (raw results array string). isSynced := localPath != null. addFiles dedupes by sessionId, delete/rename/updateTranscript key by id, markAsSynced keys by sessionId.
findings.notes: sessionId is the cross-layer identifier (device file id == BLE sessionId == createdAt source). No cloud id is ever stored for a recording.

findings.behavior: Synced audio lives in cacheDir/export (RecordingStore.exportDir), not in filesDir: both BLE exportAudio and Wi-Fi exportAudioViaWiFi are given outputDir = exportDir, format MP3, channels 1; the SDK chooses the file name (outputFile.name is only logged) and localPath is set to outputFile.absolutePath. RecordingStore.audioFilePath() (filesDir/audio/<sessionId>.opus) and clearAll() (which wipes filesDir/audio and all prefs) have no callers. FileProvider exposes both cache and files roots for sharing.

Since the device copy was deleted after sync, the audio is then unrecoverable from the app's point of view.

Nothing else (no cloud sync of the library: the app never lists or fetches recordings/transcripts from the cloud). Sign-out/unpair does NOT clear recordings.json or audio (clearAll is unreachable); the code comment says synced recordings intentionally survive.
