cross_source_agreements: iOS swiftinterface CommonType ordinal order matches Android s0$b$b name order and the ledger's 21 wire values (ledger §5.12 vs PlaudBleSDK swiftinterface:596-617).
Both templates declare bleBind(status 0) as connection success and treat GATT-then-drop as an account lock (android DeviceManager.kt:196-330; ios DeviceManager.swift:98-102,625-716).

Both templates and the SDK bytecode agree the recovery token is the historical client_user_id with 'client_user_' stripped and hyphens removed (android DeviceManager.kt:1071-1076; ios DeviceManager.swift:334-338; ALL.txt:2653-2760).
README, templates and FirmwareUpdateManager agree on SN prefix -> type mapping for 881/882 (and 880/888 in templates + FUM).
README 'V66055' example, template formatter and FirmwareUpdateManager regex '^[VT]\d+$' agree on the version string shape.
Ledger §7 SN-derived SSID/passphrase agrees with WifiAgentImpl.calculateWifiName/Password and the iOS comment 'falls back to the SN-derived default'.
Ledger §4.3 (AES-GCM Wi-Fi only, bit 3) agrees with WifiAgentImpl.saveEncryptionKeys 'wifiUseAes' selection and iOS SecretUtil.decryptWithFallback(preferAes:).
Both templates implement identical Wi-Fi teardown policy (deferred batch delete, device-led close, deferred hotspot close when BLE is down).
cross_source_disagreements: Firmware check ownership: iOS template uses SDK-internal checkFirmwareUpdate; Android template bypasses the facade because the SDK's /api/oauth/sdk-token dependency '404s on platform-us' (android DeviceManager.kt:521-530) — the two SDKs do not use the same cloud surface for the same operation (inventory §B contradiction).

blePenState arity: iOS delegate has 7 params (+2 in BleAgentProtocol: versionType, versionCode) vs Android listener 4 (state, privacy, keyState, uDisk) — Android drops findMyToken/hasSndpKey/deviceAccessToken and sessionId (android DeviceManager.kt:374-378; ALL.txt:1144-1176).
Depair variants: iOS unpair calls depair(clear:true) while Android unpair calls depair(false); no source defines `clear`.
Model prefix 883: android models/PlaudDevice.kt:28 maps '883' to 'Plaud NotePin' whereas every other source maps NotePin to 880.

Android template startWifiTransfer passes RecordingStore.userId, README calls the param userId, the facade names it 'sn', WifiAgentImpl names it 'userId' — and none of them feed the handshake token (ALL.txt:3634-3645,123454-123500).

Default partner API host: SDK defaults to platform-jp (ALL.txt:20628) while templates default to platform-test / platform-us and must call updateBaseUrl manually (android DeviceManager.kt:164-173; RecordingStore.kt:110-135).
unexplained_behaviors: Device-to-cloud channel: BLE Get/SetWebsocket (url/serToken/devToken), testWebsocket, 'sync when idle' router Wi-Fi configs (index/ssid/password/test/onWifiSyncUrl), sendApiToken/sendHttpTokenToDevice (api_token + CRC pushed to the device via sendBinFileInfo/Data/CheckSum), setSoundPlusToken(licenseKey), setCommonParams(dataType,value), getSDFLASHCID — fully present in the SDK, used by no template, described by no document. What the device does with a cloud token/URL is UNKNOWN.

The advertised bindInfo byte / isBindInfoOk and blePenState fields privacy, keyState, findMyToken, hasSndpKey, deviceAccessToken: parsed and surfaced, never consumed; product semantics (privacy mode, key state, 'sndp key', device access token) UNKNOWN.
setDeviceActive(status) / bleSetActive: an 'activation' verb with no caller and no documented meaning.
restoreFactory ('restoreFactorySettings'), clearAllFiles (opcode 104), appResetPassword/ResetPasswordRsp{defaultPassword}, resetFindmy: exist; effect on binding, keys and files UNKNOWN.
depair(clear: Bool): iOS uses true for unpair and false for recovery; what 'clear' changes is UNKNOWN. Plaud comments state depair changes the device's BLE MAC — mechanism unexplained.

OTA: meaning of p4.d() pacing constants 40 vs 160 and of the 160-byte alternate chunk mode (p4.p()); 'thirdVersion' (GetThirdVersionRsp opcode 54) and version type 'T'; 'G101' error prefix; 'isSilent' OTA (status 13) and SyncOtaFileInfoRsp (opcode 151) / bleSyncOtaFileInfo(isSilent, packetCheckOk) — a silent/background OTA path with no caller in the templates.
is_strong_guidance and is_force flags in version/latest: templates read is_force but neither enforces it.

Wi-Fi: the device 'heartbeats ~3 times then self-disconnects', '~2 min firmware timeout in AP mode', 'openWiFi status 4 busy', 'connect 1003' — all reported by Plaud engineers in comments, none observable here; OpenWiFiRsp wifiPass is discarded by Android (ledger §7) but 'echoed' per iOS comment.

Recording: any maximum file length (the 5 h premise) — nothing in the corpus constrains it; RecScene/RecMode/VadSensitivity/VpuGain/BatteryMode/VPUCLK product meanings; what 'scene' (0 in templates) and 'sceneFlag/settingScene' select; RecordStart 'reason' codes; BleFile.attribute (U3) and penCollect.
Storage: units of StorageRsp free/total/duration (U2) and whether AutoClear (wire 4) deletes synced files automatically on-device.
Charging: whether StopRecordAfterCharging/AUTO_STOP_RECORD stops a recording when the charger is attached, and BatteryMode values.
LED/buttons: hideLed, GetLedStatusRsp onOff, Backlight Bright1..6/Sec10..Always and SwitchHandlerID CallSceneSwitching semantics; 'blue LED' = AP mode is the only LED behaviour stated.

Legacy identity surfaces (appKey/appSecret/bindToken, CustomerAuth/SSNAuth temp/notRestricted/restricted, checkSn/checkCustomer, GetSsnRsp) coexist with the JWT path; which one production Plaud apps use is UNKNOWN (ledger U21).

Cloud contradiction remains: SDK-internal /api/... surface vs template /developer/api/open/partner/... surface for the same operations (inventory §B), plus platform-jp default host vs platform-us/test in templates.
The 'device lifecycle guide' (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §4.5) that both templates cite for bind/unbind/recovery order is not in the corpus.
Whether MetadataRequest (reportDeviceMetadata: sn, type, version, portVersion config) influences any cloud behaviour is UNKNOWN.

observability-lineage.evidence_role: plaud-opik = LINEAGE_FORK (fork-button copy, no Plaud delta); langfuse = LINEAGE_FORK (fork-button copy, no Plaud delta); goreplay = LINEAGE_FORK with a small Plaud-authored deployment delta (Jenkinsfile + Dockerfile committed by shuo@plaud.ai); upstream/opik and upstream/goreplay = UPSTREAM_REFERENCE
observability-lineage.why_in_corpus: These three repos are the only evidence in the corpus about Plaud's server-side observability and traffic tooling. They show what the Plaud-AI GitHub org has forked (Langfuse, Opik, GoReplay) and, for GoReplay only, one concrete Plaud-engineer commit describing how the tool is packaged and launched (raw capture on :8080 replayed to http://localhost:7100 via Jenkins). They contribute nothing to the device/app/cloud product model beyond org-level tooling interest; none of them contains Plaud configuration, prompts, evaluators, datasets or endpoints.
observability-lineage.summary: Using the precomputed delta manifests and direct file comparison (no git history, per rules), I settled lineage by content. plaud-opik is a byte-for-byte snapshot of upstream comet-ml/opik at v1.9.48 (version.txt 1.9.48, helm Chart 1.9.47, HEAD commit 2025-12-15 'Rename Hierarchical ooptimizer to HAPO (#4430)' which is comet-ml's PR numbering); upstream is now 2.2.73, so the 1503 only-in-Plaud / 3120 modified files are pure upstream version drift: a sample of 600 only-in-Plaud files shows 443 mentioning comet/opik, zero mentioning Plaud/NotePin/Tinno, and the only CJK hits are two PNGs. Verdict: fork-button copy. langfuse is a snapshot of upstream langfuse/langfuse v3.124.1 (package.json), HEAD authored by Langfuse maintainer Max Deichmann 2025-11-02 (#10145); README.md is upstream English, README.cn.md/ja/kr are upstream's own localisations (link to langfuse.com/cn), the deploy workflows are Langfuse's own ECS pipeline driven by repo vars, docker-compose pulls stock docker.io/langfuse images, env examples contain only localhost/example.com hosts, and there are zero Plaud mentions, no custom evaluators, prompts or datasets (the evals/prompts/datasets dirs are upstream product features). Verdict: fork-button copy, not a Chinese localisation. goreplay differs from upstream probelabs/goreplay (v2.0.0 in both version.go) by exactly two files: a new Jenkinsfile and a rewritten Dockerfile, both in Chinese, committed by shuolin0424 <shuo@plaud.ai> on 2025-11-25 as Plaud-AI PR #2 ('Add deployment support' / 'Add ca certs in docker file'). The Dockerfile switches from downloading the release tarball to building from source on ubuntu:20.04 with libpcap-dev and CGO static linking (needed for --input-raw pcap capture); the Jenkinsfile builds that image and runs it with --network host, --cap-add NET_RAW/NET_ADMIN, defaults --input-raw :8080 --output-http http://localhost:7100 --verbose. Verdict: deployed-and-customised (deployment-only; no Plaud markers in text, Plaud attribution comes from the commit author email). Across the rest of the corpus (Plaud source repos, the AAR javap, third-party clients) there is no import of langfuse or opik and no reference to port 7100 or goreplay, so nothing links these tools to the production Plaud app, SDK or cloud. The dump.md claim that Plaud 'runs both tracing and eval infra' is not supported by content: the evidence proves only that the org forked both platforms within ~6 weeks of each other (Nov 2 and Dec 15, 2025 snapshots) without modification; the co-presence is most consistent with an evaluation/comparison of LLM-observability vendors, but that is INFERRED. The on-device observability lineage visible in the SDK bytecode is a Timber FileLoggingTree plus an EncryptedLogExporter, unrelated to either platform.

findings.behavior: How Plaud packages GoReplay: build from source on ubuntu:20.04 with libpcap-dev, CGO_ENABLED=1, statically linked, into a FROM scratch image with CA certs (replacing upstream's alpine download-the-release-tarball flow). This is what is required for raw pcap capture (--input-raw).
findings.evidence: reference/plaud-org/goreplay/Dockerfile:1-3 (Chinese header '用于从源码构建 GoReplay，包含 libpcap 依赖'), :5 FROM ubuntu:20.04, :10-20 apt-get build-essential flex bison libpcap-dev, :34 CGO_ENABLED=1, :41 go build -ldflags '-extldflags "-static"' -o gor ./cmd/gor/, :48-55 FROM scratch + COPY ca-certificates.crt + ENTRYPOINT ["/gor"]; upstream reference/upstream/goreplay/Dockerfile:1-7 FROM alpine:3.16, wget github release tarball
findings.notes: PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE (Plaud-authored). The Go toolchain version is resolved at build time from go.dev/VERSION (Dockerfile:24-25), so the build is not pinned.

findings.behavior: How Plaud launches GoReplay: a parameterised Jenkins pipeline builds the image and runs a long-lived container on the host network with NET_RAW/NET_ADMIN, capturing raw HTTP on a port (default :8080) and replaying it to an HTTP target (default http://localhost:7100) with --verbose; container restarts unless stopped. This is a same-host traffic mirroring setup ('模式2：命令行工具方式').
findings.evidence: reference/plaud-org/goreplay/Jenkinsfile:5-17 params IMAGE_TAG/IMAGE_NAME/CONTAINER_NAME/INPUT_RAW=':8080'/OUTPUT_HTTP='http://localhost:7100'/EXTRA_ARGS='--verbose'/RESTART_CONTAINER=true; :50 gorArgs = "--input-raw ${INPUT_RAW} --output-http ${OUTPUT_HTTP}"; :58-67 docker run -d --cap-add=NET_RAW --cap-add=NET_ADMIN --network host --restart unless-stopped; :73 health check via docker ps | grep
findings.notes: PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE for the mechanism; INFERRED for purpose. The Jenkinsfile never names prod/staging/test, which service listens on :8080, or what runs on :7100; both are overridable defaults. It therefore supports 'Plaud mirrors live HTTP traffic from one service to another instance' but not specifically 'prod into test'.

findings.behavior: No Plaud source repo, no third-party cloud client, and no SDK bytecode references Langfuse, Opik, GoReplay or port 7100; nothing in the corpus ties either observability platform to the production Plaud app, SDK or cloud.

docs-apis-openapi.source_cluster: docs.plaud.ai official developer documentation (OFFICIAL_DOC claims), fetched 2026-09-23 into build/docs-plaud-ai/ — OpenAPI specs (auth, binding, file, transcription, transcription-model), api-reference pages, Plaud Embedded overview/quickstart/billing/data-retention/changelog/devices/playground pages, MCP/CLI pages; cross-checked against r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md (bytecode/template record)
docs-apis-openapi.summary: The public docs describe ONE partner HTTP surface, `https://platform-{us|jp}.plaud.ai/developer/api` (OpenAPI servers list only US+JP; data-retention adds EU `platform-eu` and SG `platform-sg` by sales contact), with 10 documented endpoints in four groups: Authentication (Basic client_id:secret_key -> partner token, TTL 3600 s with refresh_token; partner Bearer -> per-user token, user_id 6-120 chars, requested `expires_in` e.g. 86400), Device Binding (Bearer user token; bind/unbind/binding on `{type: notepro|notepins, sn}`; 403 already-bound-elsewhere, bare 404 unknown SN; `is_bind` tri-state true/false/null; `bind_history[]` client IDs newest-first with duplicates), File Upload (Bearer user token; presign 5 MB (5242880 B) chunks -> S3 PUT parts collecting ETags -> complete-upload -> DownloadUrl valid ~24 h; filetype "mp3" or "opus"), and Transcription (X-Client-Id + X-Client-Api-Key headers, NOT the user token; POST file_url + params -> `task_exec_*` id; poll GET; status enum PENDING/RECEIVED/STARTED/PROGRESS (in-progress) / SUCCESS (terminal ok) / FAILURE, REVOKED (terminal failure); limits 60 req/min, 24 h max recording, 6 h max diarization, docs also say chunk recordings >5 h; results retained 7 days by default). The two transcription specs differ: `transcription.json` (the one the api-reference pages render) has `hotwords` and an `embeddings` map in the example but no `model`; `transcription-model.json` adds `transcribe.model` (default `plaud-fast-whisper`; options `plaud-fast-whisper`, `plaud-omni-3`, `azure-fast-transcribe`) and drops hotwords/embeddings; the playground uses a fourth name `plaud-transcribe-1`. Segment shape is doc-internally inconsistent (`results[].speaker_id/language/language_probability` in OpenAPI vs `segments[].speaker` in prose pages). Billing: free 50 connected devices + 300 transcription hours (unlocked after first device connection); PAYG $15/device/month (peak devices in month) + $0.28/hour, billed end of month, 7-day grace on payment failure, no PAYG caps, enterprise for HIPAA/volume. MCP/CLI (v1.0.0 GA May 12 2026) expose login/logout/get_current_user/list_files/get_file/get_note/get_transcript; get_file adds presigned_url (24 h), source_list, note_list; CLI search is client-side case-insensitive keyword over up to 500 most recent recording names; CLI api_base default `https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api`. Changelog: v1.0.0 May 12 2026 beta launch; v1.0.5 May 18 (MP3 export, WiFi fast transfer); v1.0.6 Jun 29 (transfer insights); v1.0.11 Aug 3 (Android SDK parity); v1.0.13 Aug 24 (recoveryConnectBleDevice, connection-stage callbacks); v1.0.14 Sep 14 2026 'Workflow Query Deprecation: deprecated workflow status and result query APIs on iOS and Android' — consistent with the advanced SDK pages marking `PlaudWorkflowManager` / `workflow` methods deprecated and with r7 surface A `/api/workflows/*` existing in the binary but nowhere in the docs. Docs never document `/api/oauth/sdk-token`, `/api/sdk/api-token`, `/api/files/upload-s3/*`, `/api/workflows/*`, `/api/oauth/api-token`, but the advanced Android page explicitly states `NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice` posts to `/api/devices/bind` 'with a different credential' and is NOT the documented cloud bind, and that Android's version check is `GET /api/sdk/latest-version` while iOS uses the partner endpoint with `X-Device-Signature` — an official statement that the two families are distinct services (partially answering r7's open 'alias or not' question, still only a claim). The SDK's `ServerEnvironment` default `US_PROD = https://platform-jp.plaud.ai` (r7) contradicts the docs' US default `platform-us.plaud.ai`.

findings.behavior: Partner token: POST /oauth/partner/access-token with HTTP Basic base64(client_id:secret_key), Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, no body documented; returns {access_token, refresh_token, token_type:'bearer', expires_in} with example expires_in 3600. Refresh: POST /oauth/partner/access-token/refresh, same Basic auth, form body refresh_token (required), same response shape, 'Refresh before the current token expires'.
findings.evidence: openapi_auth.json:19-53 (partner token), :55-106 (refresh), :77-83 (refresh_token required), :43-48 and :96-101 (examples expires_in 3600), :174-178 (basicAuth scheme), :206-227 (PartnerTokenResponse); plaud-embedded_auth-api-overview.md:38-51
findings.notes: 3600 appears only as an example value, never as a stated constant; no partner refresh_token TTL is stated. api-reference pages render root `security: []` but keep operation-level basicAuth (api-reference_authentication-api_get-partner-token.md:26,51-52).

findings.behavior: User token: POST /open/partner/users/access-token with Authorization: Bearer <partner_access_token>, JSON body {user_id (string, required, minLength 6, maxLength 120, 'Your stable identifier for the user'), expires_in (integer, optional, requested lifetime in seconds, example 86400)}; returns {access_token, token_type:'bearer', expires_in} — NO refresh_token for user tokens. This is the token the Embedded SDK, file-upload and binding endpoints accept.
findings.evidence: openapi_auth.json:108-169, :131-137 (user_id constraints), :138-142 (expires_in), :229-247 (UserTokenResponse has no refresh_token); plaud-embedded_auth-api-overview.md:57-74; plaud-embedded_api-playground.md:5-11
findings.notes: No max/min for expires_in is stated; no statement whether the server honors the requested lifetime exactly.

findings.behavior: JWT claims: the user token is a JWT; the only claim the docs name is `sub`, from which the SDK derives the BLE handshake token ('The handshake token is automatically parsed from the JWT sub field'; Android NiceBuildSdk.resolveHandshakeToken(userJwt)). Refreshing the user token in the SDK (setUserAccessToken) 'automatically updates the handshake token and refreshes the RSA key pair'.
findings.notes: No `client_id` claim is documented. r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:118 says X-Client-Id is taken 'from the userAccessToken JWT client_id claim' (template source); docs say X-Client-Id is 'Your client_id, issued in the Portal' (openapi_transcription.json:148-153). Not contradictory, but the docs do not confirm such a claim exists.

findings.behavior: Transcription API does NOT use either token; it authenticates with two API-key headers: X-Client-Id (client_id) and X-Client-Api-Key (api_key). The api_key is explicitly 'NOT your client_secret' — generated in Portal under App Settings > API Keys.
findings.notes: Three credential kinds therefore exist: client_id+secret_key (Basic, backend only), user token (Bearer, mobile/SDK), client_id+api_key (headers, transcription).

findings.behavior: POST /open/partner/sdk/bind and /unbind: Bearer user token, JSON {type (required; derived from SN prefix: 881 -> 'notepro', 882 -> 'notepins'), sn (required)}; 200 -> {type, sn, is_bind}; bind is idempotent for the same owner; bind 403 {code, message:'device already bound to another account'} when bound elsewhere; 404 unknown SN. Unbind: idempotent, 404 unknown SN; must be paired with SDK depair(clear:true) so cloud and local state stay in sync. Devices bind to only one application at a time.
findings.notes: Binding is two-step: cloud bind (this API) then local BLE bind by the SDK which 'verifies and generates the key pair on-device' (openapi_binding.json:5). BLE-side details are FROZEN in docs/protocol-ledger.md; not re-derived here.

findings.behavior: GET /open/partner/sdk/binding?type=&sn= (Bearer user token) -> {is_bind: boolean|null, bind_history: string[]}. is_bind tri-state: true = bound to ANOTHER account (recovery impossible), false = unbound, null = 'signed but never bound'. bind_history = previously bound client IDs newest first, one entry per bind event so duplicates occur (de-duplicate before Device Recovery); includes bindings made in other apps. Unknown SN -> bare 404 with no error body. Used to drive SDK Device Recovery (recoveryConnectBleDevice) when cloud and local bind state diverge and the device locks.
findings.notes: 'signed but never bound' (null) implies a server-side sn-sign event precedes bind — consistent with r7's /sdk/sn-sign endpoint (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:91-97), which the public OpenAPI does not document.

findings.behavior: 3-step S3 multipart flow, Bearer user token. (1) POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls {filesize:int bytes (required), filetype:string (required, '"mp3" or "opus"')} -> {FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize (5242880), Parts:[{PartNumber (1-based), PresignedUrl}]}. (2) PUT raw bytes of each <=ChunkSize chunk directly to S3 (no auth) and read the ETag response header. (3) POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload {file_id, upload_id, part_list:[{PartNumber, ETag}] (all required), filetype (required), file_md5 (optional hex MD5)} -> {FileId, FileType, DownloadUrl (valid ~24 h), FileMd5}. Pass DownloadUrl as file_url to Transcription. The File Upload API is optional: Transcription accepts any publicly accessible audio URL.
findings.notes: Response keys are PascalCase (FileId, ChunkSize) while request keys are snake_case (file_id, part_list) — a naming split the docs preserve consistently. No max filesize and no error codes are documented for this API.

findings.behavior: POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ (trailing slash) with X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key, JSON {file_url (required; 'M4A, MP3, WAV'), params?: {transcribe?: {language: BCP-47 or 'auto', default 'auto'; detection_level: 'segment'|'chapter', default 'segment'; model (transcription-model.json only)}, vad?: {decode_silence: bool, default false}, diarization?: {enabled: bool default false; return_embedding: bool default false}, hotwords (transcription.json only): comma-separated custom vocabulary string}} -> {transcription_id:'task_exec_xxx', status:'PENDING', data:{}}. Limits (x-mint note on the submit op): Rate Limit 60 req/min, Max recording duration 24 hr, Max diarization 6 hr. Prose additionally says recordings exceeding 5 hours should be chunked.
findings.evidence: openapi_transcription.json:19-82, :24-26 (limits), :173-231 (request schema), :233-248; openapi_transcription-model.json:186-190 (model); api-reference_transcription-api_submit-audio-for-transcription.md:9; plaud-embedded_transcription-api-overview.md:52-82; plaud-embedded_devices.md:41 (5h max single-file recording on device)

findings.behavior: Model parameter: allowed names stated anywhere in the docs are plaud-fast-whisper (default in transcription-model.json; used in prose examples), plaud-omni-3, azure-fast-transcribe (both only in transcription-model.json description string), and plaud-transcribe-1 (only in the playground's curl body). The api-reference pages render transcription.json, which has NO model field at all.
findings.evidence: openapi_transcription-model.json:48, :186-190; plaud-embedded_transcription-api-overview.md:65; plaud-embedded_how-plaud-embedded-works.md:227; plaud-embedded_api-playground.md:44; grep of api-reference_*.md for 'model' returns nothing

findings.behavior: GET /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/{transcription_id} -> {transcription_id, status, data}. Status enum: PENDING, RECEIVED, STARTED, PROGRESS (in progress, keep polling); SUCCESS (data populated); FAILURE and REVOKED (terminal failures). data (on SUCCESS): {text, language, duration:int seconds, results:[segment]} and (transcription.json example only) embeddings: {"Speaker N": [256-dim float vector]} when return_embedding is true. Segment (schema TranscriptionSegment): start:number s, end:number s, text, speaker_id ('Speaker 1', present when diarization enabled), language ('en-US'), language_probabilitiy [sic, schema key misspelled] number 0-1 (example given as string '0.94'; the response example uses the correctly spelled language_probability with string '0.941').
findings.evidence: openapi_transcription.json:84-144, :116-137 (example incl. embeddings), :250-320 (schemas), :322-335 (status enum); openapi_transcription-model.json diff drops embeddings from the example; api-reference_transcription-api_get-transcription-task.md:61-68, :138-146
findings.notes: Status names are Celery task states verbatim (PENDING/RECEIVED/STARTED/PROGRESS/SUCCESS/FAILURE/REVOKED) and the id prefix is task_exec_, suggesting a Celery-backed task queue; inference only. No error body for FAILURE is documented; no 4xx codes are documented for the transcription API.

findings.behavior: Prose pages (transcription-api-overview, how-plaud-embedded-works) show a different SUCCESS payload: data.segments[] with {start, end, text, speaker} instead of data.results[] with speaker_id/language/language_probability and no embeddings.
findings.notes: Which shape the live API returns is UNKNOWN from docs alone; clients should tolerate both keys.

findings.behavior: OpenAPI servers: https://platform-us.plaud.ai/developer/api (US) and https://platform-jp.plaud.ai/developer/api (Japan) in all five specs. Data-retention page lists four public hosts: US platform-us (Default), Japan platform-jp, Europe platform-eu, Singapore platform-sg (the last three 'Contact Sales'). SDK init takes customDomain 'platform-us.plaud.ai' (domain only, no https://) and 'All SDK network requests use this domain'. CLI default api_base is the region-less https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api.
findings.evidence: openapi_auth.json:8-17 (same block in every spec); plaud-embedded_data-retention.md:41-52; plaud-embedded_auth-api-overview.md:76-80; plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:102-116; plaud-mcp-cli_cli.md:144-147

findings.behavior: Transcriptions processed by the API are retained 7 days by default (configurable on custom plans). Devices hold 64 GB local storage; builders may integrate devices only ('Full Data Custody': audio stays on device -> your app -> your services; app clears the device after sync) without sending audio to Plaud cloud. MCP HTTP mode: recording data passes through Plaud's US-hosted MCP server in transit only, not stored after the request.
findings.notes: Retention of the uploaded AUDIO in Plaud S3 (beyond the 24 h DownloadUrl validity) is not stated anywhere.

findings.behavior: PAYG along two meters: Connected Devices (max devices connected to your app in a month via the SDK) and Transcription Hours (hours transcribed via the API). Free tier per client: 50 connected devices + 300 transcription hours, the hours unlocked only after the first device connection. PAYG rates after free usage: $15 per device per month, $0.28 per transcription hour. Charged at end of month; payment failure -> 7-day grace period before service denial. PAYG has no device/transcription caps. Enterprise plans for HIPAA, volume discounts, dedicated support. Partner Program (bixgrow) for device-purchase tracking/incentives. End users need no Plaud App subscription.
findings.notes: Nothing states how a 'connected device' is counted technically (cloud bind vs BLE connect vs sn-sign) — the SDK-side signal Plaud bills on is UNKNOWN.

findings.behavior: Plaud Embedded supports only Note Pro (SN prefix 881, type 'notepro') and NotePin S (882, 'notepins'); Plaud Note and NotePin are NOT supported. Specs: Note Pro battery 30-50 h endurance, 4 MEMS + 1 VPU mics, dual-band Wi-Fi + BT, 64G, dual-mode calls+in-person; NotePin S 20 h, 2 MEMS, 64G, in-person. Max single-file recording duration 5 h on both.
findings.notes: The 5 h device cap plus the '>5 h should be chunked' transcription note versus the '24 hr max recording' x-mint limit are three different numbers describing overlapping constraints.

findings.behavior: MCP (@plaud-ai/mcp, Node>=20, OAuth browser login, tokens at ~/.plaud/tokens-mcp.json, local callback port 8199) tools: login, logout, get_current_user, list_files (query = case-insensitive keyword on name; date_from/date_to YYYY-MM-DD; page/page_size ignored when filters set), get_file, get_note (AI summary/action items/key topics), get_transcript (timestamps + speaker labels). Fields (list_files/get_file): id, name, created_at ISO8601, start_at ISO8601, duration (ms), serial_number. get_file-only: presigned_url (audio download, valid 24 h), source_list (transcript segments w/ timestamps+speakers), note_list (Markdown notes). Skills: plaud-browse/find/read/digest/followup/export. CLI (@plaud-ai/cli): login/logout/me; files (--page 1-1000, --page-size 10-100 default 20); recent [--days]; today; search <kw> [--from --to --max 50] = client-side case-insensitive keyword over recording names, scans up to 500 most recent; file/audio (24 h URL)/transcript/summary [-o]; version/update. plaud file adds start_at, serial_number, audio/transcript/summary availability booleans. Exit codes 0 ok, 1 args/unknown, 2 auth (AUTH_FAILED), 3 network, 4 timeout. Config ~/.plaud/cli.yaml {api_base default https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api, timeout 30000 ms}; env PLAUD_API_BASE, PLAUD_CLIENT_ID/PLAUD_CLI_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_CLIENT_SECRET, PLAUD_AUTH_URL, PLAUD_TOKEN_URL, PLAUD_REFRESH_URL. GA v1.0.0 on May 12 2026.
findings.notes: MCP/CLI are a personal-account (consumer) surface; their underlying HTTP endpoints are not documented. The api_base under /developer/api suggests they ride the developer platform host, not api.plaud.ai (r7 surface C).

findings.behavior: Plaud Embedded changelog: May 12 2026 v1.0.0 Developer Platform Beta Launch (iOS+Android SDK, starter app); May 18 2026 v1.0.5 MP3 export + WiFi fast transfer; Jun 29 2026 v1.0.6 live transfer speed, 0-100% export progress, batch download; Aug 3 2026 v1.0.11 Android SDK full parity (scan, connect, record, file list/sync/delete, settings, WiFi provisioning, fast transfer, OTA), MP3 over iOS WiFi; Aug 24 2026 v1.0.13 recoveryConnectBleDevice (reclaim device using historical user ID from bind history), connection-stage callbacks with failure reason, English-only SDK messages; Sep 14 2026 v1.0.14 'Workflow Query Deprecation — Deprecated workflow status and result query APIs on iOS and Android'. Advanced SDK pages: iOS 'PlaudWorkflowManager has been deprecated and will be removed in future SDK versions'; Android 'The workflow methods and models have been deprecated'.
findings.notes: This is the most plausible explanation for r7 surface A's /api/workflows/submit|status|result being in the SDK binary but absent from every documented API: the workflow surface is the SDK's own (deprecated) AI path, superseded by the documented /ai/transcriptions API. Note the changelog deprecates the status/result QUERY methods; it does not say submit is deprecated.

findings.behavior: The docs themselves acknowledge a second, undocumented '/api/...' service used by the SDK: (a) 'NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice(...) / unbindDevice(...) are not the cloud bind documented in the Android SDK reference. They post to a different service (/api/devices/bind) with a different credential. For the documented flow, call developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind directly with the user token.' (b) 'Android's firmware version check queries GET /api/sdk/latest-version with an Authorization header, while iOS uses the partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature.'
findings.notes: This is Plaud stating that surface A (/api/...) and surface B (/developer/api/open/partner/...) are different services with different credentials — bearing on r7's open question (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:130-137). It remains a claim; no runtime evidence.

findings.behavior: Four-party architecture: (1) partner backend services exchange client_id+client_secret for partner token and mint user tokens; (2) partner mobile app initializes the SDK with the user token + regional domain, binds device (cloud bind + BLE bind), syncs audio over BLE (default) or WiFi fast transfer (~10x faster); (3) Plaud device stores encrypted audio (64 GB), bound to exactly one app so stolen-device data stays inaccessible; (4) Plaud cloud: token issuance, device registry, optional S3 upload, transcription. Audio is synced 'from Plaud devices to your backend' and only the file_url is passed to Plaud cloud for transcription.
findings.notes: The docs put partner token minting on the partner backend; the playground and starter apps instead put the user token straight into the mobile app config (plaud-embedded_android-starter-app.md:68-78), so real deployments may skip the backend hop.

api_surface.name: POST /oauth/partner/access-token

api_surface.name: POST /oauth/partner/access-token/refresh
api_surface.signature_or_shape: auth: HTTP Basic base64(client_id:secret_key); Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; body form {refresh_token:string REQUIRED}; 200 PartnerTokenResponse (same shape, new access_token + refresh_token, expires_in example 3600)

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/users/access-token

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/sdk/bind
api_surface.signature_or_shape: auth: Bearer <user_access_token>; Content-Type: application/json; body DeviceRef {type:string REQUIRED ('notepro'|'notepins' by SN prefix 881/882), sn:string REQUIRED}; 200 BindResponse {type, sn, is_bind:boolean(true)}; 403 Error {code:int(403), message:'device already bound to another account'}; 404 unknown SN (no body)

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/sdk/unbind

api_surface.name: GET /open/partner/sdk/binding

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls

api_surface.name: PUT <PresignedUrl> (AWS S3, not a Plaud endpoint)

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload

api_surface.name: POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/
api_surface.signature_or_shape: auth: headers X-Client-Id + X-Client-Api-Key; Content-Type: application/json; body TranscriptionRequest {file_url:string REQUIRED (M4A, MP3, WAV; any publicly accessible URL), params?: {transcribe?: {language:string default 'auto' (BCP-47 e.g. en-US, zh-CN), detection_level:string default 'segment' ('segment'|'chapter'), model?:string default 'plaud-fast-whisper' ['plaud-fast-whisper','plaud-omni-3','azure-fast-transcribe'] (transcription-model.json only; playground uses 'plaud-transcribe-1')}, vad?: {decode_silence:bool default false}, diarization?: {enabled:bool default false, return_embedding:bool default false}, hotwords?:string comma-separated (transcription.json only)}}; 200 TranscriptionCreatedResponse {transcription_id:string 'task_exec_xxx', status:TranscriptionStatus ('PENDING'), data:{}}; limits: 60 req/min, max recording 24 hr, max diarization 6 hr

doc_vs_code_contradictions: WORKFLOWS: r7 surface A lists POST /api/workflows/submit, GET /api/workflows/{id}/status, GET /api/workflows/{id}/result in the SDK jar (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:78-81) and surface D says python-plaud-ai's workflows/* 'mirrors docs.plaud.ai' (:164). The docs fetched 2026-09-23 contain NO workflows endpoint anywhere; the only documented AI surface is /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ with X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key (openapi_transcription.json:19-144). The changelog v1.0.14 Sep 14 2026 'Deprecated workflow status and result query APIs on iOS and Android' (plaud-embedded_changelog.md:7-11) and the advanced pages ('PlaudWorkflowManager has been deprecated', plaud-embedded_advanced-ios-sdk.md:64; 'workflow methods and models ... deprecated', plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:64) indicate the binary's workflow surface is a superseded SDK path. Both sides reported; r7's characterization of D as 'the documented form' is not supported by the current docs (may reflect an older doc version).

DEFAULT HOST: r7 records the SDK ServerEnvironment default US_PROD = https://platform-jp.plaud.ai with alternates platform.plaud.cn, dev-api-us-test.plaud.work, platform-beta.plaud.ai (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:19). Docs state US = platform-us.plaud.ai is the default region and JP = platform-jp.plaud.ai (plaud-embedded_data-retention.md:47-50; openapi_*.json:8-17); the SDK docs tell integrators to pass customDomain 'platform-us.plaud.ai' (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:104). The SDK enum (per r7) contains no platform-us, platform-eu or platform-sg host and the docs list no .cn, beta or dev-test host.

BIND ENDPOINT FAMILY: r7 lists POST /api/devices/bind|unbind (Bearer api_token, BYTECODE_PROVEN) and asks whether /api/... aliases the partner API (r7:73-76, :130-137). Docs: bind is POST /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind with Bearer user token (openapi_binding.json:24-80), AND Plaud's own note states 'NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice(...)/unbindDevice(...) are not the cloud bind ... They post to a different service (/api/devices/bind) with a different credential' (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:440-442). Docs thus claim the two are distinct services — an OFFICIAL_DOC claim, not runtime proof; r7's UNKNOWN stands at runtime level.

VERSION CHECK: r7 lists GET /api/sdk/latest-version (binary, Bearer) and GET .../partner/sdk/version/latest (template, Bearer user token) (r7:83-86, :124). Docs: 'Android's firmware version check queries GET /api/sdk/latest-version with an Authorization header, while iOS uses the partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature' (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:274-276). Docs add a platform split and an X-Device-Signature auth on the iOS partner path that r7 attributes only to /partner/sdk/metadata (r7:111-114); neither version endpoint appears in the public OpenAPI.

UPLOAD PATHS: r7 binary uses POST /api/files/upload-s3/generate-presigned-urls and complete-upload with Bearer api_token (r7:60-66); docs document only /developer/api/open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls and complete-upload with Bearer user token (openapi_file.json:19-139). Same class-name (GeneratePresignedUrlsRequest) but different path prefix and credential; docs give the JSON field names r7 could not decompile (filesize, filetype, FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize, Parts, file_id, upload_id, part_list, file_md5).

TOKEN CHAIN: r7 surface A is a 3-hop chain /api/oauth/sdk-token (Bearer Base64(appKey:appSecret)) -> /api/sdk/api-token -> api_token (r7:34-51); surface D uses POST platform.plaud.ai/api/oauth/api-token (r7:164). Docs document a different 2-hop chain: Basic base64(client_id:secret_key) -> /developer/api/oauth/partner/access-token (with refresh) -> /developer/api/open/partner/users/access-token (openapi_auth.json). None of /api/oauth/sdk-token, /api/sdk/api-token, /api/oauth/api-token appear in the docs.

UNDOCUMENTED PARTNER ENDPOINTS: r7 surface B has POST .../partner/sdk/sn-sign, sn-verify, gen-key (returns RSA private key), metadata (X-Device-Signature) (r7:91-114). The public OpenAPI (openapi_binding.json) documents only bind/unbind/binding. The SDK prose pages do reference sn-sign, RSA key-pair generation and PartnerApiManager (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:59, :338, :401, :430-437), and binding's is_bind=null 'signed but never bound' presupposes sn-sign, so the docs corroborate their existence without contracting them.

X-CLIENT-ID SOURCE: r7 says X-Client-Id is 'from the userAccessToken JWT client_id claim' (r7:118, template code). Docs say X-Client-Id is 'Your client_id, issued in the Portal' (openapi_transcription.json:148-153) and the only JWT claim they name is sub (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:109; plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:139). Not contradictory, but the client_id claim is unconfirmed by docs.

CONSUMER SURFACE C vs MCP/CLI: r7 surface C is https://api.plaud.ai (community clients) (r7:21, :139-160). The official CLI's default api_base is https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api (plaud-mcp-cli_cli.md:145) — Plaud's own personal-data tools ride the developer-platform host, not api.plaud.ai. Which backend serves MCP/CLI data is otherwise undocumented.

DOC-INTERNAL (not code): transcription.json vs transcription-model.json differ in model (absent vs present with plaud-fast-whisper/plaud-omni-3/azure-fast-transcribe), hotwords (present vs absent), embeddings example (present vs absent), x-mint limits note (present vs absent), return_embedding example (true vs false) — diff at openapi_transcription.json:24-26, :50, :57-59, :132-136, :192, :224-227; playground uses model plaud-transcribe-1 (plaud-embedded_api-playground.md:44), a name in no spec.

DOC-INTERNAL: SUCCESS payload shape — OpenAPI data.results[].{speaker_id,language,language_probability}+embeddings (openapi_transcription.json:116-137) vs prose data.segments[].{speaker} (plaud-embedded_transcription-api-overview.md:102-108; plaud-embedded_how-plaud-embedded-works.md:254-260).

DOC-INTERNAL: accepted audio formats — file upload filetype '"mp3" or "opus"' (openapi_file.json:172) vs transcription file_url '(M4A, MP3, WAV)' (openapi_transcription.json:179); duration limits 24 hr max recording (openapi_transcription.json:25) vs 'exceeding 5 hours should be broken into chunks' (plaud-embedded_transcription-api-overview.md:81) vs device 5 h single-file max (plaud-embedded_devices.md:41).
unexplained_behaviors: Whether the requested user-token expires_in is honored verbatim, capped, or has a maximum; and whether user tokens can be refreshed at all (no refresh_token in UserTokenResponse, openapi_auth.json:229-247).
The partner refresh_token lifetime and whether refresh rotates the refresh_token (example shows a refresh_token in the refresh response, openapi_auth.json:96-101).

What exactly increments the billable 'Connected Devices' meter (cloud bind, BLE connect, sn-sign, or first sync) — the docs define it only as 'devices ... connected to via the Embedded SDK' (plaud-embedded_billing.md:13, :17-19).
How is_bind becomes null ('signed but never bound', openapi_binding.json:243) — implies /sdk/sn-sign writes to the registry, but sn-sign is not in the public spec.
Whether plaud-transcribe-1 (playground) is an alias of plaud-fast-whisper, a newer model, or invalid against the enum in transcription-model.json.

Whether 'hotwords' (transcription.json only) and 'model' (transcription-model.json only) can be sent together; the specs are two snapshots of one endpoint with no version marker (both info.version 0.0.1).
Retention of uploaded AUDIO in Plaud S3 after the 24 h DownloadUrl expires (only transcription results have a stated 7-day retention).
Whether FAILURE/REVOKED carry an error message/code in data; no error schema is documented for the transcription or file APIs.
Whether the POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ trailing slash is significant (every doc sample includes it; the GET has none).
Which underlying HTTP API the MCP/CLI tools call and why their default api_base (platform.plaud.ai/developer/api) is region-less while every partner spec is region-prefixed.
Whether the 'Workflow Query Deprecation' (Sep 14 2026) also removes /api/workflows/submit or only the status/result queries; the changelog names only the query APIs.

The dangling anchor auth-api-overview#find-your-region (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:115) — a 'Find your region' section appears to have been removed or never published, so the official regional-host discovery step is missing.

docs-android-sdk.summary: The Android Embedded SDK product surface, as Plaud documents it, is a three-tier stack: the static Kotlin `object` facade `sdk.PlaudDeviceAgent` (init, scan, connect/recovery-connect, depair, getState, getFileList, exportAudio, WiFi session lifecycle, three-call OTA) driven by one global `PlaudDeviceAgentListener` (32 members, 0 required; ~24 BLE callbacks + 7 WiFi auto-sync callbacks + bleConnectStage), plus `IWifiTransferAgent` (file list / batch download / batch delete, 12-member all-required `WifiTransferCallback`, `WifiConnectionState` NONE→CONNECTING→CONNECTED→HANDSHAKING→READY), over the low-level `IBleAgent` (165 methods via `TntAgent.getInstant().bleAgent`, OnRequest/OnResponse pairs, `BleAgentListener` 29 members/27 required), `NiceBuildSdk` (partner-data readiness, SN signing, RSA private key access) and `PartnerApiManager` (gen-key / sn-sign / metadata). Documented invariants: one app per device at a time; 5 h max per recording; bleConnectState 1=GATT-up-not-success/0/2; bleBind(status==0) is the real success; recovery only when cloud `is_bind` is not true, driven per deduped `bind_history` id via `recoveryConnectBleDevice` (force-clear) → depair(false) → rescan (MAC changes) → reconnect; SN signature is memory-only and needs a live sn-sign every launch; RSA key pair persisted in Keystore; export formats PCM/WAV/OPUS/MP3 with ExportStage DOWNLOADING→TRANSCODING; OTA phases TRANSFERRING/TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING/DEVICE_RESTARTING/UPGRADE_COMPLETE/TRANSFER_FAILED/UPGRADE_FAILED and firmware updates wipe recordings; permissions BLUETOOTH_SCAN/CONNECT + fine/coarse location on API 31+ (BLUETOOTH/BLUETOOTH_ADMIN + location on ≤30). Every one of the 21 CommonType wire settings in ledger §5.12 has a documented IBleAgent get/set pair except WIFI_CHANNEL (only reachable via the generic getCommonParams/setCommonParams/commonSettings channel); no value ranges are documented for any setting. `refreshRecordState` and `getSnSignature` appear nowhere in the fetched docs; `X-Device-Signature` appears only as an iOS aside (Android firmware check uses `Authorization` on `GET /api/sdk/latest-version`). Principal doc-vs-code tensions: docs present `bleBind.protVersion` as a protocol version while §14 run 4 proves it (and `timezone`) are loaded from the l3 timezone byte; docs describe bind as an "encrypted handshake [that] generates the key-pair on the device" while §4.4/4.5/4.6 show no BLE bind message, a cloud-issued RSA pair (private key returned by gen-key) and a cleartext token-only legacy path below advertised portVersion 20; docs say recovery's force-clear "wipes stale key material" while R7-S12 shows isForceClear only selects the 0xFE20 marker, inert below pv 20, with the FE20 device effect UNKNOWN (U10); the docs' listener table omits `bleTimeSync(timezone, stamp)` which ledger §5.2 names; `WifiFileInfo` claims fileName/duration/timestamp that the recovered Wi-Fi GetFileList record (§7: sessionId/fileSize/u16 scene) does not carry.

findings.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK(context, userAccessToken, customDomain) initialises the singleton; customDomain is 'domain only, no https://' and 'All SDK network requests use this domain'; initSDK 'fetches the key pair asynchronously' (gen-key) so callers must poll NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() before connecting.
findings.notes: Ledger §4.5 / r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:97-103 agree the RSA pair comes from POST /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/gen-key and that isPartnerDataReady gates connect (BYTECODE_PROVEN path, CLOUD_OBSERVED endpoint).

findings.behavior: sdk.permission.PermissionManager requests BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION on API 31+, and BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_ADMIN, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION on API ≤ 30; 'it asks for location on Android 12+ as well'. onResult receives true only when every requested permission was granted.
findings.notes: Starter app page says location is needed only 'on Android 11 and below' (plaud-embedded_android-starter-app.md:227) — internal doc inconsistency.

findings.behavior: Binding is documented as two steps: (1) 'Local bind over BLE, where the Embedded SDK runs the encrypted handshake and generates the key-pair on the device'; (2) 'Cloud bind' via POST https://<domain>/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind {type, sn} with Bearer user token, called by the app after bleBind(status=0); 403 = already bound to another account; re-bind to same owner is idempotent. Preconditions for connectBleDevice: RSA key pair arrived AND SN signed via NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn), read 'during the pre-handshake'.
findings.notes: CONTRADICTS ledger §4.4 ('There is no BLE bind message'; bleBind fires from btStatusChange(CONNECTED) ← sync_time success), §4.5 (key pair is cloud-issued incl. private key; SDK never calls KeyPairGenerator) and §4.6 (below advertised portVersion 20 there is no encryption and no signature — token only). Both sides reported in doc_vs_code_contradictions.

findings.behavior: bleConnectState(state): 1 = GATT link up, handshake still pending (explicitly 'not connection success'); 0 = disconnected; 2 = connection failed. bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone): 'status == 0 is the real connection success'. blePenState(state, privacy, keyState, uDisk) reported after the handshake.
findings.notes: Ledger §14 (run 4) proves protVersion and timezone are both loaded from the l3 timezone byte; the docs do not caveat this.

findings.behavior: bleConnectStage(sn: String?, stage: String, detail: String?) is 'the only way to see which layer refused a rejected connection'; sn may be null before SN known. stage ∈ {start, gatt_connect, set_notify, set_battery_notify, read_battery, set_data_notify, pre_handshake, send_rsa_public, first_handshake, two_handshake, handshake_get_ssn, change_handshake_timeout, sync_time}; detail ∈ {ok, old_protocol_ok, status_<n> (status_1 = token mismatch), sn_signature_empty, sn_signature_invalid, user_rsa_public_key_empty, bind_token_empty, send_fail}. Before SDK 1.0.13 all collapsed into bleConnectState(2); 1.0.13 forwards it through the facade.
findings.notes: Stage list matches ledger §4.1 (DIRECT) exactly. old_protocol_ok is the legacy (pv<20) path label observed live in §14 runs 1/3/4; docs list it without explaining that an unencrypted path exists.

findings.behavior: 'Plaud devices can only be bound to one application at a time (tied to your Partner Token).' Unbind before uninstalling; otherwise the device cannot be bound to another app or the Plaud app.
findings.notes: Cloud-side policy claim; not testable from bytecode. Ledger §4.6 notes the device decides token acceptance.

findings.behavior: Standard unbind = cloud POST sdk/unbind (idempotent no-op if already unbound, no BLE needed) + BLE depair(clear=false) → bleDepair(status) (0 = depaired) → disconnect(). 'Because an out-of-range or unresponsive device never answers, pair the callback with a short timeout that disconnects anyway' (sample: 3 000 ms). clear=true 'also clears the SDK's stored connection/bond state'; keep false during recovery. No-arg depair() is equivalent to depair(false).
findings.notes: Ledger has no depair wire message recorded; 'depair changes the MAC — rescan' (android-sdk.md:423) has no bytecode counterpart (see unexplained).

findings.behavior: Device Recovery applies when cloud and local bind state are out-of-sync ('on Android this usually surfaces as a bleConnectState(2) connect failure after a ~10s timeout'). Only when GET sdk/binding reports is_bind false or null (true = owned by another account, SDK cannot override). bind_history = client IDs newest first, one entry per bind event ('50+ duplicates of a single ID is normal' — dedupe). For each id: recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice, historicalUserId) 'uses that ID as the handshake token and connects with force-clear, so the firmware wipes its stale key material'; current user's SN signature and RSA material are reused; SDK 'restores the current user's handshake identity when the attempt ends'. On bleBind(status==0) → depair(false) → bleDepair → disconnect() + startScan() ('depair changes the MAC — rescan') → connectBleDevice(fresh) as current user. bleConnectState 0/2 while awaiting handshake = id refused, try next. historicalUserId 'Accepts either the raw client_user_id or its 32-hex form'.
findings.notes: Compare ledger §14 / r7-s12: SDK normalises by removePrefix('client_user_') + drop '-', aborts on empty (bleConnectState(2)), warns if length≠32, passes isForceClear=true which only selects 0xFE20 (inert below pv 20, observed); FE20 device effect is UNKNOWN (U10). Doc code comment at :417 ('if (status != 0) return // this ID matched the firmware lock') reads inverted relative to :245 ('0 = handshake complete').

findings.behavior: 'Plaud devices will record up to 5 hours. Recordings longer should be broken up.' getFileList() → bleFileList(List<BleFile>). exportAudio(sessionId, outputDir, format: AudioExportFormat {PCM|WAV|OPUS|MP3}, channels: Int (1=mono, optional overload), callback: AudioExporter.ExportCallback). MP3 recommended ('accepted directly by the transcription upload API'). ExportCallback: onProgress(progress 0-100 'download bytes', message), onComplete(outputFile), onError(error), optional onStageChanged(ExportStage DOWNLOADING → TRANSCODING). Facade handles 'download, caching, E2EE decrypt, and transcode'. Callbacks arrive on SDK internal threads, not main.
findings.notes: Ledger §8: chain syncFile → t7.d() → o4 pass-through → AudioExporter, sniff-based (PLAUD.AI header ≥512 B → ChaCha decrypt; 'OggS' → Ogg). 5 h limit has no bytecode counterpart.

findings.behavior: ~10x faster than BLE. setDeviceWiFi(open=true) → bleWiFiOpen(status, ssid, password, url) → startWifiTransfer(userId, WifiTransferCallback): Boolean (false if session could not open) → state NONE → CONNECTING → CONNECTED → HANDSHAKING → READY; 'No file command works before READY' → getWifiAgent()?.getFileList() → onFileListReceived(List<WifiFileInfo>) → exportAudioViaWiFi(same args as exportAudio, same ExportCallback) → endWiFiTransfer() (only this also closes the hotspot over BLE; stopWifiTransfer() leaves hotspot open draining battery). getWifiAgent() is null until an agent exists. isWifiTransferActive() checks session. deleteFiles(List<Long>) is 'the only batch delete in the SDK' → onFileDeleteCompleted. downloadFile()/downloadAllFiles() 'write undecrypted .opus bytes straight to disk'. onTransferProgress(sessionId, progress 0-100, speed KB/s).
findings.notes: Ledger §7 (SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT IMPLEMENTED): pen raises WPA2 SoftAP (SSID 'PLAUD'+last4 SN, pass = last 8 SN chars), phone runs WebSocket server on 8081, pen dials in; opcode 10 OpenWiFi / 13 CloseWiFi on BLE side. WifiFileInfo fields (fileName/duration/timestamp) exceed the recovered 10-byte GetFileList record [sessionId][fileSize][u16 scene].

findings.behavior: Three calls: checkFirmwareUpdate(cb) → downloadFirmware(info, cb) → installFirmware(file, info, cb); flow 'version query → download → MD5 verify → CRC → BLE packet push → device restart → reconnect'. FirmwareUpdateInfo{hasUpdate, currentVersion, isForceUpdate, versionResponse: DeviceVersionResponse(latest version, download URL, MD5, release notes)}. UpdateProgress{progress 0-100, message, detail, transferPhase: FirmwareTransferPhase}. FirmwareTransferPhase ∈ {TRANSFERRING, TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING, DEVICE_RESTARTING, UPGRADE_COMPLETE, TRANSFER_FAILED, UPGRADE_FAILED}. FirmwareDownloadResult{success, file, md5Valid, error}; FirmwareInstallResult{success, error}. SimpleFirmwareUpdateCallback has empty defaults. 'Firmware updates will wipe recordings.' Android version check = GET /api/sdk/latest-version with Authorization header (iOS: partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature). Low-level: appFotaPush(filePath, fromVersion, toVersion, thirdVersion, otaPushListener), isFotaPushing(), interruptFotaPush(), getSyncOtaFileInfo(), appGetThirdVersion(); FirmwareUpdateManager composes the flow.
findings.notes: Closure report: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (0x1021, init 0xFFFF) for the OTA whole-file path (BYTECODE_PROVEN); latest-version endpoint CLOUD_OBSERVED (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:83).

findings.behavior: gen-key and sn-sign are POST …/sdk/gen-key and …/sdk/sn-sign with 'Authorization: Bearer <user token>', driven by PartnerApiManager.generateRsaKeyPair / signDeviceSn. deviceType from SN prefix: 881 → notepro, 882 → notepins. 'The SN signature is stored in memory only — there is no Keystore-backed cache and no persistence across process death. Every fresh launch needs a live sn-sign call before its first connect, so the device requires network reachability at that moment.' RSA key pair IS persisted, 'wrapped by an AES master key in the Android Keystore, and is what feeds audio E2EE decryption'; NiceBuildSdk.getSecurePrivateKey() returns PEM; clearPartnerData() drops it. handshakeToken = user JWT 'sub' claim via NiceBuildSdk.resolveHandshakeToken(userJwt).
findings.notes: Ledger §4.5 (DIRECT): gen-key returns public_key AND private_key PEM; sn-sign opaque base64; token 32 hex with pad/truncate. Consistent. §4.3: private keys parsed as PKCS#8 PEM.

findings.behavior: IBleAgent = TntAgent.getInstant().bleAgent, 165 methods; every command takes AgentCallback.OnRequest{onRequestResult(success, code, msg)} + AgentCallback.OnResponse<T>{onResponse(rsp)}; 'OnRequest fires when the command is written to the device; OnResponse fires when the device answers. A successful OnRequest with no OnResponse means the device accepted the command but never replied.' BleAgentListener registered via TntAgent.getInstant().addBleAgentListeners/removeBleAgentListeners; 29 members, 27 required. workflow methods/models deprecated. NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice/unbindDevice post to /api/devices/bind with a different credential and are NOT the documented cloud bind.
findings.notes: Ledger §4.4: 'The unrelated cloud bind (POST /api/devices/bind) is never called by the SDK' — consistent (exists, unused internally). Closure report: no transport ACK, application responses serve as protocol responses — consistent with the OnRequest/OnResponse semantics.

findings.behavior: Device settings are exposed only on IBleAgent as get/set pairs: BackLightTime, BackLightBrightness, Language, RecScene, RecMode, openVAD, VadSensitivity, VpuGain, MICGain, VpuCLK, BatteryMode, getAudioChannel, isOggAudio, isNoNsAgc, AutoRecord, AutoStopRecord, AutoPowerOff, AutoSync, AutoDeleteRecordFile, SaveRAWFile, FindMyState, IBeaconWakeup, SwitchHandlerId, BleDeviceName, LedStatus, AlarmRec, setPrivacy, setActive, restoreFactorySettings, plus generic getCommonParams/setCommonParams/commonSettings. No value ranges, units or defaults are documented for any setting. Facade surfaces only bleMicGain(gain) and bleDeviceName(name) callbacks.
findings.notes: Mapping to ledger §5.12 CommonType wire values given in api_surface (20 of 21 names correspond; WIFI_CHANNEL has no dedicated documented method). Ledger: which values real firmware reports is UNKNOWN (U22); emulator values are POLICY.

findings.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent documents no start/stop recording method; recording control is IBleAgent only: startRecord(scene, …), stopRecord, recordPause(sessionId, …), recordResume(sessionId, …), startImmediateRecord, stopImmediateRecord, startSyncRecord. The facade re-emits bleRecordStart(sessionId, start, status, scene, startTime, reason), bleRecordStop(sessionId, reason, fileExist, fileSize), bleRecordPause(same), bleRecordResume(sessionId, start, status, scene, startTime).
findings.notes: refreshRecordState is not documented anywhere in the fetched Android (or iOS) docs.

findings.behavior: getRecSessions(startSessionId: Long — 0 lists everything), syncFileStart(sessionId, start: Long (0 = whole file / resume offset), end: Long (0 = to end of file), onRequest, onHeadRsp, onTailRsp, voiceDataCollector: ISyncVoiceDataKeepOut built with VoiceDataCreatorFactory.newOriginalData()), syncFileStop, syncFileDel(sessionId), clearRecordFile, fileDataCheck. 'There is no format conversion and no decryption at this layer.'
findings.notes: Matches ledger §5.6 (opcode 26; startSessionId stored but never read — U5) and §5.8 (y6 = session/start/end; end inclusivity & 0=EOF are U14). Docs assert '0 transfers to the end of the file' which the ledger holds UNKNOWN from static evidence.

findings.behavior: Starter app: minSdk 21, compileSdk 34, JDK 17, physical arm64-v8a/armeabi-v7a device only; local.properties keys PLAUD_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN (required), PLAUD_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_API_KEY (transcription only); default namespace/applicationId com.plaud.template; Play Store requires compileSdk 35; bump versionCode every upload; $25 one-time Play fee; Bluetooth permission declaration (+ location on Android 11 and below).
findings.notes: Product/packaging constraints, not protocol.

api_surface.semantics: Results on bleScanResult (accumulated list); maps to IBleAgent.scanBle(true)

api_surface.semantics: Clears ownership lock on device; result on bleDepair(status); clear=true also clears SDK stored connection/bond state; keep false during recovery; maps to IBleAgent.depair(clear, onRequest, onResponse)

doc_vs_code_contradictions: bleBind.protVersion: DOC (android-sdk.md:244,283,827) presents bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone) with protVersion as a protocol-version parameter and no caveat. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §14 lines 1468-1475, run 4; final-closure-report.md:143-147, RUNTIME_PROVEN): the facade passes status=0 literally and loads BOTH protVersion and timezone from q.n = the l3 timezone byte (offset 6), not from l3 portVersion; setting emulator l3 tz=5 produced bleBind protVersion=5 tz=5. The true port version is never surfaced through bleBind.

Meaning of 'local bind': DOC (android-sdk.md:180) 'Local bind over BLE, where the Embedded SDK runs the encrypted handshake and generates the key-pair on the device'; (android-sdk.md:176) 'Binding a Plaud device generates a key-pair using the user token'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.4 lines 341-349, SOURCE-DERIVED): 'There is no BLE bind message'; bleBind fires from btStatusChange(CONNECTED) ← sync_time success, gated on handshake status 0 + opcode-9 battery (pv≥5) + syncTime, with SYNC_TIME_FAIL (-8) if the last never lands. §4.5 (DIRECT): the RSA key pair is issued by POST …/sdk/gen-key (public AND private key PEM); 'The SDK never calls KeyPairGenerator for this'. Nothing is generated on the device.

Encryption is unconditional in the docs but portVersion-gated in code: DOC (android-sdk.md:176-180; advanced-android-sdk.md:328 lists old_protocol_ok without explanation) implies every connect runs the encrypted handshake. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.2, §4.6 lines 266-276, 362-390; §14 lines 1462-1466): only advertised portVersion ≥ 20 runs the RSA pre-handshake and sealed channel; below 20, q.b0 goes straight to first_handshake whose only precondition is a non-empty token, no signature, no key, no cryptography (RUNTIME_PROVEN against the emulator at pv 7: 'old_protocol_ok → sync_time → bind 0').

Recovery force-clear semantics: DOC (android-sdk.md:409) 'connects with force-clear, so the firmware wipes its stale key material'; (android-sdk.md:350) 'the recovery handshake has already force-cleared the device's key material'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §2 lines 180-206, §9 U10, §14 lines 1465-1466; r7/r7-s12-k3-runtime-capture.md:36-48): isForceClear only selects marker 0xFE20 (PRE_HANDSHAKE_AND_CLEAR) vs 0xFE10, consumed by the pre-handshake; 'isForceClear is inert below portVersion 20 (predicted; observed)' — no marker frame was written; 'The meaning of isForceClear (0xFE20 vs 0xFE10)' is UNKNOWN (U10), settled only by hardware. The wipe claim is a doc assertion with no bytecode/runtime counterpart.

Recovery token handling: DOC (android-sdk.md:444) historicalUserId 'Accepts either the raw client_user_id or its 32-hex form'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §14 runs 1-3 lines 1446-1453; r7-s12 write-up lines 36-42): the SDK strips prefix 'client_user_' and '-', aborts with bleConnectState(2) on empty, warns when length ≠ 32 ('lower layer pads with zeros / truncates'), then k3 right-pads with '0' to 32 (pv≥9) or 16 chars — run 3 silently TRUNCATED a 32-char id to 16 at pv 7. Also DOC (android-sdk.md:409) says 'nothing has to be signed for the historical user' and the SDK 'restores the current user's handshake identity' — the ledger confirms no cloud call on this path (t3.a with no resolveHandshakeToken) but records nothing about an identity-restore step.

Recovery sample-code comment inversion (doc-internal): android-sdk.md:417 'if (status != 0) return // this ID matched the firmware lock' vs :245 '0 = handshake complete' and :417 flow (status==0 → depair). The comment labels the non-zero branch as the match while the code treats status==0 as the match.

PlaudDeviceAgentListener enumeration: DOC (android-sdk.md:822-851; advanced-android-sdk.md:290 '32 members') lists 24 table callbacks + 7 onWifiSync* + bleConnectStage = 32 and never mentions a time-sync callback. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §5.2 lines 469-472, DIRECT): syncTime$1.onCallback forwards n7.c() as the first argument of PlaudDeviceAgentListener.bleTimeSync(timezone, stamp). Either the docs' 32 count omits bleTimeSync or one listed member is not a listener member.

WifiFileInfo metadata: DOC (android-sdk.md:931) WifiFileInfo carries sessionId, fileName, fileSize, duration (ms), timestamp (epoch seconds), scene. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §7 lines 1075-1080, SOURCE-DERIVED): Wi-Fi GetFileList (type 11) returns JSON {uid,status,count,offset} plus 10-byte records [u32le sessionId][u32le fileSize][u16le scene] — no fileName, duration or timestamp on the wire. Those fields must be derived client-side or come from an unrecovered field; the doc's 'more per-file metadata than BleFile' is not supported by the recovered record layout.

bleData payload: DOC (android-sdk.md:842) 'A chunk of streaming audio/PCM bytes'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §8 / final-closure-report.md Audio): o4 is a pure pass-through, so DATA payloads equal the stored file byte-for-byte (Opus/Ogg, possibly PLAUD.AI-encrypted) — not PCM; PCM only exists after AudioExporter transcode.

syncFileStart end=0 semantics: DOC (advanced-android-sdk.md:252-254) 'End byte offset. 0 transfers to the end of the file.' CODE (protocol-ledger.md §9 U14): 'Whether y6's end is inclusive or exclusive, and whether 0 formally means EOF' is UNKNOWN — no shipped code sends a non-zero end and no capture exists. The doc statement is a claim the record cannot confirm.

downloadFile output shape: DOC (android-sdk.md:604) IWifiTransferAgent.downloadFile/downloadAllFiles 'write undecrypted .opus bytes straight to disk'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §9 U20; final-closure-report.md Audio): which of {plain, PLAUD.AI-encrypted} × {Ogg, raw Opus} real firmware emits is UNKNOWN; selection is sniff-based at export time. The doc asserts both 'undecrypted' and '.opus' as fixed.

Locked-device timeout: DOC (android-sdk.md:357) 'bleConnectState(2) connect failure after a ~10s timeout'. CODE: the ledger records no 10 s connect/handshake timeout constant (only change_handshake_timeout as a stage name §4.1, 'retried a few times' §4.4, and the 5 000 ms file-sync stall timeout §5.8/5.9). Unverified rather than contradicted.

Bind-to-one-app enforcement locus: DOC (android-sdk.md:298; android-starter-app.md:141) 'can only be bound to one application at a time (tied to your Partner Token)'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.6): on the legacy path 'the host sends a token, and the DEVICE returns a status. The secret belongs to the device'; R7-S12 emulator accepted any token as HARNESS POLICY. Whether real firmware enforces a single-owner lock (status_1) is DEVICE_REQUIRED (no contradiction, but the docs' cloud-tied framing is not what the bytecode shows — the device-side check is local).
unexplained_behaviors: 'depair changes the MAC — rescan' (android-sdk.md:423): no depair wire message, and no MAC-rotation behaviour, is recorded in protocol-ledger.md or the closure report; DEVICE_REQUIRED.
'~10x faster than BLE' (android-sdk.md:522) and 'up to 5 hours' per recording (android-sdk.md:465): no bytecode or runtime counterpart; product claims only.

Transfer-speed reporting on BLE: plaud-embedded_changelog.md:35-37 announces 'Live download speed reporting for WiFi fast transfer and BLE transfers', but the Android AudioExporter.ExportCallback (android-sdk.md:874-888) exposes no speed argument; only WifiTransferCallback.onTransferProgress carries speed (KB/s). Where BLE speed surfaces on Android is undocumented (possibly the onProgress `message` string).
WifiTransferCallback.onError(code, message) and AgentCallback.OnRequest code: no error-code table is documented anywhere in the three files.

Setting value ranges: none of the 21 CommonType settings (nor LED/alarm/name/privacy) has a documented range, unit or default; ledger §5.12 likewise marks real-firmware values UNKNOWN (U22) — the emulator's DEFAULT_COMMON_SETTINGS are POLICY.
WIFI_CHANNEL (wire 21) has no dedicated IBleAgent get/set method in the docs' settings list; presumably only reachable via getCommonParams/setCommonParams/commonSettings.
PlaudDeviceAgent.deleteFile(...) is implied by the bleDeleteFile description (android-sdk.md:845) but its signature is never given.

The seven onWifiSync* listener callbacks (android-sdk.md:850) have no documented signatures and no documented triggering methods on PlaudDeviceAgent (IBleAgent's getWifiList/getWifiInfo/setSyncWifi/deleteWifiInfo/testWifiInfo/testWifiResult at advanced-android-sdk.md:220-221 are the likely drivers).
Permission scope inconsistency between pages: android-sdk.md:169 says location is requested on Android 12+ as well; android-starter-app.md:227 says location is needed only on Android 11 and below.

'The SDK restores the current user's handshake identity when the attempt ends' (android-sdk.md:409): no corresponding step is identified in the ledger's recovery trace (r7-s12 lines 36-42 end at t3.a(...)).

ADV:341 claims bleConnectStage has been 'a default-bodied member of BleAgentListener since the first public release' while ADV:289 counts 27 of 29 members required and ADV:315 marks commonSettingNotify as the (only named) default — the second default member is not named.
IBleAgent 'exposes 165 methods' (advanced-android-sdk.md:80) — not verified against the AAR here; the docs list ~110 by name.

refreshRecordState and getSnSignature (named in the task) do not appear in any fetched doc; X-Device-Signature appears only as an iOS aside (advanced-android-sdk.md:275) and in r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:112 for POST …/sdk/metadata (computation site UNKNOWN). The Android PartnerApiManager.postDeviceMetadata(signature, request) takes the signature as a caller-supplied string, so how an Android app obtains it is undocumented.

docs-wrappers-web.source_cluster: OFFICIAL_DOC (docs.plaud.ai plaud-embedded wrapper pages, fetched 2026-09-23) + official wrapper source (reference/plaud-org/embedded-capacitor, embedded-react-native, embedded-flutter). Evidence class for doc statements: OFFICIAL_DOC (claim). Evidence class for wrapper source: VENDOR_SOURCE (readable, uncompiled bridge code that calls the compiled native SDK). No endpoint was called.
docs-wrappers-web.summary: All three official wrappers (Capacitor, Expo/React Native, Flutter) bridge the SAME thin slice of the native PlaudDeviceAgent facade: 9 core methods (initSDK, startScan, stopScan, connectBleDevice, disconnect, depair, isConnected, getFileList, exportAudio) and 12 events (scanResult, scanTimeout, connectState, penState, bind, fileList, exportProgress, recordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume, depair). Capacitor adds two CORS-workaround methods (readFile, putBinary) and five Android-only diagnostic events (connectFail, connectStage, handshakeWaitSure, btStatus, scanFail); RN adds an Android-only requestPermissions(). Every wrapper vendors byte-identical SDK binaries (AAR sha256 041a6f88... identical across all three and plaud-sdk-public; the three iOS xcframework binaries are identical across wrappers but differ from plaud-sdk-public/sdk/ios/*.framework). DROPPED relative to the native SDK docs (ios-sdk.md / android-sdk.md): user-token refresh (setUserAccessToken), device recovery (recoveryConnectBleDevice), deleteFile, the entire WiFi fast-transfer path (setDeviceWiFi, PlaudWiFiAgent.connectWifi/getFileList/exportAudioViaWiFi/syncFile/endWiFiTransfer; Android startWifiTransfer/exportAudioViaWiFi/deleteFiles), the entire OTA path (checkFirmwareUpdate/startFirmwareUpdate/pushFirmwareFile; Android checkFirmwareUpdate/downloadFirmware/installFirmware), app-initiated recording start/stop, playback, and all device state/settings (battery, charging, storage, status, FOTA result, WiFi-sync, motor, angles: the Capacitor Android plugin explicitly stubs 20+ BleAgentListener callbacks). The bleBind `timezone` argument is dropped from the bridged `bind` event by every wrapper. Web-app-wrapper architecture: Capacitor shell loads a REMOTE origin (https://plaud-capacitor-demo.vercel.app, cleartext:false) in WKWebView/WebView; the web layer (React page, registerPlugin proxy, transcription-runner) runs in the WebView; the Plaud SDK, BLE, file reads and S3 PUTs run natively in the hand-registered PlaudSdkPlugin (Swift SwiftPM package with 3 binaryTargets / Java class against plaud-sdk.aar); token minting and Plaud-API proxying run server-side in Next.js Node route handlers. The user token reaches the plugin as: page.tsx POSTs {user_id:"jackmu"} to /api/user-token -> server does Basic(client_id:secret) -> partner token -> Bearer partner -> user token -> JSON to WebView -> held in SWR/React state only (no storage) -> PlaudSdk.initSDK({userAccessToken, customDomain, userId}) over the Capacitor bridge -> PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK. The same token is echoed back in the body of /api/transcription/presign and /complete, which relay it as Bearer. Security posture of the demo routes: all five are unauthenticated and origin-unchecked; /api/user-token is a token-minting oracle for any user_id; /api/transcription/submit and /status/[id] spend the partner X-Client-Api-Key on any caller-supplied file_url/id; presigned URLs and full task payloads are console.logged; upstream HTTP status is leaked in 502 bodies. No secrets are committed (no .env files; .gitignore excludes .env*; the only regex hit is a Swift mangled symbol). RN and Flutter demos deliberately bake partner credentials into the client (EXPO_PUBLIC_*, --dart-define) with "DEMO ONLY" warnings. Recommended partner-backend responsibilities (docs + repo README/CLAUDE.md): exchange client credentials for partner token and mint per-user tokens; keep client_id/secret/api_key server-side; proxy presign/complete (Bearer user token) and transcription submit/poll (X-Client-* headers); optionally host audio yourself since the Transcription API accepts any public URL. Notable contradictions: docs say deviceToken=userId "binds the device to the user" whereas the Capacitor Android source states the on-wire bind token is the JWT `sub` claim (NiceBuildSdk.parseUserIdFromJWT) and the frozen ledger records the handshake token as 32 hex chars; web-app-wrapper doc instructs `cp .env.example .env` but no such file exists in embedded-capacitor; doc appId differs from repo appId; transcription response shape in how-it-works (data.segments[].speaker) differs from the Capacitor lib types (data.results[].speaker_id) and the RN/Flutter clients defensively parse both.

findings.behavior: All three wrappers expose the same 9 core methods and 12 events over PlaudDeviceAgent; the Flutter Dart header states this parity explicitly ('the same nine methods and twelve events'), and the RN Swift module lists exactly those 12 Events().
findings.notes: Capacitor adds readFile/putBinary (CORS shims) and Android-only diagnostic events; RN adds Android-only requestPermissions.
