findings.behavior: Flutter repo docs enumerate the unbridged native capabilities: app-initiated startRecord/stopRecord, downloadFile/deleteFile, WiFi fast transfer, firmware OTA, playback via JXOggPlayer/PlaudPCMPlayer -- 'left out, as in the RN demo'.
findings.notes: Vendor's own statement of scope.

findings.behavior: Capacitor Android plugin attaches a raw BleAgentListener (transport layer) and deliberately stubs the device-state/settings callbacks it does not forward: rssiChange, batteryLevelUpdate, chargingStatusChange, deviceOpRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume, deviceOpStorageRsp, deviceStatusRsp, deviceStatusDetailed, deviceLogSync*, deviceFotaResult, deviceFotaThirdVersion, deviceWifiSyncStartRsp, deviceSwitchWifiMode, motorStatus, stickAngles, deviceNewFeature, sendMoreFailDisconnect, mtuChange. This is the most complete in-source inventory of what the transport offers and the wrappers drop (battery/charging/storage/status/OTA result/WiFi mode/motor/angles).
findings.notes: Only bleConnectFail, bleConnectStage, btStatusChange, handshakeWaitSure, scanFail are forwarded (as Android-only events).

findings.behavior: Every wrapper receives bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone) from the SDK but emits only {sn, status, protVersion}; the timezone argument is dropped on all six native implementations.
findings.evidence: PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:317-319 (Capacitor iOS); PlaudSdkPlugin.java:683-689 (Capacitor Android); PlaudSdkModule.swift:294-296 (RN iOS); PlaudSdkModule.kt:342-344 (RN Android); plugins/plaud_sdk/ios/Classes/PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:286-288 (Flutter iOS); PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:551-554 (Flutter Android)
findings.notes: Cross-reference to frozen record: docs/final-closure-report.md:145-146 records that in the facade 'both protVersion and timezone are the l3 timezone byte' -- so the protVersion the wrappers forward is, per the frozen record, the timezone byte, not a protocol version. Cited, not re-derived.

findings.behavior: Capacitor shell loads a remote HTTPS origin rather than bundled assets: server.url='https://plaud-capacitor-demo.vercel.app', cleartext:false, webDir:'public' (ignored). Consequence stated in README: the app runs whatever is deployed to Vercel; native changes need Xcode/Gradle rebuild.
findings.notes: Doc's copy of the config uses appId 'ai.plaud.capacitordemo' (web-app-wrapper.md:307-319) while the repo uses 'ai.plaud.pwademo'.

findings.behavior: Split of responsibilities: WebView runs React page.tsx, the registerPlugin('PlaudSdk') proxy (lib/plaud-sdk.ts) and app/transcription-runner.ts (the only code that touches raw audio bytes). Native runs PlaudSdkPlugin (SDK init/scan/connect/list/export, file read, S3 PUT). Server (Next.js route handlers, Node runtime) mints tokens and proxies Plaud APIs. Route handlers never see audio bytes; multipart PUTs go native -> S3.
findings.notes: lib/ is reserved for server-only modules; runner lives under app/ on purpose (README.md:341-347).

findings.behavior: The plugin is app-local (SwiftPM package with three .binaryTarget xcframeworks; Java class in the app module against libs/plaud-sdk.aar), so it is not in Capacitor's packageClassList and must be registered by hand: iOS bridge?.registerPluginInstance(PlaudSdkPlugin()) in MainViewController.capacitorDidLoad(); Android registerPlugin(PlaudSdkPlugin.class) before super.onCreate().
findings.notes: Docs web-app-wrapper.md:154-220 match this.

findings.behavior: User token path: page.tsx useSWR POSTs {user_id: USER_ID='jackmu'} to `${window.location.origin}/api/user-token`; server mintUserToken() does POST /oauth/partner/access-token with Basic base64(PLAUD_CLIENT_ID:PLAUD_SECRET_KEY) then POST /open/partner/users/access-token with Bearer partner token and {user_id, expires_in:86400}; returns {access_token, expires_in}; client keeps it in SWR state only (no localStorage/sessionStorage) and passes it across the bridge in PlaudSdk.initSDK({userAccessToken, customDomain:'platform-us.plaud.ai', userId}); native calls PlaudDeviceAgent.shared.initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:). The same access_token is later sent in the JSON body of /api/transcription/presign and /complete, which forward it as Authorization: Bearer.
findings.notes: initSDK is called lazily on first Scan tap (initedRef guard), not at mount.

findings.behavior: POST /api/user-token: no authentication, no origin/CSRF check, no rate limit; accepts any non-empty user_id string and mints a Plaud user token for it using the partner secret -- a token-minting oracle for anyone who can reach the deployed origin. Logs the user id. Errors: 400 bad JSON/user_id, 502 PlaudApiError (message includes upstream status), 500 generic.
findings.notes: Demo code; README/CLAUDE.md frame the route's purpose as keeping credentials server-side, not as an auth boundary.

findings.behavior: POST /api/transcription/presign and /complete: unauthenticated proxies that take the caller-supplied access_token from the JSON body and relay it as Bearer; validate filesize>0 and filetype in {mp3,opus}; /complete validates part_list shape and optional file_md5. Both console.log the full upstream response (presigned S3 URLs and DownloadUrl are written to server logs).
findings.notes: filetype restricted to mp3|opus although exportAudio can produce pcm/wav.

findings.behavior: POST /api/transcription/submit and GET /api/transcription/status/[id]: unauthenticated; submit accepts any file_url string and optional params and spends the partner credentials (X-Client-Id / X-Client-Api-Key from PLAUD_CLIENT_ID / PLAUD_API_KEY) on it; status accepts any id. Both log full task payloads. No allow-list on file_url host, no rate limiting.
findings.notes: Anyone reaching the origin can submit arbitrary public URLs for transcription billed to the partner.

findings.behavior: readFile (base64 of an exported file; accepts raw path, file:// or a capacitor://.../_capacitor_file_/... URL) and putBinary (native PUT of base64 body to arbitrary URL returning {status, etag}; sets Content-Type only if caller passes one, Android explicitly blanks it) exist solely because the remote-origin WebView's CORS check blocks fetch() of convertFileSrc URLs and browser PUTs to S3 presigned URLs (and ETag would not be readable without bucket ExposeHeaders).
findings.notes: putBinary is an open native PUT primitive callable from any JS running in the WebView (no URL allow-list). RN README says these shims were 'not ported' because RN has no WebView/CORS constraint (modules/plaud-sdk/README.md:113-117).

findings.behavior: All three Android implementations perform work the iOS ones do not: (1) NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl('https://'+customDomain) before PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK because the SDK's Partner API Retrofit client 'hardcodes https://platform-jp.plaud.ai and does not follow customDomain'; (2) before connect, wait up to 10 s for NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() (RSA key pair fetched asynchronously by initSDK); (3) NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn) / signDeviceSnAsync so the handshake has an snSignature. deviceType is derived from SN prefix: 881 notepro, 880 notepin, 882 notepins, else note.
findings.notes: Consistent with frozen record: docs/final-closure-report.md:151-155 ('default host platform-jp.plaud.ai'; gen-key returns the RSA private key, sn-sign returns the signature) and docs/protocol-ledger.md:353-357 (credentials are cloud-issued). Cited, not re-derived. iOS wrappers call only agent.initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:) with no repoint, implying the iOS SDK honours customDomain internally (inference, not verified here).

findings.behavior: Capacitor Android source asserts the on-wire bind token is NOT the deviceToken passed to connectBleDevice; the SDK derives it from the JWT `sub` claim (NiceBuildSdk.parseUserIdFromJWT()), and an empty `sub` aborts the handshake with UUID_IS_EMPTY. Yet every wrapper (and the docs) describe deviceToken=userId as 'what binds the device to the user during the handshake'.
findings.evidence: PlaudSdkPlugin.java:414-425,821-832 vs PlaudSdkPlugin.java:126-130, PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:46-49, PlaudSdkModule.kt:103-107, plaud_sdk.dart:98-100; docs: how-plaud-embedded-works.md:109-115, react-native.md:184-188, flutter.md:165-169
findings.notes: Frozen ledger (docs/protocol-ledger.md:357) records the handshake token as 'account/partner issued, 32 hex characters' with padding/truncation -- neither 'userId' nor an arbitrary JWT sub. Both sides reported; not resolved here.

findings.behavior: Capacitor Android logs the derived bind token and the deviceToken in plaintext to logcat on every connect (Log.i with 'bindToken=' and 'deviceToken='), plus initSDK domain and userId.
findings.notes: Credential material in device logs; demo code.

findings.behavior: iOS implementations (all three) gate PlaudDeviceAgent.startScan() on BleAgent.shared.isPoweredOn, polling every 0.3 s up to 60 attempts (~18 s) then emitting scanTimeout {reason:'bluetoothNotPoweredOn'}. Capacitor Android and Flutter Android replicate the poll; RN Android checks adapter.isEnabled once and emits scanTimeout immediately.
findings.evidence: PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:78-109; PlaudSdkModule.swift:144-171; Flutter PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:130-158; PlaudSdkPlugin.java:236-266; PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:283-319; PlaudSdkModule.kt:159-184
findings.notes: Divergent RN Android semantics.

findings.behavior: Permission denial semantics differ per wrapper: Capacitor emits scanTimeout{reason:'permissionDenied'} AND rejects 'Bluetooth permissions denied'; RN rejects ERR_PLAUD_PERMISSIONS (and exposes requestPermissions()); Flutter emits scanTimeout{permissionDenied} and resolves. Permission sets also differ: Capacitor/Flutter request BLUETOOTH_SCAN+CONNECT (API31+) or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION; RN requests SCAN+CONNECT+FINE+COARSE (API31+) or BLUETOOTH+ADMIN+FINE+COARSE.
findings.notes: Capacitor also re-checks BLUETOOTH_CONNECT in connectBleDevice because the SDK swallows the SecurityException silently (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:284-309).

findings.behavior: The scanResult.supportWiFi field has three different semantics on Android: Capacitor = IBleAgent.isSupportWifi() of the currently connected agent (false until connected); RN = constant false; Flutter = (projectCode == 881, i.e. NotePro). iOS always reports BleDevice.supportWiFi from the scan record.
findings.notes: Flutter's mapping ties project code 881 to NotePro (matches deviceType('881')='notepro').

findings.behavior: Android BleFile lacks sn/channels/isOgg/duration; wrappers synthesize them: Capacitor from TntAgent statics (isOggAudio, OPUS_CHANNEL) and IBleAgent.getSerialNumber(); RN/Flutter from the last-connected BleDevice (audioChannel, isOggAudio, serialNumber; Flutter also updates connectedSn from bleBind status==0). Duration = BleFile.calculateOpusDuration(size, channels)/1000 (80 bytes per 20 ms frame per channel), over-reports for OGG.
findings.notes: sessionId is read as long on Android to avoid 32-bit truncation (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:474-484).

findings.behavior: exportAudio writes to a private dir (iOS Documents/PlaudExports, Android files/PlaudExports), formats pcm|mp3|wav|opus (default mp3), channels default 1; the call's promise stays pending until AudioExportCallback.onComplete/onError; progress via exportProgress {sessionId, progress, message}. Wrappers retain the callback bridge in a Set so it is not deallocated mid-export.
findings.notes: Flutter Android adds an AtomicBoolean 'replied' guard against double completion.

findings.behavior: All wrappers map bleConnectState(state) to {connected: state==1, failed: state in {2,-1,-2}, state}; 0 = disconnected. Failures are collapsed by the facade; only Capacitor Android recovers the reason via the transport listener (connectFail reason enum: HANDSHAKE_FAIL, SN_NOT_MATCH, TOKEN_NOT_MARCH, TIME_OUT, BLE_CONNECT_FAILED, RECORDING_NOW, USER_REFUSE, MODE_NOT_MATCH, SSN_FAILED, APP_KEY_NOT_MATCH, SYNC_TIME_FAIL, HANDSHAKE_CMD_SEND_FAIL, UUID_IS_EMPTY).
findings.notes: Frozen record cross-ref: docs/final-closure-report.md:139 and docs/protocol-ledger.md:1450 record bleConnectState(2) as the empty-token abort path. Cited only.

findings.behavior: The Android AAR is byte-identical across Capacitor, RN, Flutter and plaud-sdk-public (sha256 041a6f8814d350db...). The three iOS framework binaries are byte-identical across the three wrappers (PlaudBleSDK 55487f13..., PlaudWiFiSDK b468530d..., PlaudDeviceBasicSDK 7574af36...) but DIFFER from plaud-sdk-public/sdk/ios/*.framework (fd1f893a..., dbbcff0a..., 1d453126...).
findings.evidence: shasum run 2026-09-23 over reference/plaud-org/*/ (see Bash output); embedded-flutter/plugins/plaud_sdk/android/build.gradle.kts:76-77 asserts AAR parity
findings.notes: plaud-sdk-public ships plain .framework (not .xcframework); the difference may be packaging/build rather than API. Not investigated further (out of scope).

findings.behavior: RN and Flutter demos deliberately bake the per-user token AND partner client id / API key into the client (EXPO_PUBLIC_* inlined into the JS bundle; --dart-define-from-file compile-time constants) and call generate-presigned-urls / complete-upload (Bearer user token) and transcriptions submit/poll (X-Client-* headers) directly from the device, with explicit 'DEMO ONLY ... never ship it' warnings and a pointer to the Capacitor backend pattern.
findings.notes: No secret VALUES are committed; .env.example values are empty.

findings.behavior: No committed secrets found in any of the three repos: no .env/.env.local files exist; Capacitor .gitignore excludes .env*; the only JWT-pattern regex hit is inside a Swift ABI json mangledName string (a symbol, zero dots, not a token). Hardcoded non-secret identifiers: USER_ID 'jackmu' in all three demos, domain platform-us.plaud.ai, Vercel URL, appId ai.plaud.pwademo.
findings.evidence: grep sweep (see Bash output); nextjs-demo/.gitignore:37-38; page.tsx:16-17; react-native-demo/src/app/index.tsx:14-15; embedded-flutter/lib/src/config.dart:9-10; abi.json context shows '"mangledName": "$s19PlaudDeviceBasicSDK0A15WifiSettingPageC11blePenState...'
findings.notes: Existence-only reporting as instructed.

findings.behavior: Doc's end-to-end flow: (1) partner token via POST /developer/api/oauth/partner/access-token with Basic base64(client_id:secret_key) -> access_token/refresh_token/expires_in 3600; (2) user token via POST /developer/api/open/partner/users/access-token Bearer partner + {user_id 6-120 chars, expires_in 86400}; (3) bind = device linked to exactly one application, partner/user credentials used for encrypting/decrypting/syncing; (4) sync via BLE or WiFi fast transfer (~10x faster, needs HotSpot entitlement); (5) optional upload via generate-presigned-urls / PUT chunks / complete-upload (Bearer user token); (6) transcription POST/GET with X-Client-Api-Key + X-Client-Id, poll to SUCCESS.
findings.notes: OFFICIAL_DOC claim. The Next.js demo implements exactly this split server-side (plaud-auth.ts / plaud-transcription.ts).

findings.behavior: Starter app (plaud-template-app, native iOS) is described as including fast-transfer modal, device detail with battery/charging/firmware, manage-device screen and a firmware-update flow -- i.e. exactly the capabilities the cross-platform wrappers omit.
findings.notes: Confirms the wrappers are a subset by design.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.initSDK
api_surface.signature_or_shape: initSDK({userAccessToken: string; customDomain: string; userId?: string}): Promise<void>
api_surface.semantics: Rejects if token/domain empty ('customDomain is required (domain only, no https://)'); stores userId as default deviceToken; sets agent.delegate=self; iOS calls PlaudDeviceAgent.shared.initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:); Android first repoints NiceBuildSdk PartnerApiManager base URL to https://<domain>, then PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK(ctx, token, domain), then attaches BleAgentDiagnostics.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.startScan / stopScan
api_surface.signature_or_shape: startScan(): Promise<void>; stopScan(): Promise<void>
api_surface.semantics: Resolves immediately; real scan gated on Bluetooth powered-on (0.3 s x 60 polls) else scanTimeout{bluetoothNotPoweredOn}. Android requests BLUETOOTH_SCAN/CONNECT (API31+) or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION first; denial -> scanTimeout{permissionDenied} + reject.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.connectBleDevice
api_surface.signature_or_shape: connectBleDevice({uuid?: string; serialNumber?: string; deviceToken?: string}): Promise<void>
api_surface.semantics: Looks up retained BleDevice by uuid (iOS CoreBluetooth id / Android MAC) or serialNumber; rejects 'Unknown device' if absent; token = deviceToken ?? userId; resolves as soon as connect is issued (outcome via connectState/penState). Android: requires BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, rejects if SDK not initialised or Bluetooth off, stops scan natively (GATT 133 avoidance), runs prepareHandshake (partner-data wait + SN sign, 10 s cap) before PlaudDeviceAgent.connectBleDevice(device, token).

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.disconnect / depair / isConnected
api_surface.signature_or_shape: disconnect(): Promise<void>; depair({clear?: boolean}={clear:true}): Promise<void>; isConnected(): Promise<{connected: boolean}>
api_surface.semantics: Thin pass-throughs to PlaudDeviceAgent.disconnect(), depair(clear:), isConnected(). depair result arrives via depair event.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.getFileList
api_surface.signature_or_shape: getFileList({startSessionId?: number}={startSessionId:0}): Promise<void>
api_surface.semantics: Requests recording list; result via fileList event. Android reads startSessionId as long.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.exportAudio
api_surface.signature_or_shape: exportAudio({sessionId: number; format?: 'pcm'|'mp3'|'wav'|'opus'; channels?: number}): Promise<{sessionId: number; outputPath: string}>
api_surface.semantics: Decodes to Documents/PlaudExports (iOS) or files/PlaudExports (Android); default mp3, channels 1; promise settles on AudioExportCallback onComplete/onError; exportProgress events in between.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.readFile
api_surface.signature_or_shape: readFile({path: string}): Promise<{data: string /* base64 */}>
api_surface.semantics: Native read of exported file; accepts raw path, file:// or a *_capacitor_file_* URL; exists because remote-origin WebView cannot fetch convertFileSrc URLs (CORS). JS helper readExportedFile(path) -> ArrayBuffer.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudSdk.putBinary
api_surface.signature_or_shape: putBinary({url: string; data: string /* base64 */; contentType?: string}): Promise<{status: number; etag: string|null}>
api_surface.semantics: Native HTTP PUT (URLSession / HttpURLConnection) to any URL; Content-Type only when supplied (Android blanks it otherwise) to avoid S3 SignatureDoesNotMatch; returns ETag header. Used per multipart part by transcription-runner via putBinaryNative().

api_surface.name: Capacitor events (cross-platform)
api_surface.signature_or_shape: scanResult{devices:[{name,uuid,macAddress?(Android),serialNumber,rssi,supportWiFi}]}; scanTimeout{reason?}; connectState{connected,failed,state}; penState{state,privacy,keyState,uDisk,findMyToken?,hasSndpKey?,deviceAccessToken?}; bind{sn,status,protVersion}; fileList{files:[{sn,sessionId,size,scenes,channels,isOgg,isMusic,duration}]}; exportProgress{sessionId,progress,message}; recordStart{sessionId,start,status,scene,startTime,reason}; recordStop/recordPause{sessionId,reason,fileExist,fileSize}; recordResume{sessionId,start,status,scene,startTime}; depair{status}
api_surface.semantics: Forwarded from PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol / PlaudDeviceAgentListener via notifyListeners on the main thread. Recording events are device-initiated only (no start/stop record methods).

api_surface.name: Capacitor events (Android-only)
api_surface.signature_or_shape: connectFail{mac,reason,code,message}; connectStage{mac,stage,message}; handshakeWaitSure{mac,timeoutMs}; btStatus{mac,status}; scanFail{reason}
api_surface.semantics: Emitted from a BleAgentListener attached to TntAgent after initSDK; never fire on iOS. connectFail.reason is the SDK ConnectBleFailed enum name or 'permissionDenied'.

api_surface.name: Capacitor PlaudAudioFormat
api_surface.signature_or_shape: 'pcm' | 'mp3' | 'wav' | 'opus'
api_surface.semantics: Mapped to AudioExportFormat .pcm/.wav/.opus, default .mp3 (unknown strings fall through to mp3; Android lowercases with Locale.ROOT).

api_surface.name: Capacitor scan gate limit
api_surface.signature_or_shape: 60 attempts x 0.3 s (~18 s); HANDSHAKE_PREP_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 (Android)
api_surface.semantics: Power-on poll cap before scanTimeout; Android handshake-prerequisite deadline.

api_surface.name: Next.js POST /api/user-token
api_surface.signature_or_shape: Body {user_id: string} -> 200 {access_token, expires_in} | 400 | 502 {error} | 500 {error}
api_surface.semantics: Server-side two-step OAuth (Basic client_id:secret -> partner token -> Bearer -> user token, expires_in 86400). Unauthenticated; runtime nodejs. Env: PLAUD_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_SECRET_KEY.

api_surface.name: Next.js POST /api/transcription/presign
api_surface.signature_or_shape: Body {access_token, filesize: number>0, filetype: 'mp3'|'opus'} -> {FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize, Parts:[{PartNumber, PresignedUrl}]}
api_surface.semantics: Proxies POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls with Bearer <access_token>. Logs response.

api_surface.name: Next.js POST /api/transcription/complete
api_surface.signature_or_shape: Body {access_token, file_id, upload_id, part_list:[{PartNumber, ETag}], filetype:'mp3'|'opus', file_md5?} -> {FileId, FileType, DownloadUrl, FileMd5?}
api_surface.semantics: Proxies POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload with Bearer. DownloadUrl documented as valid 24 h.

api_surface.name: Next.js POST /api/transcription/submit
api_surface.signature_or_shape: Body {file_url: string, params?: {transcribe?:{language?, model?: 'plaud-fast-whisper'|'plaud-omni-3'|'azure-fast-transcribe', detection_level?: 'segment'|'chapter'}, vad?:{decode_silence?}, diarization?:{enabled?, return_embedding?}}} -> {transcription_id, status, data}
api_surface.semantics: Proxies POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ with X-Client-Id / X-Client-Api-Key from env (PLAUD_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_API_KEY). Unauthenticated.

api_surface.name: Next.js GET /api/transcription/status/[id]
api_surface.signature_or_shape: -> {transcription_id, status: PENDING|RECEIVED|STARTED|PROGRESS|SUCCESS|FAILURE|REVOKED, data:{text?, language?, duration?, results?:[{start,end,text,speaker_id?,language,language_probability}]}}
api_surface.semantics: Proxies GET /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/{id} with X-Client-* headers. Client polls every 5 s, max 120 attempts (~10 min), terminal SUCCESS|FAILURE|REVOKED.

api_surface.name: Next.js PlaudApiError
api_surface.signature_or_shape: class PlaudApiError extends Error { status: number }
api_surface.semantics: Thrown on non-OK upstream; routes map it to HTTP 502 with the message (which embeds the upstream status); other errors -> 500 generic.

api_surface.name: Next.js BASE_URL
api_surface.signature_or_shape: 'https://platform-us.plaud.ai/developer/api'
api_surface.semantics: Region hardcoded to US for OAuth, upload and transcription helpers; README says switch for platform-jp; EU/Singapore 'not available yet'.

api_surface.name: RN PlaudSdk (Expo module) methods
api_surface.signature_or_shape: initSDK({userAccessToken, customDomain, userId?}); requestPermissions?(): Promise<{granted}> (Android only); startScan(); stopScan(); connectBleDevice({uuid?, serialNumber?, deviceToken?}); disconnect(); depair({clear?}); isConnected(): Promise<{connected}>; getFileList({startSessionId?}); exportAudio({sessionId, format?, channels?}): Promise<{sessionId, outputPath}>
api_surface.semantics: Registered as Name('PlaudSdk') via requireNativeModule; typed as class PlaudSdkModule extends NativeModule<PlaudSdkEvents>; on unsupported platforms a Proxy stub rejects every call and isAvailable=false. No readFile/putBinary (RN has no WebView CORS constraint).

api_surface.name: RN PlaudSdkEvents
api_surface.signature_or_shape: scanResult, scanTimeout, connectState, penState, bind, fileList, exportProgress, recordStart, recordStop, recordPause, recordResume, depair (12; same payload shapes as Capacitor, minus macAddress)
api_surface.semantics: Declared in Events(...) on both native modules; delivered via sendEvent on main thread. Android supportWiFi is constant false.

api_surface.name: RN error codes
api_surface.signature_or_shape: ERR_PLAUD_ARGS (initSDK/exportAudio), ERR_PLAUD_UNKNOWN_DEVICE (connect), ERR_PLAUD_EXPORT, ERR_PLAUD_PERMISSIONS (Android startScan), ERR_PLAUD_CONNECT (Android), ERR_PLAUD (default CodedException)
api_surface.semantics: Promise.reject codes; iOS uses ERR_PLAUD_ARGS/UNKNOWN_DEVICE/EXPORT only.

web-app-wrapper.md:307-309 shows capacitor.config.ts with appId 'ai.plaud.capacitordemo' / appName 'Plaud Capacitor Demo'; the repo's nextjs-demo/capacitor.config.ts:4-5 has appId 'ai.plaud.pwademo' / 'Plaud PWA Demo'. The repo README additionally shows a generated JSON with server.url 'https://pwa-demo-plaud.vercel.app' (README.md:156-168) while the config uses 'https://plaud-capacitor-demo.vercel.app' (capacitor.config.ts:12).

web-app-wrapper.md:13-17 says the PlaudPlugin 'implements the basic methods for ... 3. Transcription'; the plugin itself (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:23-35) has no transcription method -- transcription is implemented by Next.js server routes plus app/transcription-runner.ts, with the plugin contributing only readFile/putBinary CORS shims.

Bind-token semantics: docs (how-plaud-embedded-works.md:109-115) and all wrapper comments (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:46-49; PlaudSdkPlugin.java:126-130) say the deviceToken (= app userId) is 'what binds the device to the user during the handshake'; the same Capacitor Android file (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:414-425, 821-832) says 'The handshake's bind token is not the deviceToken we pass in -- the SDK derives it from the sub claim of the initSDK JWT' (NiceBuildSdk.parseUserIdFromJWT). The frozen ledger (docs/protocol-ledger.md:357) records the handshake token as 'account/partner issued, 32 hex characters'. Three descriptions of one credential; reported, not resolved.

Transcription result shape: how-plaud-embedded-works.md:247-262 shows data.segments[] with fields start/end/text/speaker; the Capacitor server type (lib/plaud-transcription.ts:97-115) declares data.results[] with start/end/text/speaker_id/language/language_probability; RN and Flutter clients parse both `results` and `segments` and both `transcription_id` and `data.task_id`, and both `status` and `data.task_status` (react-native-demo/src/lib/plaud-transcription.ts:136,142-152,166-170; transcription.dart:140,155-181,204-207).

Transcription statuses: docs mention only PENDING and SUCCESS (how-plaud-embedded-works.md:216,236,249); Capacitor code enumerates PENDING|RECEIVED|STARTED|PROGRESS|SUCCESS|FAILURE|REVOKED (lib/plaud-transcription.ts:88-95).
flutter.md:51 clones 'Plaud-AI/embedded-flutter.git' but flutter.md:90 and :106 reference 'Plaud-AI/embedded_flutter' (underscore) -- inconsistent repo slug within one doc.

flutter.md:33 says 'guard with isPlaudSdkAvailable off-iOS' and :18 recommends 'the native Embedded iOS SDK directly' (no Android mention), yet the plugin and doc body support Android (plugins/plaud_sdk/pubspec.yaml:18-23; plaud_sdk.dart:25 returns true on Android).

react-native.md:168 says 'the packaged manifest includes the necessary permissions for Android versions <12'; the module's own AndroidManifest.xml is empty of permissions (modules/plaud-sdk/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:1-8) and relies on the AAR's manifest merge -- consistent in effect, but the permissions are not in the module's packaged manifest.

Wrapper bind event vs frozen record: wrappers forward `protVersion` from bleBind as if it were a protocol version; docs/final-closure-report.md:145-146 records the facade quirk that 'both protVersion and timezone are the l3 timezone byte' (cited from frozen record, not re-derived).
unexplained_behaviors: Why the Android SDK's Partner API Retrofit client hardcodes platform-jp and ignores customDomain (every Android wrapper must call NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl); iOS wrappers do no repoint, so whether the iOS SDK honours customDomain for gen-key/sn-sign is inferred, not verified (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:170-176; PlaudSdkModule.kt:136-141; docs/final-closure-report.md:153).

Why iOS handles partner-data readiness and SN signing internally while Android leaves both to the caller (asymmetry acknowledged in PlaudSdkPlugin.java:345-359 and PlaudSdkModule.kt:425-432 without explanation).
Whether the on-wire bind token is the deviceToken/userId, the JWT `sub` claim, or the 32-hex handshake token in the frozen ledger -- three descriptions coexist (see contradictions).

Meaning of penState fields (state, privacy, keyState, uDisk, findMyToken, hasSndpKey, deviceAccessToken) -- Flutter treats the payload as an 'informational raw map' (plaud_sdk.dart:64-65); no wrapper or wrapper-doc decodes them.
Meaning of bind.status values: Flutter Android treats status==0 as success for connectedSn (PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:552); nothing in the wrappers or the five docs defines the status enumeration.

connectState numeric codes 2 / -1 / -2 are all labelled 'connection/handshake failure' by every wrapper with no distinction (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:306); the closure report ties state 2 to the empty-token abort (docs/final-closure-report.md:139) but -1/-2 remain undescribed here.

supportWiFi on Android has three different implementations across the three official wrappers (connected-agent flag / constant false / projectCode==881); the authoritative source for WiFi capability on Android is unresolved.

Whether the Android SDK's BleFile.calculateOggDuration page-geometry parameters are documented anywhere; all Android wrappers over-report OGG durations by design (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:786-801; PlaudSdkModule.kt:458-467).

Why the three iOS framework binaries vendored by the wrappers differ from plaud-sdk-public/sdk/ios/*.framework (sha256 differ) while the Android AAR is byte-identical everywhere -- version/packaging relationship not established.
SN prefix -> device type mapping (881 notepro, 880 notepin, 882 notepins, else note) is asserted by wrapper code only; 'notepins' as a distinct device type is not explained in the five target docs.

Whether Plaud's S3 presigned URLs accept a blank Content-Type header (Capacitor Android sends Content-Type: '' when none supplied, PlaudSdkPlugin.java:593-597) -- stated as SignatureDoesNotMatch avoidance, not verified.

Device-recovery semantics ('is_bind false or null' vs true; GET /sdk/binding) are documented for the native SDK (ios-sdk.md:290-300) but no wrapper exposes recoveryConnectBleDevice; how a wrapper-based partner app recovers a locked device is unaddressed.

ai-lineage-liveagent.evidence_role: LINEAGE_FORK (with substantial PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE-grade Plaud-authored additions: a new FastAPI service, new providers, new prompts, deploy files). Role of live-agent = LINEAGE_FORK; xiaozhi-esp32 = LINEAGE_FORK; live-agent-memory = LINEAGE_FORK (mem0); xiaozhi-esp32-server = UPSTREAM_REFERENCE.
ai-lineage-liveagent.why_in_corpus: live-agent is the only corpus source that shows Plaud engineers building a server-side realtime voice-agent stack (ASR/LLM/TTS/VAD/turn-detection/memory) for an ESP32 voice companion, together with a Plaud-written 'Live Agent API' (users, agents, devices, voices, chat history, memory sharing). It reveals the product model of an experimental hardware line (branch 'feat_hardware', 'hi plaud' wake word on an ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 dev board) that is separate from the NotePin/Note recorder cloud: no Plaud production hostname, app, or recorder concept appears anywhere in it. It also refutes the dump's assumption that live-agent is livekit/agents.
ai-lineage-liveagent.summary: reference/plaud-org/live-agent (origin https://github.com/Plaud-AI/live-agent.git, HEAD 'Merge branch feat_hardware into main', 2026-01-15) is a fork of xinnan-tech/xiaozhi-esp32-server, not of livekit/agents: its README (README.md:1-24) calls it 'LiveAgent Server', a backend for ESP32 smart hardware with xiaozhi-server(8000)/manager-api(8002)/manager-web(8001), and its main/README.md is upstream's Chinese technical doc for xiaozhi-esp32-server. The upstream clone is nine months newer (2026-09-21), so the 107 'common_modified' files mix Plaud edits with upstream drift, but the 227 only-in-Plaud files are verifiably Plaud-authored: none of the sampled provider/plugin files exist anywhere in upstream. Plaud added (a) main/live-agent-api, a 79-file FastAPI+Postgres 16+S3/MinIO service under /api/live_agent/v1 with JWT auth, agents, devices, voices (Fish Audio/MiniMax clone+library), chat history with opus audio, memory (MemU) and memory-sharing tables, and unauthenticated 'internal' endpoints that xiaozhi-server calls to resolve an agent by device+wake word and load its config; (b) a turn-detection microservice (FastAPI /turn-detect, GPU image jasonyang1/turn-detection-serve:v2) and a 'TEN' turn-detection provider; (c) a core/parallel LLMCompiler-style orchestrator with feature flags (parallel tool execution, smart interruption <400ms, guardrails, tracing) wired into receiveAudioHandle; (d) new providers: BytePlus streaming ASR, Groq Whisper ASR, Cartesia/Deepgram/ElevenLabs/Fish dual+single stream/MiniMax dual-stream TTS, FSMN VAD, MemU memory provider; (e) a roles/prompt system (role.md voice-call persona template with emotion tags, English/Chinese language hints, MemU user persona) and persona-generation prompts oriented to character IP (Labubu/Pop Mart). Deep rewrites of connection.py (+1446/-1053), receiveAudioHandle, helloHandle, sendAudioHandle and asr/tts/vad bases implement agent-id/timezone/JWT headers, wake-word→agent resolution, greeting cache, chat reporting, and interruption. Default runtime (custom_config.yaml:643-655) is SileroVAD + TenTurnDetection + GroqASR + OpenRouter gemini-2.5-flash (fallback openai/gpt-5.2-chat) + MiniMax dual-stream TTS; the OTA handler was stripped of firmware serving, and manager-api/manager-web/manager-mobile were removed from the tree though still referenced. The only hosts are a config backend at http://34.221.190.98:8002/, a MinIO example at http://18.143.177.88:19000, and third-party APIs (api.memu.so, api.fish.audio, api.minimax.io, openrouter.ai, api.groq.com, BytePlus); no plaud.ai/NotePin/Tinno string exists in the repo (the manifest's libopus.js flag is a false positive: 0 matches). The sibling Plaud-AI/xiaozhi-esp32 fork targets CONFIG_BOARD_TYPE_ESP32S3_KORVO2_V3 with CONFIG_CUSTOM_WAKE_WORD='hi plaud' (MultiNet phonemes 'hi PLAA1D') and OTA at a LAN address 10.1.164.12:8002, which is the device side of this same server. Verdict: (b) an evaluation/experiment fork with real, deployed dev/staging infrastructure (EC2 'sg' and Dokploy compose files, DEBUG=True, default postgres/minio credentials) for an ESP32 voice-companion hardware line, not a production component of the Plaud recorder product and not a fork-button copy.

findings.behavior: Device lifecycle in live-agent-api: bind (creates device row or re-owns it, clearing previous agent bindings), unbind, list, add/remove agent to device, set default agent; many-to-many agent_device_bindings with is_default. Devices are identified by a free-form device_id (MAC-style or 'mobile_001').

Wake-word → agent resolution: a device connection has no agent-id header (conn_from_device); on the first listen/detect the server calls internal GET /devices/{device_id}/agent-by-wake with the wake-word text, sets agent_id and owner_id, else marks need_bind and the audio path short-circuits to check_bind_device. Unauthenticated internal endpoints also return agent config (instruction, voice, language from Fish Audio, greeting only if no messages today, last N rounds of chat).
findings.notes: config_loader.py:80 hard-codes read_config_from_live_agent_api=True, so this mode is always on.

findings.behavior: Chat history: xiaozhi-server reports every ASR and TTS turn to live-agent-api POST /chat/report with role (1 user/2 agent), content parts [{message_type text|audio|image|file, message_content text or S3 URL}] and message_time; opus packets are concatenated and base64-encoded; API stores JSONB content in chat_messages and serves cursor-paginated GET /chat/{agent_id}/messages and DELETE (also deletes S3 files). Attachment websocket messages ({type:'attachment', attachment_type image|file, url}) are converted to OpenAI input_image/input_file content.

A mobile app is a client of the same websocket protocol as the ESP32: wss://host/xiaozhi/v1/?device-id=..&authorization=Bearer JWT&agent-id=..&timezone=..; hello (opus 16 kHz mono 60 ms) → listen {mode:auto,state:detect,text:'小智小智'} or agent-id in URL → tts/start … tts/stop → binary audio; stt/tts text messages; doc ends 'contact the backend team'.

ai-lineage-memory.source_cluster: Memory / knowledge stack: live-agent-memory (mem0 fork), plaud-memU-server, plaud-memU-ui, yt-DeepResearch-Backend, plus the memU/mem0 providers inside live-agent (xiaozhi-esp32-server fork) and upstream mem0 / xiaozhi-esp32-server for delta
repos: reference/plaud-org/live-agent (memory providers + live-agent-api memory API only)
ai-lineage-memory.evidence_role: LINEAGE for live-agent-memory (fork of mem0 0.1.117, only packaging-level Plaud edits) and for the memU/mem0 providers in live-agent (Plaud-authored provider + memory API code); PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE-adjacent LINEAGE for plaud-memU-server/-ui (verbatim NevaMind memU wrappers, no Plaud edits); UNRELATED for yt-DeepResearch-Backend. None of this is CLOUD_OBSERVED: no source in the corpus shows the Plaud production app or api.plaud.ai using mem0 or memU.
ai-lineage-memory.why_in_corpus: These repos are the only evidence of what Plaud engineers have done with agent memory. They establish (a) that Plaud pinned and repackaged mem0 0.1.117 in Nov 2025, (b) that by Jan 2026 the Plaud live-agent fork ships a memU provider, selects it as the active Memory module, and wraps the hosted memU API (api.memu.so) behind its own /api/live_agent/v1/memories API, and (c) that plaud-memU-server/-ui are untouched NevaMind copies. Together they SUPPORT a mem0 -> memU migration inside the live-agent (voice companion) project, but say nothing about the recorder app's transcript search / 'ask' features.
ai-lineage-memory.summary: live-agent-memory is a fork of mem0ai/mem0 at version 0.1.117 (pyproject.toml:7) while the upstream clone is 2.1.0 (upstream pyproject.toml:7); the 964 only-in-Plaud / 1237 only-in-upstream / 350 modified files are almost entirely version drift (embedchain 629, openmemory 192, docs 68 files only in the fork; rerankers, integrations, cli, skills only upstream), and the only Plaud-specific content is packaging: pyproject.toml:8-13 ("Plaud AI Fork", harold.guo@plaud.ai, homepage Plaud-AI/live-agent-memory), README.md:85-116 (git+ install at tags v1.0.0/v1.0.0-beta.X/rc.X), LICENSE:189-192 (Plaud copyright over derived work), and the single commit "feat: remove openai dependecy contraince in another place" by Harold (harold.guo@plaud.ai) dated 2025-11-05; no file under mem0/ mentions Plaud and the graph-memory files only-in-fork are stock 0.1.x content. plaud-memU-server (9 files) and plaud-memU-ui (36 files) are verbatim NevaMind memU-server/memU-ui: README points to NevaMind repos, LICENSE is AGPL-3.0, zero Plaud strings; the server is a 43-line FastAPI wrapper (app/main.py) over memu-py==0.6.0 MemoryService exposing POST /memorize (writes conversation JSON to ./data then service.memorize(modality="conversation")) and POST /retrieve (service.retrieve([query])); memu-py 0.6.0 depends only on httpx/numpy/openai/pydantic (uv.lock:382-390), i.e. OpenAI embeddings + numpy similarity, no vector DB. The UI (package name "hippocampus-playground") reveals the memU data model: Resource -> MemoryItem(memory_type, summary, score) -> MemoryCategory(name, description, summary, score) with relations, and a retrieve response carrying original_query / rewritten_query / needs_retrieval / next_step_query (src/types/memory.ts). The decisive lineage evidence is inside reference/plaud-org/live-agent (a fork of xiaozhi-esp32-server, not livekit/agents): upstream ships mem0ai/mem_local_short/mem_report_only/nomem/powermem providers, the Plaud fork adds a memu provider (core/providers/memory/memu/memu.py), a MemU admin HTTP handler (core/api/memu_handler.py, route /api/memu/memories), pins mem0ai==1.0.0 (PyPI, NOT the Plaud fork) and memu-py==0.2.2 (pyproject.toml:62-63), selects "Memory: memu" in custom_config.yaml:657, and adds a whole live-agent-api service with /api/live_agent/v1/memories/{search,create,update,delete,sharing/get,sharing/update} proxying api.memu.so v2 (services/memory_service.py:178) with per-agent memory-sharing tables in Postgres (init_db.sql:214-232). The memU integration uses a two-category persona model ("profile" and "event"), injects a persona block into the system prompt (connection.py:728-745), and prefetches query_memory on partial ASR text with a 1.5s timeout (receiveAudioHandle.py:187,293). Therefore the dump's "mem0 -> memU migration" claim is SUPPORTED as a migration within the live-agent voice-companion stack (mem0 provider is upstream-inherited and still present; memU is Plaud-added and selected), but the two standalone memU repos add no Plaud engineering and the mem0 fork is not consumed by any Plaud code in the corpus. yt-DeepResearch-Backend is a copy of ShenSeanChen's LangGraph deep-research tutorial backend with a single "test demo" commit (Cloudreal, 2025-10-13), a committed server.log, and no Plaud strings; it has no connection to the memory stack. Nothing in the corpus links any of this to the Plaud recorder cloud (r7 inventory lists only /ai/transsumm and file/transcription endpoints); any "ask your recordings"/RAG feature remains UNKNOWN.

findings.behavior: Plaud-authored live-agent-api exposes a memory API under /api/live_agent/v1/memories: POST /search (agent_id, query?, type profile|event, cursor, limit<=100, include_shared), POST /create (type, content, title), PUT /update, DELETE /delete, POST /sharing/get, PUT /sharing/update (share_type none|specific|all, shared_with[]). JWT Bearer user_id from token. Service proxies memU v2 endpoint POST /api/v2/memory/retrieve/related-memory-items (top_k=100, min_similarity 0.3 with query / 0.1 without; generic Chinese query '记忆 用户 事件 偏好' when no query) with Authorization: Bearer MEMU_API_KEY, one call per agent_id, and falls back to an in-memory mock (use_mock=True) when memU fails.
findings.notes: LINEAGE. Memory type is 'passed through from memU category' (schemas/memory.py:65).

findings.behavior: Cross-agent memory sharing is modelled in Postgres tables memory_sharing (user_id, agent_id, share_type, unique per user-agent) and memory_sharing_targets (sharing_id FK, target_agent_id); search merges memories from agents sharing to the requested agent and flags is_shared/shared_from.
findings.notes: Memory content itself lives in memU cloud; only sharing config is local.

findings.behavior: xiaozhi-server also exposes an admin route POST /api/memu/memories (actions incl. search, get_categories via retrieve_related_clustered_categories, delete, by-session) and a stub GET /api/chat-history/has-memory/{session_id} that always returns has_memory=false with a TODO to integrate memU.

web-product.evidence_role: CLOUD_OBSERVED (four independent community clients that talked to api.plaud.ai from a browser-session token) + LINEAGE (two Plaud-org web-stack forks with no Plaud-specific content). No PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE for the web app exists in the corpus; the web app itself (web.plaud.ai bundle) is absent, so everything about its UI is INFERRED from the endpoints the clients replay and the browser-storage artefacts they read.
web-product.why_in_corpus: This cluster is the only window onto Plaud's consumer product layer above the device: the account/session model (OTP, password, Google/Apple SSO shadow accounts, cookies pld_ut/pld_urt, long-lived user token, short-lived workspace token), the region topology (global/EU/APAC/CN with -302 redirects), and the recording data model as the web app sees it (file list, detail content_list, transcription/summary job, tags, speakers, trash, upload). It also lets the WEB API be separated from the SDK/partner plumbing frozen in r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md. The two Plaud-org forks contribute only negative evidence: neither contains Plaud web-app scaffolding.
web-product.summary: The corpus contains no Plaud web-app source; the two Plaud-org candidates are an unmodified Cloudflare Workers/Hono/React template (reference/plaud-org/vite-react-template/README.md:1-3, package.json:2, src/worker/index.ts:4 returns {name:"Cloudflare"}) and an unmodified NevaMind memU-ui playground (reference/plaud-org/plaud-memU-ui/package.json:2 name "hippocampus-playground", src/App.tsx:39-43 routes "/" and "/settings" placeholder, src/pages/playground/client.ts:6,25 call /api/memorize and /api/retrieve of memU-server). Everything known about web.plaud.ai therefore comes from four community clients that replay its browser traffic. They agree on the consumer API base https://api.plaud.ai with regional hosts api-euc1 (Frankfurt), api-apse1 (Singapore), api.plaud.cn (China, web.plaud.cn/app.plaud.cn) and a JSON-envelope region redirect {status:-302,data.domains.api} (riffado servers.ts:4-34, auth.ts:49-59; applaud client.ts:4-8,152-166; plaud-api session.py:140-145; toolkit client.ts:50-54). The edge is Cloudflare-protected: non-browser User-Agents get 403 (applaud client.ts:100-104; toolkit types.ts:29-32), and the web app sends app-platform:web / edit-from:web headers and a random r= cache-buster (plaud-api session.py:45-47,87,93). The auth model evolved: a legacy long-lived user JWT in localStorage key tokenstr under origin web.plaud.ai (applaud chrome-leveldb.ts:9-14,81-84) — riffado calls the key pld_tokenstr (connect-token/route.ts:78) — was replaced by first-party cookies pld_ut (~1 day) and pld_urt (~30 days) on api.plaud.ai refreshed via POST /auth/refresh-user-token with rotating Set-Cookie (applaud session.ts:7-19,369-396; README 'How it works'), plus a workspace layer: GET /team-app/workspaces/list?need_personal_workspace=true then POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{wid} mints a ~24 h workspace token (claims ut_ref/wid/wtype) that the web app uses on /device/list and /file/simple/web (riffado workspace.ts:29-144, auth.ts:107-169; applaud session.ts:402-489). Login paths are OTP (/auth/otp-send-code, /auth/otp-login), form password (/auth/access-token, which mints a new sid and evicts other sessions, logging the phone out: toolkit auth.ts:5-8,107-129), and Google/Apple SSO that creates an identity separate from the OTP email account (riffado connect-token/route.ts:16-21). The recording feature surface implied by endpoints is: list with trash filter and sort (/file/simple/web), batch detail with inline trans_result/ai_content (/file/list), per-file content manifest with S3 presigns for transaction/outline/auto_sum_note/sum_multi_note/transaction_polish items (/file/detail/{id}), audio via presigned temp_url/temp_url_opus (Ogg/Opus bytes labelled .mp3, vendor PALUD.AI: riffado regressions/160 test:4-5), rename/trash/start-transcription/persist-results via PATCH /file/{id} (tranConfig language/diarization/llm/type 'REASONING-NOTE'), poll transcript+summary via POST /ai/transsumm/{id}, 4-step web upload (get_upload_presigned_url → S3 PUT → merge_multipart → confirm_upload with scene 101), tags (/filetag/), global speaker list with embeddings (/speaker/list) and client-side speaker rename, devices read-only (/device/list), account + membership_type (/user/me). Sharing, export, server-side search, folders beyond tags, template catalogue, Ask-AI chat (only a has_thought_partner flag), team workspace content, subscription purchase, OTA, settings, unbind and reset are NOT visible on any web endpoint in the corpus. Compared with the frozen SDK/partner surfaces, the web API is a distinct namespace (/file, /ai, /filetag, /speaker, /team-app, /user-app, /device/list) with different auth, and no operation is shared by path with the SDK's /api/... or partner /developer/api/open/partner/... families.

findings.behavior: Region mismatch is signalled in-band: HTTP 200 with JSON {status:-302, msg:'user region mismatch', data:{domains:{api:'https://api-xxx.plaud.ai'}}}; clients follow once (riffado caps at 3 redirects) to the returned domain. Envelope convention: status 0 = success, msg, optional request_id.

api.plaud.ai sits behind Cloudflare bot protection: a custom UA ('applaud/x.y.z', Node default 'node') receives 403; clients present desktop Chrome/Safari UAs, and riffado layers full browser client-hint headers (sec-ch-ua, Origin https://web.plaud.ai, Referer https://web.plaud.ai/, sec-fetch-site same-site) and optionally rotates Webshare proxies on 403/407.
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED (applaud cites its issue #26); CORROBORATED for UA gating
findings.notes: Only edge-hosting evidence for the API; nothing about where the web bundle is hosted.

findings.behavior: Web app request fingerprint replayed by plaud-api: headers 'app-platform: web', 'edit-from: web', Origin/Referer web.plaud.ai, Authorization 'bearer <jwt>' (lowercase), and a random 'r' query/body parameter added to GET/POST/PATCH (cache-buster). Recordings carry an edit_from field.
findings.notes: Whether the server requires app-platform/edit-from is UNKNOWN; other clients omit them and still work.

findings.behavior: Login flow A (OTP): POST /auth/otp-send-code {username:email} → {status:0, token:<otp token>}; POST /auth/otp-login {code, token} → access_token (top-level or data.access_token). plaud-toolkit's plan adds a user_area field to both. Flow B (password): POST /auth/access-token form-urlencoded username/password → {status, access_token, token_type}. Flow C: Google/Apple 'Continue with' accounts are a DIFFERENT identity from the OTP email account (OTP returns a token for an empty shadow account); Google users must set a password via Forgot Password to use flow B.
findings.confidence: CORROBORATED (OTP: riffado+toolkit plan; password: toolkit; SSO split: riffado + toolkit README)

findings.behavior: Every password login mints a new session (JWT 'sid' claim) and the backend evicts older sessions for the account, which logs the phone app out; toolkit therefore caches the token and re-logs in only on 401. Token lifetime: README/plan say ~300 days, but the code comment says Plaud currently issues ~30 days.

Legacy browser persistence: web.plaud.ai stored the long-lived user JWT in localStorage key 'tokenstr' (value 'bearer eyJ…'), under Chrome LevelDB origin prefix '_https://web.plaud.ai'; other keys use a per-user prefix 'PLADU_<email>_…' and 'PLADU_<uid>_bearer <jwt>_welcomeFileShown' (a per-account onboarding flag). riffado instead tells users to copy localStorage 'pld_tokenstr'. Plaud later stopped exposing tokenstr (applaud issue #31).
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED; key name DISPUTED (tokenstr vs pld_tokenstr)
findings.notes: Mechanism described only. Reading another user's browser store is out of scope and was not executed.

findings.behavior: Current first-party model (ported from the RoveNotes Connector): three tokens — UT cookie pld_ut (~1 day) used as Bearer for workspace list + mint; URT cookie pld_urt (~30 days) used to refresh the UT; WT (workspace token) used as Bearer for data endpoints. Cookies are set on host plaud.ai / *.plaud.ai. POST /auth/refresh-user-token with Cookie 'pld_ut=…; pld_urt=…' and body {} returns status 0 and Set-Cookie headers: Max-Age=0 clearers FIRST, real tokens LAST; URT is rotated near expiry so both must be persisted; sometimes only one cookie is set. UT JWT carries claims sid/ut_sid, region, iat, exp, and no email. Windows: sign in at web.plaud.ai then open api.plaud.ai/auth/refresh-user-token in the browser to refresh, copy cookies manually.
findings.confidence: CLOUD_OBSERVED (applaud, citing RoveNotes as reference implementation)

findings.behavior: Workspace layer: GET /team-app/workspaces/list?need_personal_workspace=true (Bearer UT) → data.workspaces[{workspace_id, member_id, name/workspace_name, role, status, workspace_type ('0' = personal; other = team/shared), region, api_domain, created_at, creator_user_id}]. POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{workspace_id} (Bearer UT, body {}) → data{workspace_token, expires_in, wt_expires_at, refresh_token, refresh_expires_in, refresh_expires_at, workspace_id, member_id, role}. On regional servers, recording endpoints called with a UT instead of a WT return EMPTY lists. 401 on mint = UT dead; other 4xx = stale workspace id (relist). riffado falls back to the UT if mint fails.

findings.behavior: Batch detail: POST /file/list with body = JSON array of file ids → data_file_list[] where each file additionally carries trans_result[] (segments {speaker, content, start_time, end_time}), ai_content (markdown, or a JSON string {markdown} / {content:{markdown}} / {summary}), summary_list[], and extra_data. plaud-api builds transcript, summary, per-recording speaker stats and speaker rename from this.

Per-file manifest: GET /file/detail/{id} → data{file_id, file_name, file_version, duration, is_trash, start_time, scene, serial_number, session_id, filetag_id_list, content_list[{data_id, data_type, task_status (1=ready), err_code, err_msg, data_title, data_tab_name, data_link (presigned S3, body may be gzip)}], embeddings, download_path_mapping, pre_download_content_list[{data_id, data_content (inline JSON string)}], extra_data, has_thought_partner}. Observed data_type/data_id pairs from a captured response: 'transaction' (source_transaction:<hash>:<fid>), 'outline' (source_outline:…), 'auto_sum_note' (auto_sum:…, the primary Summary tab, delivered inline), 'sum_multi_note' (sum_multi:…:<template id>, secondary template notes), 'transaction_polish'. Transcript file named trans_result.json.gz; segments carry speaker and original_speaker. Older recordings keep transcripts only here; newer ones are served by /ai/transsumm.

findings.behavior: Transcription job on web: start = PATCH /file/{id} {extra_data:{tranConfig:{language, type_type:'system', type:'REASONING-NOTE', diarization:1, llm:'auto'}}}; poll = POST /ai/transsumm/{id} {is_reload:0, summ_type:'REASONING-NOTE', summ_type_type:'system', info:JSON{language,diarization,llm}, support_mul_summ:true} → {status (plaud-api: 0 'task processing', 1 'task complete', also -111 'success'), data_result[] transcript, data_result_summ (JSON string or object), data_result_summ_mul, outline_result[{start_time,end_time,topic}], outline_task_status, task_id_info, data_source_result, data_note_result, download_link_map, file_version, auto_save, ppc_status, err_code, err_msg}; persist = PATCH /file/{id} {trans_result, ai_content, outline_result, support_mul_summ, extra_data:{task_id_info, aiContentHeader}}. applaud calls transsumm with body {} purely as a read. Long recordings take up to ~10 min.
findings.confidence: CORROBORATED for the endpoint; PARTIAL for semantics (request bodies and status codes differ between clients)

findings.behavior: Audio download: GET /file/temp-url/{id}?is_opus=0|1 → {status, temp_url, temp_url_opus?} presigned S3 URLs fetched without auth; GET /file/download/{id} (Bearer) streams directly. Cloud files are labelled .mp3 / audio/mpeg but bytes are Ogg/Opus with vendor tag PALUD.AI (frozen baseline: cloud re-tags/transcodes; not the SDK writer's TinnoTech vendor).

Web upload (scene 101): POST /file/get_upload_presigned_url {filesize, file_type:'MP3'|'OPUS'} → data{part_urls[], upload_id, object_name}; PUT part to S3 (Content-Type application/octet-stream, ETag captured); POST /file/merge_multipart {upload_id, object_name, parts:[{Etag, PartNumber}]}; POST /file/confirm_upload {upload_id, object_name, scene:101, is_tmp:0, support_mul_summ:true, file_type, filename, start_time(ms), session_id(s), serial_number:<uuid4>} → data = Recording.
findings.notes: serial_number = random uuid suggests uploads impersonate a virtual device; scene 101 meaning INFERRED (web import).

findings.behavior: Mutations via PATCH /file/{id}: {filename} rename (riffado; note edit_from will be 'web'); {is_trash:true} trash, with a POST /file/trash {file_ids:[…]} fallback that is unverified; {trans_result} speaker rename (client rewrites segment.speaker then PATCHes).

embedded-firmware-lineage.source_cluster: ESP32 firmware forks (xiaozhi-esp32, client-sdk-esp32) + AAR/iOS-header firmware-update surface
repos: reference/plaud-org/plaud-sdk-public (AAR javap, jni .so strings, iOS headers, Android template)
embedded-firmware-lineage.evidence_role: xiaozhi-esp32: LINEAGE_FORK (Plaud engineer's prototyping snapshot of upstream v2.0.3 with a 'hi plaud' wake word and LAN server defaults). client-sdk-esp32: LINEAGE_FORK (LiveKit ESP32 SDK 0.3.0 snapshot with a dynamic-token demo and audio diagnostics). plaud-sdk-public AAR/headers: OFFICIAL_BINARY / OFFICIAL_SOURCE for the real recorder's OTA path. Neither ESP32 fork is OFFICIAL_SOURCE for any shipped Plaud device.
embedded-firmware-lineage.why_in_corpus: The two ESP32 forks are the only firmware-shaped artefacts in the corpus, so they are the sole place a 'Plaud firmware' claim could be grounded; they turn out to describe a Wi-Fi voice-agent prototype on an Espressif Korvo-2 dev kit that talks to Plaud's live-agent (xiaozhi-esp32-server fork), not the BLE recorder. The AAR bytecode and iOS headers, by contrast, carry the real recorder's firmware-update model (cloud version check, phone-side download+MD5, BLE push with opcodes 50/52/51, device restart and verdict) plus two otherwise-unattested hardware lines (G101 glasses, a 'Heili three-way-switch' pen). Together they fix what CAN be said about Plaud firmware from legitimate artefacts: nothing about the recorder's own firmware image, everything about how the phone drives its update.
embedded-firmware-lineage.summary: The Plaud fork of xiaozhi-esp32 is an older upstream snapshot (PROJECT_VER 2.0.3 vs upstream 2.5.0; CMakeLists.txt:7 vs :12), so 370+ of the 376 'only-in-Plaud' paths are upstream files that upstream later moved under vendor sub-directories (main/boards/<board> vs main/boards/<vendor>/<board>); the genuine Plaud delta is confined to a 'hi plaud' MultiNet wake word (custom_wake_word.cc:91-126, custom_wake_word_multinet_only.cc:93-131, sdkconfig:713-716), a private-LAN server pair (OTA http://10.1.164.12:8002/xiaozhi/ota/ at main/Kconfig.projbuild:3-5 and sdkconfig:603; WebSocket ws://10.1.164.12:8000/xiaozhi/v1/ at main/protocols/websocket_protocol.cc:91-95), a committed sdkconfig selecting the Espressif ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 v3 dev kit (sdkconfig:633), and a backup sdkconfig named 'wrong_board' showing an earlier bread-compact/OLED build (sdkconfig.backup.wrong_board_20251010_181726 diff). There is no Plaud board definition, no Plaud pin map, no Tinno/881/NotePin string anywhere in either fork; Bluetooth is compiled out (sdkconfig:1068), the audio path is ES8311/ES7210 at 24 kHz resampled to 16 kHz Opus 60 ms frames (boards/esp32s3-korvo2-v3/config.h:7-8, audio/audio_service.cc:38-43, audio_service.h:38), OTA is upstream's esp_ota_begin/write/end + HMAC-SHA256 activation (main/ota.cc:328-357, 409-431), and the two LAN ports match Plaud's live-agent server fork (live-agent/README.md:21-22). The client-sdk-esp32 fork is LiveKit 0.3.0 vintage (idf_component.yml livekit 0.3.0 vs upstream 0.3.11) whose Plaud additions are a 'dynamic token' path that POSTs to cloud-api.livekit.io with an X-Sandbox-ID header and joins a 'demo-room' with a 'hospital_assistant' agent (voice_agent/main/example.c:115-369, sdkconfig:605-611), six audio-diagnostic modules, and a committed test Wi-Fi SSID/password (sdkconfig:620-621); it also targets an Espressif Korvo dev board (sdkconfig:602). Neither fork is the BLE recorder: the ledger's Tinno evidence stands and is corroborated here by the AAR native libs, which contain only TinnoTech symbols (tntGetFileCrc, ogg_opus_build_tinno_buf, vendor 'TinnoTech123456789012') and zero OTA-image/bootloader/partition strings. The recorder's real firmware-update path lives in the AAR and iOS headers: cloud GET .../partner/sdk/version/latest (X-Device-Signature) returns version_code/download_url/file_md5 (DeviceManager.kt:555-590), the phone downloads and MD5-checks (FirmwareUpdateManager access$calculateMD5, javap ALL.txt:91613ff), then SimpleFirmwareTransfer pushes over BLE with command 50 (push info: uid, from/to version 'T0012/V0012', thirdVersion, fileSize, CRC-16) answered by 52 (packet requests) and 51 (device verdict), followed by a device restart and reconnect (javap ALL.txt:125590-128653; PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:759-793, 1441-1442). The device's OTA status codes 0-12/255 name two hardware lines absent from every other source: 'G101 glasses' (charging-only, low-battery, OTA_MODE) and a 'Heili three-way-switch' recording pen (status 255), and a newer header adds status 13 'silent OTA' (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1395, 2241). Verdict: the ESP32 forks describe a Wi-Fi voice-agent prototype (product line unknown, wake word 'hi plaud'/'hi nicebuild') on off-the-shelf Espressif hardware; nothing about the Note Pro/NotePin S firmware image can be reconstructed from legitimate artefacts, but the phone-side OTA state machine, cloud version model, and device status bitfield can.

findings.behavior: The Plaud xiaozhi-esp32 fork is an upstream v2.0.3 snapshot; upstream in corpus is 2.5.0 with boards reorganised into vendor subdirectories, which is why the delta manifest reports 376 'only-in-Plaud' paths (all but ~25 are upstream board/asset files at their pre-reorg paths).

findings.behavior: OTA mechanism in the prototype is upstream xiaozhi's: HTTP POST to OTA_URL with headers Activation-Version (1 or 2 depending on efuse serial), Device-Id (MAC), Client-Id (board UUID), Serial-Number (efuse USER_DATA), User-Agent; response JSON {firmware:{version,url}, activation:{code,challenge,message,timeout_ms}, ...}; upgrade streams url into the next OTA slot via esp_ota_begin/esp_ota_write/esp_ota_end/esp_ota_set_boot_partition; activation answers the challenge with hmac-sha256 over efuse HMAC_KEY0. No custom image format, no esp_https_ota component.
findings.notes: Identical mechanism to upstream; Plaud only changed the URL.

findings.behavior: Phone-side firmware update state machine for the real recorder (AAR): FirmwareUpdateManager.checkForUpdate(BleDevice, cb) → downloadFirmware(info, cb) (download with progress + MD5 calc) → installFirmware(file, BleDevice, info, cb) → cancel(); UpdateStatus enum CHECKING, AVAILABLE, NOT_AVAILABLE, DOWNLOADING, DOWNLOADED, INSTALLING, INSTALLED, FAILED; FirmwareTransferPhase TRANSFERRING, TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING, DEVICE_RESTARTING, UPGRADE_COMPLETE, TRANSFER_FAILED, UPGRADE_FAILED; results carry success/error/md5Valid. Manager performs a device reconnect after the reboot (access$performDeviceReconnect) and waits for the upgrade verdict.
findings.evidence: build/evidence/javap/ALL.txt:91613-91700 (FirmwareUpdateManager methods incl. access$calculateMD5, access$downloadFileWithProgress, access$performDeviceReconnect), :88001 (FirmwareTransferPhase), :91275 (UpdateStatus), :91545 (FirmwareUpdateCallback), :89396 (UpdateProgress), :90250 (FirmwareDownloadResult.getMd5Valid), :91054 (FirmwareInstallResult); string '【阶段3-重连】开始重连设备' in FirmwareUpdateManager

findings.behavior: BLE push protocol driven by sdk.ble.util.SimpleFirmwareTransfer: computes CRC-16 of the file (proto.t0.a), sends a 'firmware push' command built by proto.i(long uid, String fromVersion, String toVersion, int thirdVersion, long fileSize, int crc).enPkg() as opcode 50 registered with expected response opcodes {50, 52}; the device then requests data ranges (52, 'received data packet request', '到达请求边界 start/end'), the phone sends packets with retry, and the device ends with 51 (verified as u16le at offset 1 via TntBleCommUtils.b, data length >= 7) carrying a status byte; phone sends sendFotaComplete(uid, status) and enters DEVICE_RESTARTING → RECONNECTING_DEVICE → WAITING_UPGRADE_RESULT. Status decode: 0 Success, 1 Upgrade failed, 2 Version mismatch, 3 Flash write failed, 4 File too large, 5 Too many attempts, 6 Device is in USB drive mode, 7 Device is recording, 8 Not enough space, 9 Device is busy, 10 G101 glasses: upgrade only while charging, 11 G101 glasses: battery too low, 12 G101 glasses: switching to OTA_MODE; also 'Wrong device mode (recorder is not in recording mode)'.
findings.evidence: build/evidence/javap/ALL.txt:125590-128653 (class span); status tableswitch and strings at process_item_data(int) (ldc 'Success'…'Wrong device mode'); opcode constants bipush 50/52 at ~:128591 with '【阶段2-推送】发送固件推送命令' and proto.i.<init>(JLjava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;IJI)V; bipush 51 / bipush 7 / TntBleCommUtils.b at ~:127165 with '【命令验证】期望命令类型'; '【阶段2-CRC】CRC-16: 0x%04X' ; 'sendFotaComplete:(II)V'; enum com.plaud.sdk.proto.s0$i (:54569) with OTA_PUSH_ERROR_G101_POWER_LOW / _NO_CHARGING / _MODE_TRANS
findings.notes: Opcode numbering (50/51/52) is read from bipush constants adjacent to the send/verify calls; the ledger's opcode table (§5) does not list them, so wire layout beyond 'type-1 frame, u16le opcode at offset 1' is not re-derived here. Matches iOS header cmd docs: pushFotaInfo → callbacks bleFotaPackReq / bleFotaResult.

findings.behavior: Official iOS header documents the same OTA contract: pushFotaInfo(uid, fromVersion 'T0012'/'V0012', toVersion, thirdVersion ('G101 project, else 0'), fileSize bytes, crc) with a typed overload adding fromVersionType/toVersionType and 'target version must exceed current'; device→phone bleSyncOtaFileInfo (cmd 151: uid, start, end, toVersion, toVersionType, isSilent, packetCheckOk); OTA result status list identical to the Android decode plus 13 = 'silent OTA transfer succeeded (firmware received, upgrade on next reboot)' and 255 = 'wrong mode (recording pen not in recording mode, specific to Heili three-way switch)'; errmsg returns the post-upgrade version on protocol version 4.
findings.notes: Version strings 'T0012'/'V0012' = versionType letter + numeric code; Android template validates '^[VT]\d+$' (DeviceManager.kt:575-577).

findings.behavior: Cloud version check (template implementation, mirrors iOS SDK): GET {platformHost}/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/version/latest?type=<notepro|notepin|notepins|note>&sn=<SN>&current_version=-1 with header X-Device-Signature (the sn-sign signature); response JSON version_code, download_url, version_type, version_number, version_description, is_force, is_strong_guidance, file_md5; hasUpdate = version_code > device code && download_url non-empty. The AAR's own checkFirmwareUpdate needs an internal sdkToken from /api/oauth/sdk-token which the developer platform does not serve (404 per the template comment), so the template bypasses it. DeviceVersionResponse model: type, model, versionType, versionCode, versionNumber, versionDescription, downloadUrl (+isForce, isStrongGuidance, fileMd5 per constructor use).

A 'common params' setter/getter exposes dataType 1 = Wi-Fi cloud-upload domain/IP and 2 = FindMy PPID.

The ledger's Wi-Fi message types 20-22 (SendOTAFileInfo/RequestOTAPackage/OTAStatusSync, ledger :1071-1072) are the phone-hosted counterpart.

findings.behavior: Both Plaud-authored ESP32 edits are debugging-heavy: the compiled wake-word file logs feed statistics every 100 frames and per-command probabilities; the LiveKit fork adds audio_stats/audio_monitor/audio_diagnostics tasks and ESP console commands (audio_diag, mic_test, speaker_test, audio_stats). Consistent with bring-up, not production.

unexplained_behaviors: Wake word 'hi nicebuild' (custom_wake_word.cc:108-109): 'NiceBuild' is the AAR's SDK brand (sdk.NiceBuildSdk), but no source explains why a firmware prototype carries it or what product it names.

'G101 glasses' product code with charging-only/low-battery/OTA_MODE rules and a dedicated 'thirdVersion' OTA field (javap SimpleFirmwareTransfer strings; PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:766,1395): no other source describes the device, its radio platform, or its firmware.
'Heili (黑黎) three-way switch' recording pen behind OTA status 255 'not in recording mode' (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1395): unnamed elsewhere; unclear whether it is a Plaud SKU or a Tinno platform sibling.

OTA status 13 'silent OTA transfer succeeded, upgrade on next reboot' exists only in the newer iOS header (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:2241) and in bleSyncOtaFileInfo's isSilent flag (:1442); the Android bytecode status switch covers 0-12 only, so how the Android SDK handles a silent-OTA device is unknown.

Device status bit6 'pan上云' (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1437) — the meaning of 'pan' (network drive? partner?) and the upload path are unexplained; bit5 Wi-Fi cloud upload and its domain/IP setter (dataType 1, :922-929) imply direct device-to-cloud upload that no client in the corpus exercises.

The xiaozhi prototype's server pair sits on private LAN IP 10.1.164.12 (ports 8000/8002); which live-agent deployment/agent it targeted, and whether 'hi plaud' devices were ever provisioned against production, is unknown.

client-sdk-esp32's dynamic-token demo names a 'hospital_assistant' agent with role metadata (voice_agent/sdkconfig:610-611); no corpus source explains the scenario or its relationship to any Plaud product.

The 'sdkconfig.backup.wrong_board_20251010_181726' file shows an earlier build against bread-compact-wifi with an SSD1306 OLED; whether custom Plaud hardware was ever targeted (rather than dev kits) cannot be determined — no Plaud board directory exists in either fork.

The xiaozhi OTA endpoint's activation flow (efuse serial + HMAC_KEY0 challenge, main/ota.cc:409-431) is upstream code; whether Plaud's live-agent fork actually issues activation challenges to 'hi plaud' devices is not visible from the device side.

Wi-Fi OTA (device status bit8, PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1438) vs the ledger's phone-hosted WebSocket OTA message types 20-22: which side downloads the image in the Wi-Fi path (device from cloud, or phone pushing) is not established by any source.

dump_claims_verdicts.claim: The Plaud device is ESP32-class
dump_claims_verdicts.evidence: For the BLE recorder (Note Pro 881 / NotePin S 882 / NotePin 880 / Note 888): ledger §1.4 and closure report identify a TinnoTech Pen BLE platform; AAR native libs contain only TinnoTech JNI symbols and no ESP/OTA-image strings (build/evidence/aar/jni/*/libtnt_ble_utils.so, libjni_ogg.so); the two ESP32 forks contain zero Tinno/881/NotePin strings and compile Bluetooth out (xiaozhi sdkconfig:1068), so they cannot be the 1910-service recorder. The forks target Espressif Korvo dev kits (xiaozhi sdkconfig:633; client-sdk voice_agent/sdkconfig:602). Whether some other Plaud line (e.g. the 'G101 glasses' seen only in OTA status strings) is ESP32-class is UNVERIFIABLE from the corpus.

dump_claims_verdicts.claim: xiaozhi-esp32 is Plaud's reference firmware
dump_claims_verdicts.evidence: It is a Plaud engineer's prototyping snapshot of upstream xiaozhi-esp32 v2.0.3 (CMakeLists.txt:7) with a 'hi plaud' MultiNet wake word (custom_wake_word.cc:91-126, sdkconfig:713-716) and LAN defaults pointing at Plaud's live-agent server fork (Kconfig.projbuild:3-5, websocket_protocol.cc:93; live-agent/README.md:21-22). That makes it reference/prototype firmware for a Wi-Fi voice-agent companion, not for any shipped recorder: no Plaud board definition, no Plaud pin map, no product-name strings, dev-kit hardware only, debug-level thresholds (0.15 'maximum sensitivity testing'). It does not describe the Note Pro/NotePin S firmware.

dump_claims_verdicts.claim: Plaud firmware OTA can be reconstructed from the repositories
dump_claims_verdicts.evidence: The phone-side OTA state machine, cloud version model and BLE push handshake (opcodes 50/52/51, CRC-16, status codes, restart/reconnect) are PROVEN_BYTECODE and PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE (javap ALL.txt:125590-128653, 91613ff; PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:759-793, 1392-1397, 1441-1442; DeviceManager.kt:555-590). The firmware image format, bootloader, partition layout and device-side installer of the Tinno recorder are absent from every legitimate artefact (native-lib strings: none).

cross_source_agreements: Model-code mapping 880 NotePin / 881 Note Pro / 882 NotePin S / 888 Note: ledger :1004-1005 (from proto.u4, javap :81176-81183) agrees with the Android template's getDeviceType SN-prefix mapping to cloud type strings notepin/notepro/notepins/note (DeviceManager.kt:791-797).

OTA status code table: Android bytecode switch 0-12 (javap SimpleFirmwareTransfer.process_item_data(int)) matches the iOS header list word-for-word including the G101 entries (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1395; PlaudDeviceBasicSDK-Swift.h:1255).

CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE for the OTA whole file: ledger :1224 / closure report :42 (tntGetFileCrc) agrees with SimpleFirmwareTransfer logging '【阶段2-CRC】CRC-16: 0x%04X' before the push and the iOS pushFotaInfo 'crc' parameter (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:770-774).

Server layout: the xiaozhi fork's LAN defaults (OTA :8002/xiaozhi/ota/, WS :8000/xiaozhi/v1/) match the live-agent fork's documented ports and paths (live-agent/README.md:21-22; docs/mcp-endpoint-enable.md:115-118) and upstream xiaozhi-esp32-server config (config.yaml:12 port 8000).

Three-call firmware API shape (check → download+MD5 → BLE push+restart): official README.md:471-473 agrees with FirmwareUpdateManager's public methods (javap :91613ff) and the template's use (DeviceManager.kt:941-1030).
Version-check endpoint: template DeviceManager.kt:555 (partner/sdk/version/latest with X-Device-Signature) agrees with r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:124.
cross_source_disagreements: Silent OTA: iOS header (newer build) documents status 13 'silent OTA transfer succeeded' and an isSilent flag (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:2241, 1442); the Android AAR's status decoder stops at 12 (javap tableswitch 0..12) — SDK generations diverge.

Version check ownership: the AAR exposes FirmwareUpdateManager.checkForUpdate (javap :91613ff) but the official Android template says it cannot work through the GA facade (needs /api/oauth/sdk-token, 404 on platform-us) and re-implements the check app-side (DeviceManager.kt:523-530) — SDK claims a capability the published platform does not serve.

Wake-word threshold: sdkconfig:716 says CONFIG_CUSTOM_WAKE_WORD_THRESHOLD=50 (0.5) and Kconfig help says default 20, but the compiled code ignores the macro and hard-codes 0.15 (custom_wake_word.cc:98) while the uncompiled multinet_only variant uses 0.5 (custom_wake_word_multinet_only.cc:98).

Delta manifest vs content: the manifest's 376 'only-in-Plaud' paths suggest large Plaud additions, but content shows ~350 of them are upstream v2.0.x files that upstream v2.5.0 relocated under vendor directories; the true Plaud delta is <10 files.

README of client-sdk-esp32 fork advertises livekit 0.3.0 and lacks the upstream 0.3.11 custom_hardware (ES8311+ES7210) example, so the fork predates the very example that would have been the natural base for custom hardware.

dump-claims-audit.evidence_role: Cross-source falsification audit. Verdicts are assigned per claim with the evidence class that carries them (PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE / PROVEN_BYTECODE / RUNTIME / CLOUD_OBSERVED / CORROBORATED / LINEAGE / UPSTREAM_REFERENCE / INFERRED / UNKNOWN). Fork lineage was settled by CONTENT diff (diff -rq -x .git against the cloned upstream), never by git history; the shallow clones' single commit messages are quoted only as content of that commit object.
dump-claims-audit.why_in_corpus: dump.md is the original research conversation whose product claims seeded the whole project; SOURCES.md is the project's own catalogue that already corrects one of them (live-agent parentage). This pass is the only place where every product-level assertion (chipset, sensors, radios, AI features, memory/observability stack, file-format quirks) is tested against the shipped SDK bytecode, the official Embedded docs, the community cloud clients and the actual fork deltas, and where marketing statements are separated from evidenced behaviour. It also surfaces product features the corpus proves but dump.md never mentioned (E2EE recordings, 21-setting device config surface, Find My/iBeacon, FOTA, marking tags, the cloud workflow/ETL schema, the live-agent-api prototype backend).
dump-claims-audit.summary: Of dump.md's ~40 factual claims about Plaud, the hardware-platform claims are the weakest: "ESP32-class" is REFUTED for the recorder by the SDK itself (the AAR is TinnoTech's penblesdk with 1,301 com/tinnotech references, the native Ogg writer tags vendor TinnoTech123456789012, and BleDevice.getManufacturer() maps the advertised BLE company ID to exactly two values, 70 = "MTK" and 89 = "Nordic", with zero esp32/Espressif strings anywhere in the binary); ESP32-S3 appears only in the xiaozhi/LiveKit voice-agent lineage forks, where Plaud's delta is a "hi plaud"/"hi nicebuild" wake word and an internal OTA URL, i.e. a voice-agent prototype, not the shipping recorder. "live-agent = livekit/agents" is REFUTED (content matches xiaozhi-esp32-server; SOURCES.md's correction stands) and the Plaud delta is substantial: a FastAPI live-agent-api with agents/templates/memories/devices/tts routes that calls the hosted MemU API, which is the only real evidence behind the "mem0 -> MemU migration" story (PARTIAL, LINEAGE). "They run Langfuse and Opik" and "GoReplay shadows prod traffic" have no Plaud-specific content beyond a Dockerfile+Jenkinsfile for gor (UNVERIFIABLE / PARTIAL). "Opus with .mp3 extension" is PARTIAL: it is a cloud-download labelling quirk (riffado #160, vendor PALUD.AI), not how the device or SDK stores files. The "repetition loop detection" and "two-pass voice-fingerprint diarization (JoshTickles)" claims are not present in any corpus repo. "VCS vibration sensor" is PARTIAL/INFERRED: the SDK exposes VPU_GAIN/VPU_CLK settings separate from MIC_GAIN plus a CallSceneSwitching handler, proving a distinct pickup unit and a call scene, but nothing names it a vibration conduction sensor. "10,000+ templates" and "press-to-highlight" are PARTIAL: template IDs, summary_type, prompt-form variables and device-side marking tags all exist, but neither the count nor a marker-to-summarizer link is evidenced. Wi-Fi bulk offload is SUPPORTED (ledger §7, Note Pro only); "BLE 5.2" and "2-4 MEMS mics with beamforming" are UNVERIFIABLE. "Plaud Embedded opens a platform" and "Note Pro records calls from a card holder" are SUPPORTED as official statements (PE-setup-skill), the latter with no technical mechanism in the corpus. SOURCES.md is largely accurate; its "~300d tokens" note is contradicted inside plaud-toolkit itself (auth.ts says ~30 days), and dump.md's "15 repos" should be 16.
