Which BLE company ID real hardware advertises (70 MediaTek vs 89 Nordic per s0$h) and whether Note, NotePin, NotePin S and Note Pro differ — the SDK never gates on it, and no capture exists (U1/U18).

What 'VPU' physically is: VPU_GAIN (Low/Medium/High) and VPU_CLK are separate from MIC_GAIN and only the Note Pro is sold as a call recorder, but no string in the corpus expands VPU or mentions vibration/bone conduction.

How device marking tags (getMarking/getRecordMarkingTags, markList:[UInt32]) reach the cloud summarizer, if at all — WorkflowTaskParams only carry fileId/language/diarization/summaryType/etlType/templateId.
The bundled ai_summarize sample reports endpoint 'azure-gpt-4o-sc' and model 'gpt-4.1' for the same task (plaud_ai_data.txt:460 vs the endpoint field) — routing between them is unexplained.

Device telemetry fields earphoneCnt, uDiskCnt, mp3PlayCnt, rereadCnt, voicePlayCnt, acceleratePlayCnt (ALL.txt:27309) imply playback/earphone/USB-disk features not present on any known Plaud recorder — likely inherited from the Tinno pen product line; which fields Plaud firmware populates is unknown.
The 'hi nicebuild' wake word in the xiaozhi fork and the NiceBuildSdk class in the AAR share a name whose meaning (codename? OEM?) is unexplained.

The SDK binary uses /api/... (Bearer api_token) while the template source uses /developer/api/open/partner/... for the same operations; whether these alias one backend is unknown (r7 inventory contradiction).
PlaudDownloadFormat.mp3 is marked '@available(*, unavailable, message: "MP3 format is not supported")' while AudioExportFormat.mp3 is the recommended export — two APIs disagree on MP3 support.
Legacy TntAgent host for /recorder/device/{checkSn,checkCustomer,saveOperation} (U21) and whether current firmware/app still hits it.
membership_type values beyond 'starter', and how the cloud enforces plan limits (minutes, templates, Ask-AI) — nothing in any client reads an entitlement.

The live-agent-api backend's config console at http://34.221.190.98:8002 and the internal OTA host 10.1.164.12:8002 appear in committed content; whether these prototypes reached production is unknown.
Storage units of getStorage free/total/duration (U2) and therefore the true on-device capacity/hours figures used in marketing.

docs-ios-sdk.summary: The iOS docs describe a thin, curated slice of a much larger binary. The documented surface is: PlaudDeviceAgent (initSDK/setUserAccessToken, startScan/stopScan, connectBleDevice x2, recoveryConnectBleDevice, disconnect, depair(clear:), getFileList(startSessionId:), exportAudio(4 formats), deleteFile, setDeviceWiFi, endWiFiTransfer, isWiFiTransferActive, checkFirmwareUpdate, startFirmwareUpdate, pushFirmwareFile), PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol (doc lists ~21 of 50 members; 1 required = blePenState), AudioExportCallback (3 required), PlaudWiFiAgent (connectWifi/listenPort/disconnect/isConnectedTo/getFileList/syncFile/stopSyncFile/deleteFile/exportAudioViaWiFi), PlaudWiFiAgentProtocol (doc lists 9 of 21), plus low-level BleAgent/WiFiAgent/PlaudPartnerApiManager in the advanced page. Protocol member counts in the docs (BleAgentProtocol 96 required + 1 optional; PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol 1 + 49; PlaudWiFiAgentProtocol all optional) are exactly confirmed by the swiftinterface. Three hard doc-vs-binary errors: (1) `bleState(powered:)` is listed twice as a PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol callback but the protocol has no such member; (2) `startSyncDeviceLogFile`/`deleteDeviceLogFile` are documented without their required `logIndex:` parameter; (3) the docs describe v1.0.14 (workflow APIs deprecated) while the shipped frameworks are 1.0.13 with PlaudWorkflowManager fully present and un-annotated. One doc rationalisation contradicts the frozen ledger: `wifiCommonErr(cmd:16,status:0)` is called a 'successful sync' but WiFi message type 16 is ExtendExitTime, not FileSync (12). Undocumented binary capabilities are extensive: facade recording control (start/stop/pause/resume), `tryReconnectLastDevice`, `skipPermissionCheck` + an SDK-side permission/resource gate with callbacks, a second legacy `initSDK(hostName:appKey:appSecret:…)` plus embedded `getTestAppKey/Secret`, a full device WiFi auto-sync (sync-when-idle) configuration API with SDK-shipped UIViewControllers, `sendApiToken`/`sendBinaryFile` and WebSocket profile push (WebsocketType url/serToken/devToken), a `PlaudFileUploader` with its own cloud `bindDevice/unbindDevice/uploadRecording`, auto log upload + encrypted log export telemetry, `PlaudDomainManager` with cn/us/jp regions and language-based auto-region, a second legacy OTA stack (quickUpdateCheck/silentUpdateCheck/showUpdateConfirmation with SDK-drawn UI), a 'glass' product delegate, public ChaCha20 key/nonce/AD vars on BleAgent, self-signed TLS trust, and a WiFi connect state machine (WiFiConnectStage/Reason incl. personalHotspot detection) that the high-level facade does not re-emit. Parity vs Android exposes app-policy vs SDK-behaviour lines: Android requires the app to call `signAndStoreDeviceSn` before connect (iOS facade does it), Android `depair(false)`+3 s timeout vs iOS `depair(clear:true)` fire-and-forget, Android `startWifiTransfer` joins the hotspot itself vs iOS app-driven `connectWifi` with entitlement + 3 s delay, Android typed WifiConnectionState/ExportStage/FirmwareTransferPhase vs iOS closures/4-phase enum, Android batch `deleteFiles` and per-file batch results vs iOS single delete and counts, Android `WifiFileInfo` (fileName/duration/timestamp) vs iOS `BleFile` — the ledger shows the wire record carries only sessionId/fileSize/scene, so Android's extra fields are client-derived. Both platforms are single-connection singletons; 'multi-device' in the docs means multiple models, and binding is one app per device tied to partner token and app installation.

findings.behavior: Docs list `bleState(powered: Bool)` as a PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol callback ('Phone Bluetooth power state') but the protocol in the binary has no such member. PlaudDeviceAgent implements BleAgentProtocol.bleState internally but cannot forward it to an app delegate because the app-facing protocol lacks the selector.
findings.evidence: IOS:225, IOS:803 (doc tables) vs BASIC:1152-1203 (full PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol, no bleState) and BASIC:1340 (facade's own BleAgentProtocol conformance has bleState)
findings.notes: App must drop to BleAgent.isPoweredOn (BLE:207) or its own CBCentralManager to observe radio state.

findings.behavior: Docs say `wifiCommonErr(cmd: 16, status: 0)` at end of transfer 'is expected behavior and indicates a successful sync'. Frozen ledger: WiFi WebSocket message type 16 = ExtendExitTime; FileSync is 12, FileSyncStop is 15. Type 0 is UniversalErr. So the callback is the status-0 (OK) UniversalErr reply to the agent's own keepalive `appExtendWifiExitTime()`, not a sync-completion signal.
findings.evidence: IOS:594-596, ADV:466-468 vs LEDGER:1069-1071 (message type table), WIFI:152 `appExtendWifiExitTime()`, ADV:437 ('keep the hotspot alive longer')
findings.notes: Both sides reported per instructions. Doc-listed command numbers 11/12/14/15 for GetFileList/FileSync/FileDelete/FileSyncStop DO match the ledger (ADV:382-385 vs LEDGER:1070).

findings.behavior: The iOS WiFiAgent conforms to `JXWebSocketServerDelegate` (serverDidStart/clientDidOpen/clientDidReceive…), i.e. the phone runs the WebSocket SERVER and the pen dials in — exactly the inverted role the ledger derived from Android bytecode.
findings.notes: Neither iOS doc page mentions that the phone is the server; `isServerStart`, `isClientOpen`, `wifiVersion`, `isHandshakeOk` (WIFI:100-111) are undocumented.

findings.behavior: BleDevice exposes computed `wholeName` and `wifiName` (BLE:576-581); doc says pass `wholeName`/`wifiPass` from bleWiFiOpen. Ledger: SSID = 'PLAUD'/'Plaud' + last 4 of serial, WPA2 pass = last 8 chars of serial, derivable from the advertisement.
findings.confidence: CONFIRMED (Android side); iOS consistent at interface level
findings.notes: Docs never state that the hotspot password is derivable from the BLE advertisement.

findings.behavior: Low-level PlaudWiFiSDK has a typed 8-stage state machine (WiFiConnectStage wifiIdle=0…wifiClosed=7) with failure reasons (WiFiConnectReason none/personalHotspot/connectSlow/timeout/failed) delivered on optional `onWiFiConnectStateChanged(_ event:)`. The high-level PlaudWiFiAgent's WiFiAgentProtocol conformance does not implement that optional, so apps on the facade never see it; docs mention none of it.
findings.evidence: WIFI:170-203, WIFI:95 vs BASIC:1699-1720 (no onWiFiConnectStateChanged), IOS:850-877
findings.notes: Android docs surface the equivalent typed `WifiConnectionState NONE→CONNECTING→CONNECTED→HANDSHAKING→READY` (AND:567). Parity gap is a facade-exposure choice, not a transport difference.

findings.behavior: iOS requires the Hotspot Configuration entitlement (NEHotspotConfiguration): WiFiAgent imports NetworkExtension, `connectWifi` is `@available(iOS 11.0,*)` with defaults overtimeSec=60, needRetry=true, hotspotCheckDelaySec=10, stallTimeoutSec=30; `WiFiAgent.isPersonalHotspotEnabled()` and reason `.personalHotspot` show the SDK detects the phone's own hotspot as a blocker. The facade's connectWifi exposes only 3 of the 6 parameters.
findings.notes: ADV:378 maps `PlaudWiFiAgent.connectWifi(_:_:_:)` to `WiFiAgent.connectWifi(_:_:_:)` — under-describes the 6-arg low-level signature. Doc example uses overtimeSec 180 (IOS:499) and a 3 s bring-up delay (IOS:496-498); neither number is in the binary.

findings.behavior: Binary exposes PlaudEncryptHeader (headerSize, magicString 'PLAUD.AI', 256-byte keyCipher, nonce, counter, encryptType, userId) and AudioFileDecryptor, matching the ledger's 512-byte header with RSA-2048-wrapped key. BleAgent additionally publishes mutable `chacha20Key/chacha20Nonce/chacha20AD`, `wifiUseAes`, `globalSendSeq/globalReceiveSeq`, `secretPackages`, and SecretUtil offers ChaChaPoly1305 and AES-256 with `decryptWithFallback(preferAes:)`.
findings.notes: Docs only mention ChaCha20-Poly1305 / AES-256 in one comment (ADV:304). That session keys are public mutable properties is undocumented.

findings.behavior: AudioExportFormat = pcm 0, mp3 1, wav 2, opus 3 with `fileExtension` — matches docs. A second enum PlaudDownloadFormat {pcm 0, mp3 1 (unavailable: 'MP3 format is not supported'), wav 2} backs the undocumented `downloadFile(sessionId:desiredOutputPath:format: = .wav)` legacy path with its own `bleDownloadFile(...)`/`bleDownloadFileStop()` callbacks. `getSupportedExportFormats()` exists but is undocumented.
findings.notes: Changelog: MP3 export added v1.0.5 (CHG:47), MP3 over iOS WiFi only from v1.0.11 (CHG:29). Ledger notes cloud downloads are Ogg/Opus served as .mp3 (CLOSURE:119-122) — distinct from SDK-local transcode via JXFileDecoder.oggToMp3 (BLE:959).

findings.behavior: Docs on both platforms treat `bleBind(status == 0)` as 'handshake complete'. The frozen Android record proves the facade passes status=0 literally on the connected transition and fills BOTH protVersion and timezone from the l3 timezone byte, so the true port version is not surfaced through bleBind. iOS behaviour is not derivable from the swiftinterface.
findings.confidence: CONFIRMED for Android (RUNTIME_PROVEN in ledger); UNKNOWN for iOS
findings.notes: Docs' 'status == 0 is the real connection success' may be tautological on Android.

findings.behavior: iOS docs: 1 = GATT up, 0 = disconnected, 2 / -1 / -2 = failed. Android docs: only 0/1/2. Ledger knows only `bleConnectState(2)` for the empty-token guard. -1/-2 exist nowhere in the binary interface or ledger.
findings.notes: Locked-device symptom also differs: iOS 'GATT connect followed by a silent drop' (IOS:292) vs Android 'bleConnectState(2) after ~10 s timeout' (AND:357).

findings.behavior: iOS facade runs sn-sign/gen-key inside `connectBleDevice` (ADV:44, ADV:519-521); Android docs require the APP to poll `NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady()` and call `signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn)` before `connectBleDevice`, else the handshake fails. iOS binary also has `isPartnerDataReady()` and RSASecretConfig SN-signature cache but docs do not require the app to use them.
findings.notes: Either an SDK-behaviour difference or Android doc lag; ADVA:139 says the Android facade calls resolveHandshakeToken internally, so only the SN signing step is app-owned on Android.

findings.behavior: iOS docs pass `deviceToken: userId` and the facade 'rejects an empty string by emitting bleConnectState(state: 2)'; a no-token overload exists. Android docs say omit it 'to connect with an empty token, which is what most integrations do' and the handshake token comes from the JWT sub.
findings.notes: What the iOS no-arg overload substitutes for the token is not stated anywhere.

findings.behavior: iOS standard unbind: `depair(clear: true)`, fire-and-forget ('does not wait on bleDepair'). Android: `depair(false)` then `disconnect()` in bleDepair with a 3 s fallback timeout; Android explicitly says the template passes false. Both say pass false during recovery.
findings.notes: Pure app-policy difference: ADV:108 says facade depair is a pass-through to BleAgent.depair(clear:) with 'no added logic' (BLE:293 default false).

findings.behavior: Identical flow on both platforms: GET /sdk/binding → dedupe bind_history (one entry per bind event, 50+ dupes normal) → recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice, historicalUserId) which pins the historical ID as handshake token and connects with isForceClear=true → bleBind(0) → depair(clear:false) → disconnect → rescan (depair changes the MAC) → connectBleDevice as current user. Only when is_bind is false/null. Accepts raw client_user_id or 32-hex.
findings.evidence: IOS:290-382, ADV:106, ADV:139 vs AND:355-447, ADVA:113, ADVA:150-151; BLE:286 (isForceClear param); LEDGER:1439-1452 (isForceClear inert below portVersion 20)
findings.notes: Android adds UX guidance for two entry points and stopping the reconnect loop (AND:449-456). iOS has undocumented `tryReconnectLastDevice()` / `recentConnectDevice` (BASIC:1211, 1244) that could be that reconnect loop.

findings.behavior: 13 stage strings in docs equal the raw values of BleAgent.ConnectStage (start, gattConnect, setNotify, setBatteryNotify, readBattery, setDataNotify, preHandshake, sendRSAPublic, firstHandshake, twoHandshake, handshakeGetSSN, changeHandshakeTimeout, syncTime); detail values ok, status_<n>, sn_signature_empty, sn_signature_invalid, user_rsa_public_key_empty, bind_token_empty. Re-emitted by the facade since 1.0.13.
findings.notes: Same on Android (ADVA:317-341).

findings.behavior: iOS: `checkFirmwareUpdate(completion:)` → PlaudFirmwareCheckResult(hasUpdate,currentVersion,latestVersion,versionCode,releaseNotes,downloadUrl,md5,isForce); `startFirmwareUpdate(progress:completion:)` one-call; `pushFirmwareFile(filePath:toVersion:…)`; phase enum PlaudFirmwarePhase downloading=0/installing=1/restarting=2/complete=3, percentage Float 0–1; result PlaudFirmwareUpdateResult(success,version,errorMessage). Binary ALSO ships a second, undocumented legacy OTA stack (quickUpdateCheck, silentUpdateCheck, checkForceUpdate, downloadUpdatePackage, showUpdateConfirmation with SDK-drawn UI, performUpdateCheck, UpdateStatus enum, UpdateError enum, LatestVersionResponse with is_strong_guidance, global PlaudQuickUpdateCheck/PlaudSilentUpdateCheck, default snType 'notepin' versionType 'V').
findings.notes: Task's 'FirmwareUpdatePhase' is `PlaudFirmwarePhase` on iOS; Android's is `FirmwareTransferPhase` with 6 cases (AND:741). Android is three-call (check/download/install) with `md5Valid` and `versionResponse` exposed (AND:663-797).

findings.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent exposes startRecord/stopRecord/pauseRecord/resumeRecord/checkIsRecording/checkIsDownloading/getCurrentSessionID and the delegate has bleRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume, blePcmData. The iOS docs list only the callbacks (and only Start/Stop/PcmData), never the control methods.
findings.notes: Android doc likewise lists only callbacks (AND:835-838) though CHG:27 claims 'recording' coverage.

findings.behavior: Facade has a complete undocumented API for the device's own scheduled upload: getWifiSyncEnable/setWifiSyncEnable, getWifiSyncList, getWifiSyncConfig/setWifiSyncConfig(operation:wifiIndex:ssid:password:), deleteWifiSyncConfig, setWifiSyncTest/getWifiSyncTestResult, with callbacks onWifiSyncEnabled/ListReceived/ConfigReceived/ConfigSet/DeleteResult/TestStarted/TestResult/WillStart(seconds:)/onWifiSyncUrl/onWifiRssiRequestConfirmed, plus SDK-shipped UIKit screens PlaudWifiSettingPage / PlaudWifiAddingPage. Underlying BleAgent methods are named SyncInIdle*. Android docs mention only the callbacks in a note.
findings.notes: Distinct from WiFi Fast Transfer; this is device→cloud without the phone.

findings.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent has `skipPermissionCheck: Bool`, `checkSdkResource()`, `reportDeviceMetadata()` and delegate callbacks onSdkFetchPermissionResult / onSdkCheckPermissionResult / onSdkCheckResourceResult(pass:tips:). ADV describes 'Permission gating — a call that fails the gate silently no-ops' but not the callbacks or the bypass flag.
findings.notes: Gate semantics (server-side entitlement per partner?) not derivable from interface.

findings.behavior: BleAgent.setWebsocketProfile/getWebsocketProfile/testWebsocket with `WebsocketType` Swift enum {url, serToken, devToken} : UInt8 (implicit raw 0,1,2) and facade `sendApiToken(token:callback:)`, `sendBinaryFile(type:data:callback:)`, `onBinaryFileReq/onBinaryFileEnd`, BleAgent sendBinFileInfo/Data/CheckSumResult. Ledger: BLE opcode 16/17 Get/SetWebsocket with types 1=url, 2=serToken, 3=devToken; 'Type 0 throws'.
findings.confidence: CONFIRMED that it exists; type-numbering relation UNKNOWN
findings.notes: Swift raw values 0/1/2 vs ledger wire 1/2/3 — either iOS adds 1 when encoding or the two platforms disagree. Not documented on any page.

findings.behavior: Both docs instruct the app to POST /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind and /unbind itself. The iOS binary has PlaudFileUploader.bindDevice(ownerId:sn:) / unbindDevice / uploadRecording / uploadLogFile / calculateSnType. Android ADVA warns NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice posts to a different service (/api/devices/bind) with a different credential.
findings.notes: Likely the same alternate path on iOS; docs are silent.

findings.behavior: Binary ships PlaudSDKLogger.logEvent (analytics per gated call per ADV:41), PlaudLogUploadManager (setAutoUploadEnabled, startAutoUpload, uploadLogsAfterRecording(sn:sessionId:)), PlaudLogConfig defaults maxFileCount 10, maxFileAge 7 days, maxFileSize 10 MB, uploadInterval 300 s, uploadTimeout 30 s, PlaudLogFileRotationManager, PlaudLogEncryption.exportEncryptedLogs, BleEventReporter hook, and BleAgent/WiFiAgent openLog/openReleaseLog. WiFiAgent.appGetLogs and BleAgent device-log sync pull logs off the pen.
findings.notes: None of the doc pages mention automatic log upload or whether it is on by default.

findings.behavior: PlaudDomainManager has Region {cn, us, jp}, setCustomDomain, setRegionForLanguage, setAutoLanguageAssociation, buildAPIURL. Docs only require `customDomain` (domain without https://).
findings.notes: Whether auto language association is enabled by default (and could redirect traffic to cn/jp) is not derivable from the interface.

findings.behavior: PlaudWorkflowManager (submitWorkflow, pollWorkflowStatus, doTranscribeAndAISummaryWorkflow(templateId:'MEETING', model:'openai'), createAIEtlWorkflow, audio merge) with result models exposing clinicalReport, doctorProjects, dealAnalysis/dealIntention, customerProjects — vertical (medical/sales) ETL products. Deprecated per docs v1.0.14.
findings.notes: Not in scope of the frozen BLE protocol; listed as undocumented capability.

findings.behavior: Second overload `initSDK(hostName:appKey:appSecret:bindToken:extra:customDomain:partnerToken:)`, `setPartnerToken` (deprecated→setUserAccessToken), `setDeviceBinding(token:)`, `clearSDKCredentials()`, and static `getTestAppKey(beta:)`/`getTestAppSecret(beta:)` — the release binary embeds test app credentials. BleAgent has `setUserIdentifier(appKey,bindToken,hkServer:)`, `checkAppKey`, `bleAppKeyState(result:)`, CustomerAuth/SSNAuth {temp, notRestricted, restricted}.
findings.notes: Documented initSDK also has an undocumented `extra: [String:String]` parameter (BASIC:1224).

findings.behavior: BleAgent is a URLSessionDelegate with `selfSignedHosts` and `selfSignedTrust(session:challenge:)` — accepts self-signed TLS for listed hosts.
findings.notes: Host list values not visible in interface.

findings.behavior: BleAgent has `glassDelegate: GlassProtocol` (glassData/glassDataClear), readGlassData(uid:), clearGlassData(), GlassData(year,month,day,time); JXFileDecoder.avcToNoiseReductionWav(sound_plus:) and setSoundPlusToken(licenseKey:); bleAngles(pitch/roll/yaw); iBeacon wakeup read/set; Find My state and resetFindmy.
findings.notes: Not mentioned on any doc page except Find My token in blePenState params.

findings.behavior: No simultaneous multi-connection: PlaudDeviceAgent.shared, BleAgent.shared with single `bleDevice`, `isOnlyOne`, `recentConnectDevice`; WiFiAgent.shared single `bleDevice`. Scan filters accept multiple names (`setFilter(_ names:[String])`) and `startLoopScan()`. 'Multi-device support' in starter-app-specs means multiple models (NotePin and Note Pro). Binding: one application per device, tied to Partner Token AND app installation; unbind before uninstall.
findings.evidence: BASIC:1205, 1211; BLE:199-201, 216-218, 279-280, 284; WIFI:98, 120-123; build/docs-plaud-ai/plaud-embedded_starter-app-specs.md:35; STA:186-192; IOS:227-229, IOS:237
findings.notes: Android starter doc has the identical warning (plaud-embedded_android-starter-app.md:139-141).

findings.behavior: iOS doc: iOS 14.0+, Xcode 16.0+, arm64 only, Swift 6.0.3. Binary: PlaudBleSDK and PlaudWiFiSDK target arm64-apple-ios14.0, PlaudDeviceBasicSDK targets arm64-apple-ios13, compiler Swift 6.0.3. Flutter page says deployment target 15.1 'the Plaud frameworks require it, don't go lower'.
findings.evidence: IOS:19, IOS:47, STA:48-51 vs BLE:3, WIFI:3, BASIC:2-3; FLT:101, FLT:141
findings.notes: Doc-vs-doc contradiction (14.0 vs 15.1); binary supports the lower claim.

findings.behavior: iOS WiFi getFileList returns [BleFile] (sn, sessionId, size, offset, timezone, zoneMin, scenes, penCollect, channels, nsAgc, isOgg, duration()). Android returns WifiFileInfo with fileName, fileSize, duration ms, timestamp, scene — doc claims 'more per-file metadata than BleFile exposes'. Ledger: WiFi GetFileList wire record is 10 bytes [u32 sessionId][u32 fileSize][u16 scene]; BLE record differs (scene + attribute).
findings.notes: Android's fileName/duration/timestamp must be client-derived (sessionId is a timestamp; duration from size via BleFile.calculateDuration-like math).

findings.behavior: iOS low-level syncFile/stopSyncFile/deleteFile take `scene` (default 1) that must equal BleFile.scenes or the device rejects with non-zero wifiSyncFile status. Android exportAudioViaWiFi takes sessionId only; scene is not exposed.
findings.notes: SDK-exposure difference; Android presumably fills scene from its file list internally.

findings.behavior: iOS: downloadAllFiles/startDownloadAll/stopDownloadAll with wifiDownloadAllProgress(totalFiles,currentFileIndex,currentFile,totalProgress) and wifiDownloadAllCompleted(completed,failed); deleteFile is single-session. Android: downloadAllFiles with onBatchDownloadStarted/Progress/Completed(success,failed,results: List<BatchDownloadResult>) and batch `deleteFiles(List<Long>)` 'the only batch delete in the SDK'.
findings.notes: iOS doc omits downloadAllFiles from the method list though the callbacks are listed; CHG:39 v1.0.6 announced batch download.

findings.behavior: iOS AudioExportCallback: onProgress(_:message:), onComplete(outputPath: String), onError(_:) — all required, @objc so conformer must be NSObject, and the app must retain it. Android: onComplete(outputFile: File) plus optional onStageChanged(stage: ExportStage DOWNLOADING→TRANSCODING). iOS has no stage signal; speed is on `currentDownloadSpeedKBps` / `getFormattedDownloadSpeed()` (undocumented).
findings.notes: CHG:37 claims live speed reporting on both.

findings.behavior: BleAgent.syncFile(sessionId:start:end:decode:) with `decode:false` for V20+ E2EE devices then AudioFileDecryptor; facade syncFile(sessionId:start:end:) decrypts; bytes on bleData(sessionId:start:data:), end bleDataComplete(); bleSyncFileHead(sessionId,status), bleSyncFileTail(sessionId, crc) (Android names it status). Ledger: DATA payload concatenation equals stored file byte-for-byte; stopSync opcode 29→30; deleteFile 30→31; transfer-tail CRC never computed by SDK.
findings.notes: iOS `bleSyncFileTail(crc:)` naming matches the ledger's unexplained TAIL CRC (U13).

findings.behavior: PlaudBleSDK ships JXFileDecoder (avcToOgg, oggToOpus, oggToMp3 quality=4, avcToMp3, pcmToMp3, avcToPcm, oggToPcm, avcToWav, avcToNoiseReductionWav gain 6), JXAvcDecoder (packSize consts), JXPcmProcess/JXWave2PcmProcess, JXFileSoundWave, JXRecordVolumer/JXRecordingVolumer, JXWaveHelper (16 000 Hz), JXCrcHelper, PD* duplicates with onVolumePerTwentyMsec, OggOpusParser, PlaudPCMPlayer, PlaudAudioPlayerViewController(sessionId:), SwiftySound `Sound`. Ledger codec geometry: 16 kHz, 20 ms/320-sample frames, 80 B/frame/channel.
findings.notes: 20 ms granularity in PDRecordingVolumer matches the ledger frame size.

findings.behavior: PermissionManager (runtime BLE/location permissions), NiceBuildSdk (signAndStoreDeviceSn, isPartnerDataReady, resolveHandshakeToken, getSecurePrivateKey, clearPartnerData), IWifiTransferAgent (getConnectionState, checkPrerequisites, stopWifiTransfer), SimpleFirmwareUpdateCallback, bleDeviceName/bleMicGain/blePowerChange listed in the main table.
findings.notes: iOS binary has counterparts for most (isPartnerDataReady BASIC:1230, RSASecretConfig BASIC:1721, bleDeviceName/bleMicGain/blePowerChange BASIC:1155,1161,1163) but the iOS docs omit them.

doc_vs_code_contradictions: IOS:225 and IOS:803 list `bleState(powered: Bool)` as a PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol callback; BASIC:1152-1203 shows the protocol has no `bleState` member (the facade only consumes BleAgentProtocol.bleState at BASIC:1340 and cannot forward it). Doc side: 'Phone Bluetooth power state' is available on the facade delegate. Binary side: it is not.
ADV:228-229 give `startSyncDeviceLogFile(logType: Int)` and `deleteDeviceLogFile(logType: Int)`; BLE:342 and BLE:344 require `(logType:logIndex:)`. The documented calls do not compile.

ADV:63-65 and CHG:7-11 (v1.0.14, 2026-09-14) say PlaudWorkflowManager is deprecated; the shipped frameworks are 1.0.13 (Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString) and BASIC:815-860 expose PlaudWorkflowManager, PlaudWorkflowManagerTest and PlaudWorkflowManagerExample with no deprecation attribute. Doc describes a newer release than the public binary.

IOS:594-596 and ADV:466-468 state `wifiCommonErr(cmd: 16, status: 0)` 'indicates a successful sync'. LEDGER:1069-1071 (frozen, bytecode-proven on Android) assigns WiFi message type 16 = ExtendExitTime and 12 = FileSync, 15 = FileSyncStop; type 0 = UniversalErr. The observed callback is the OK reply to the agent's keepalive `appExtendWifiExitTime()` (WIFI:152), not a sync-completion indicator. Both sides reported; the doc statement is a rationalisation of an observed symptom.

ADV:378 maps `PlaudWiFiAgent.connectWifi(_:_:_:)` to `WiFiAgent.connectWifi(_:_:_:)`; the low-level method is 6-arg `connectWifi(_ ssid:_ passphrase:_ overtimeSec:=60,_ needRetry:=true,_ hotspotCheckDelaySec:=10,_ stallTimeoutSec:=30)` (WIFI:128). Facade exposes only 3 (BASIC:1681). Doc under-describes rather than misstates.

IOS:19 / STA:49 say iOS 14.0+ and the binaries target ios14.0 (BLE:3, WIFI:3) / ios13 (BASIC:3); FLT:101 and FLT:141 say deployment target 15.1 'the Plaud frameworks require it, don't go lower'. Doc-vs-doc contradiction; binary supports 14.0 (13 for DeviceBasicSDK).

IOS:102-106 document `initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:)`; the binary signature has a third `extra: [String:String] = [:]` parameter (BASIC:1224) and a second, entirely undocumented overload `initSDK(hostName:appKey:appSecret:bindToken:extra:customDomain:partnerToken:)` (BASIC:1225).

ADV:445 says 'most of WiFiAgentProtocol are required'; WIFI:74-96 has 19 required + 2 optional (`wifiConnected()`, `onWiFiConnectStateChanged(_ event: WiFiConnectEvent)`), and the doc table (ADV:447-464) omits both optionals and the WiFiConnectEvent/WiFiConnectStage/WiFiConnectReason types.

IOS:867-877 lists 9 PlaudWiFiAgentProtocol callbacks and says 'All members are @objc optional'; BASIC:1630-1652 has 21 optional members; `wifiConnectResult(_ success:_ errorCode:_ message:)` (BASIC:1634) appears on no doc page.

IOS:794-814 presents ~21 PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol callbacks as 'the most commonly used'; BASIC:1152-1203 has 50. Omitted entirely: bleAppKeyState, bleDeviceName, bleMicGain, blePowerChange, bleRecordPause, bleRecordResume, bleSyncFileHead, bleSyncFileTail, bleDecodeFail, bleSyncFileStop, bleDownloadFile, bleDownloadFileStop, all onWifiSync*, onWifiSyncUrl, onWifiRssiRequestConfirmed, onSdkFetch/Check* permission and resource results, onCommonMsgChannel, bleFotaPackReq, bleFotaPackFin, bleOtaDataSendFail, bleSetActive, bleCommonSetting, bleRate.

IOS:175, IOS:182-183, AND:237, AND:244-245 treat `bleBind(status == 0)` as the handshake-complete signal. LEDGER:1471-1477 (RUNTIME_PROVEN, Android facade) shows status is passed as literal 0 on the connected transition and both protVersion and timezone are loaded from the l3 timezone byte, so protVersion never carries the real port version. iOS behaviour unknown from the interface; both sides reported.

BLE:714-717 `enum WebsocketType: UInt8 { case url, serToken, devToken }` has implicit raw values 0/1/2. LEDGER:1093-1096 (Android bytecode) shows wire types 1=url, 2=serToken, 3=devToken and 'Type 0 throws'. Either the iOS SDK offsets by one on encode or the platforms disagree; undocumented on both.

unexplained_behaviors: bleConnectState values -1 and -2 are documented only on iOS (IOS:160, IOS:220, IOS:368); they appear in no swiftinterface constant and the ledger knows only state 2. Meaning of -1 vs -2 unknown.
What the no-token overload `connectBleDevice(bleDevice:)` (BASIC:1241, IOS:170) substitutes as the handshake token, given ADV:131 says an empty deviceToken is rejected with bleConnectState(2).

The purpose and gate criteria of the SDK permission/resource check (`onSdkFetchPermissionResult`, `onSdkCheckPermissionResult`, `onSdkCheckResourceResult`, `checkSdkResource()`, `skipPermissionCheck`) — ADV:42 says failed gates silently no-op; which calls are gated and against what (server entitlement?) is undocumented.
Whether `PlaudLogUploadManager` auto-upload and `PlaudDomainManager` auto-language-association are enabled by default (BASIC:359-361, 315-316); defaults not visible in the interface.
`WebsocketType` Swift raw values 0/1/2 vs ledger wire types 1/2/3 (BLE:714-717 vs LEDGER:1093-1096) — encode offset or platform mismatch.
iOS `bleSyncFileTail(sessionId:crc:)` (BASIC:1171) vs Android `bleSyncFileTail(sessionId, status)` (AND:841): same event, different second field. Ledger U13 says the SDK never computes the tail CRC.
`sceneFlag` (BASIC:1212), `isOnlyOne` (BLE:216), `settingScene` (BLE:235), `flutterMapData` (BLE:261), `bleBlock: Int2Void` (BLE:205) — semantics unknown.

The '~2 minute firmware WiFi timeout' (IOS:538), the '3 s hotspot bring-up' (IOS:496-498), the 180 s overtimeSec in the example (IOS:499) and the '5 hour' recording cap (IOS:391, AND:465) have no counterpart in the binary interface or the frozen ledger; source is presumably firmware/app policy.

Android `IWifiTransferAgent.deleteFiles(List<Long>)` batch delete (AND:623-631) vs iOS single `deleteFile(_ sessionId,_ scene)` — whether WiFi type 14 FileDelete accepts multiple sessions on the wire or Android loops client-side is not in the ledger excerpt.

Android `WifiFileInfo.fileName/duration/timestamp` (AND:931) vs ledger 10-byte GetFileList record [sessionId][fileSize][u16 scene] (LEDGER:1078-1081): the extra fields must be client-derived; derivation not documented.
`BleAgent.selfSignedHosts` (BLE:206, BLE:467-470) — which hosts get self-signed TLS trust is not visible.
`getTestAppKey/getTestAppSecret(beta:)` (BASIC:1231-1232) — what backend accepts these embedded test credentials.
Glass product line (`GlassProtocol`, `readGlassData`, `GlassData` year/month/day/time; BLE:48-56, 172-175, 348-349) — device family unknown.
Values of `BleAgent.protocolVersionNewBatteryService` and `protocolVersionV20Features` (BLE:197-198) are not emitted in the interface; docs say V20+ = 'NotePro and newer' (ADV:162).
Whether the iOS facade shares the Android bleBind quirk (status literal 0, protVersion==timezone; LEDGER:1471-1477) — not derivable without the iOS binary.
Why PlaudDeviceBasicSDK targets ios13 while its dependencies target ios14.0 (BASIC:3 vs BLE:3/WIFI:3) and the Flutter page demands 15.1 (FLT:101).
